Because of the wide viewing angle I'm able to create different zones for the front door, driveway and "everything". I can then adjust alerts based on what's captured in those views.

The doorbell also features a two-way radio function to speak to whoever is at the door if you're unavailable. You can also listen in to the live feed if you want to see what's going on around your house. Apparently, the audio quality is good enough to incite a flinch and an eyeroll from my wife when she was out watering flowers on the front porch. Do with this what you want.

One downside for me is that it doesn't natively integrate with Google Assistant or Apple HomeKit. I thought I'd be clever and use IFTTT to trigger automations, but it appears that isn't going to be simple. No big deal as I get alerts on my phone and I'll experiment more as I get time.

Overall, I'm super pleased with the quality of the product and will be looking at other Ring security products for future needs.
reviews.title: Excellent Video Doorbell
reviews.author: DaveG

reviews.body:
I’ve owned a number of Ring products over the years, and this is my second battery operated doorbell. The device itself is thicker, taller, and heavier than the one I got a couple years ago, though not as wide. The unit’s permanently installed battery charges via a USB-C cable (not included) via a port on the back, and it can last up to 120 days between charges, depending on usage and weather conditions.

As it can be installed completely wire-free, you can place it anywhere including sheds, fence posts, and doors that don’t have existing doorbell wiring, provided it receives good WiFi signal. Just keep in mind you’ll need to take the doorbell down when the battery is depleted to charge it. It also has two wire terminal screws at the back so that you could hard wire it to your existing doorbell system to work with an in-home chime, and the doorbell transformer would keep the battery topped up in lieu of periodic charging, which I opted to do.

To set it up, you’ll use the Ring mobile app and create or log into an account. Setup takes only a few minutes and linking your Ring and Amazon accounts gives you access to features like voice control and doorbell press alerts on your Alexa-enabled speakers. The doorbell releases from its wall mount when you insert the removal tool into the slot on the underside, although a flathead screwdriver would work just as well, so it isn’t meant to be a security measure against theft. In that event, you can report the unit stolen in the Ring app which would prevent it from being setup by another user.

The doorbell comes with a 30-day free trial of a Ring Pro plan. This provides you with cloud storage of video and snapshot history for 180 days, emergency services response, smart alerts to categorize and reduce notifications based on what is being recorded, AI text descriptions and search, and more. Users that don’t have a subscription will only be able to bring up an on-demand live view from the doorbell to communicate and respond to events as they happen in real-time, and video footage will not be recorded or saved.

The video quality is non-HDR retinal 2K at 1920 x 1920 pixels with 140° horizontal and vertical fields of view providing head-to-toe coverage. The wide field of view means that there aren’t any blind spots, so you can see if there are packages set on the ground below the doorbell as well as areas off to the sides. There is also 6x digital zoom during live view and playback. When viewing the camera’s feed in the app, images and video appear as a square and fisheye distortion is minimal. You can also customize the motion detection zones to exclude areas where motion may trigger nuisance alerts as well as limit the time of day and frequency of notifications.

The quality of the video varies, and sometimes it’s really clear and other times it’s very blurry, even at different points in time within the same video clip or live view session. Performance will depend largely on the strength, speed, and consistency of your WiFi signal. We have gig speed internet and a WiFi 7 mesh network with the closest access point on the other side of the wall just inside the door; the unit typically receives RSSI 35 – 40 signal strength. I also saw some variation in the framerates of the recorded videos with the blurriest ones having around 14 fps and numerous frozen or dropped frames, while the clearest ones had closer to 24 fps with smooth consistent video throughout.

The speakers for the unit are located on the sides near the top of the device, which can play automatic greetings or warn folks that they are being recorded. There’s also a microphone, so you can engage in 2-way talk via the app with someone at the doorbell. The audio quality is generally decent and clear, though if your connection is weak, digital compression artifacts or delays may occur. The mic picks up voices and captures a bit of ambient noise as well. However, in some video recordings the audio would occasionally drop out, sometimes at the beginning, end, or randomly in the middle of the recording.

When pressing the doorbell button, you’ll receive a push notification from the app and can also have any number of your Alexa speakers sound a “chime” and make an announcement. This version of the doorbell camera has black and white infrared night vision and is limited to 2.4 GHz WiFi connections. Nighttime images are detailed, clear, and bright, though can wash out objects close to the camera lens.

Overall, the Ring Battery Doorbell (2026) is a very good, basic video camera doorbell. It has clear HD audio and video quality, as long as your WiFi signal is fast, strong, and consistent, but you’ll need a paid subscription if you want to be able to view recorded video history, alert SOS emergency responders automatically, or enable more advanced alerts. It’s quick and easy to upgrade your doorbell if you have pre-existing wiring, or add it as a new doorbell camera just about anywhere you can mount it. The hardwire charging option further simplifies things, as you'd never have to take it down to charge the battery. With Amazon integration, all your Alexa-enabled speakers can be used as chimes throughout your home, and with push notifications and 2-way communication, you’ll never miss a package or visitor at your door.
reviews.title: Clear audio & video, strong/fast WiFi required
reviews.author: ReviewedByPhil

reviews.body:
Ring, widely considered the undisputed leader in smart residential cameras, just released a battery doorbell that produces extremely sharp video with no wires required to connect it. This battery doorbell captures wide-angle video in stunning retinal 2K; the camera resolution is 1920 x 1920 with a 1:1 aspect ratio. You can see floor to ceiling & can zoom in on the video with your cellphone up to 6x. Even when you are away from home, you can chat two-way with the visitor at your door.

Ring Battery Doorbell 2K has a built-in rechargeable battery. To recharge it, use the included removal tool to detach the doorbell from the wall. Next, plug in a USB-C cable to charge the doorbell battery. The internal battery lasts up to 180 days before it is ready to be recharged.

The doorbell measures 5.78"H x 1.41" W x 2.11"D. It is solidly built & has a quality feel. The speckled grey color blends with virtually any door. Optional Ring Protect Plans are reasonably priced. I already subscribe to a Ring monitoring plan, so there was no additional cost to add an extra camera.

CONCLUSION:

The new Ring Battery Doorbell is very easy to set up; no wiring is required & like other Ring cameras, operation is very intuitive. When a friend dropped by the house last week, Ring asked me to name him, so I did. When he came by again today, this new doorbell that I just installed called out his name & said he was at the rear door! I love how it recognizes & shares visitor identification with all of my other Ring cameras! It earns my highest recommendation.
reviews.title: Battery Doorbell w/ Retinal 2K
reviews.author: gadgetguy11

reviews.body:
So I have used several video doorbells from Ring and other manufacturers. With this updated model from Ring I expected a slightly better experience than my previous Ring doorbell, but I have been left a little disappointed.

The setup process is easy and straightforward. Download or open the Ring app, scan the QR code, connect to Wi-Fi, sign-in or create your account, and you're in business. Now, just install the doorbell and adjust the settings.

The Ring app has a pretty nice layout. Your devices are displayed in a list format with a preview window as soon as you open the app. There are a decent number of settings which make personalizing your device easy. You can customize notification types and styles, detection types and zones, which alerts you want to receive, link devices, check the health and battery level, adjust power settings, and much more.

I appreciate that events can be viewed in both a timeline view and chronological view.

The two-way audio works well in both directions. Voices are fairly clear and the speaker is loud enough for visitors to hear.

Unfortunately the biggest downfall with this doorbell is the video quality. I have placed the doorbell in a few different locations and adjusted the settings repeatedly, all with lackluster results. Image and video quality are grainy and unclear, especially in lower lighting conditions such as overcast skies and evening. The zoom yields virtually unusable results. With video quality being the most important factor in a doorbell of this type, I'm left pretty underwhelmed overall.

I really did not think this is something I would be saying, but I find it hard to recommend this particular version of Ring's doorbell.
reviews.title: Not Ring's Best Doorbell
reviews.author: FlightMedic

reviews.body:
I’m not a stranger to Ring doorbells and each generation tended to be more of the same without any real noteworthy improvements. I’m happy to note that this newest model with the Retinal 2K is worth talking about. The video quality is leaps and bounds above previous doorbell versions, with remarkably clear and sharp images regardless of whether it’s day or night. It’s easier to tell exactly what the images are using the 6x Zoom feature, and the 140-degree wide-angle lens covers my entire front and driveway. And the two-way talk feature delivers clear audio sound when communicating even when I’m away from home.

Being battery operated, set up was quick and the Ring app has clear step-by-step instructions. Charge the doorbell, install the mounting bracket, attach the unit, connect to wi-fi and finish set-up in the app and you’re ready to go. If preferred, the unit can be hardwired if you want to avoid having to remove the unit when it’s time to charge the battery. The one great con for me here is that the entire unit will have to be detached for charging, which increases the amount of time it’s down and unavailable for use. I’d still rather have a removable battery that I can swap out with a spare. Be sure to keep up with that little orange removal tool and you will need a USB-C charging cable because it does not come with one.

A couple things to take note of. You will need a Ring cloud subscription to retain any history of video recording events. And be mindful that there can be an occasional lag in recording events versus getting alert notifications about them.

Overall, the new slimmer design of this latest Ring doorbell model makes it more appealing. And the updated camera and video quality, both live and recorded, makes it a worthwhile purchase and gives a great sense of security and coverage.
reviews.title: Greatly improved and amazing video quality!
reviews.author: MzRose

reviews.body:
TLDR: wide-angle 2K video, up to 6x Zoom, Two-Way Talk, Built-In Battery newest camera from Amazon brand Ring. Uses the same rechargeable battery as other Ring models; improved Ai features also.

This is the newest model of the Ring doorbell camera and it now has 2K resolution, AI and a wider view from its lens camera system.
The battery is easily removed to charge it up and it promises 60 days of use on a charge. It uses the same battery style as other Ring cameras so it is easy to just swap out a charged battery from another if the house has more than one. A supplied small plastic tool allows opening and removing the rechargeable battery. It is strictly battery operated.

The lens allows 6x Enhanced Zoom to capture faces and close up details
The night vision allows color video in semi darkness and crisp black and white in total darkness

Speak to people seen on camera with a built in speaker and microphone on the camera outside while the user is literally anywhere with an internet connection on the phone Ring app. Of course the app and the camera needs a WiFi internet connection to operate properly.

With the Ring app, a user can get Person, Package and Vehicle Alerts as seen and sensed by the camera. It also has motion sensor detection with fast notifications on the Ring app. The motion detection works similarly to the last version, but the descriptive AI is an added bonus. The built in AI sees the image, and then describes what it sees. It uses basics like person, pet, car, eventually an image of the scene is displayed.

In use on the front door which faces our street, the camera supplies very clear and sharp color images in the day and very sharp and defined color night vision video at night. Sound is also clear and very understandable when tested with adults as well as children for our testing.

From the Amazon website: “Combine this device with Alexa for hands-free home monitoring. When anyone triggers Ring’s built-in motion zones, your Echo device will illuminate and make an announcement, so you’ll always know when someone’s there.
And if you have an Echo Show, you can also see, hear and speak to anyone captured on camera.”
This function indeed works with our Echo Show 8” devices.

It is functional within these temperature ranges: -4°F to 122°F (-20°C to 50°C). It is also weather proof to Weather Resistant IP55

This model is a positive upgrade from Ring
reviews.title: Retinal 2K is a Positive Upgrade from Rind
reviews.author: AtrixNY

reviews.body:
So I just received my new Ring Battery Doorbell about a week ago and have been testing it out and comparing it to my older Rind camera. We had another Ring camera at our front door and had been wanting to install another camera at our back door, so this Ring doorbell camera came along at the perfect time. Over the years we have tested and tried several top-leading brand names for video doorbell cameras and the like, but Ring had us sold. After using the other Ring camera for several months and absolutely loving it, we were excited to try out this Ring Battery Doorbell.

Unboxing Includes:

* Ring Battery Doorbell
* Installation Toolkit
* Window Decal Sticker
* User Documentation

To get started, simply download the Ring app from the App Store for iOS or Google Play Store for Android devices. Next if you don’t already have a Ring account, you will need to create an account and follow along with the instructions. Even though this is a battery-powered doorbell, you can actually hardwire it to your doorbell line. For our purpose we will be installing this at the backdoor. If you’re doing a hardwire install of this doorbell camera, be careful and make sure you know which line at the breaker box the doorbell is connected to. Turn that switch off at the breaker box and follow along with Ring’s in-app installation process which is super simple.

Once I got everything installed and turned the power back on, I waited for the camera to properly boot up and get connected to the home network. This doorbell camera has some amazing features, such as Motion Detection, Retinal Vision 2K with wide-angle video and up to 6x Enhanced Zoom, and 2-way audio; which is amazing. You can clearly hear those on the other side of your door no matter whether you're away from home or not. That lets would-be intruders know that you’re watching them. As far as video, the quality of the 2k as well as the wide-angled field of view tops our other more expensive Ring doorbell camera. The older (and more expensive) Ring doorbell camera is nice, but doesn’t have the wide-angle view like this newer model. We’re very happy and pleased with this choice and you will be too.
reviews.title: Ring Battery Doorbell w/2K Wide Angle & 6x Zoom
reviews.author: Mistabritt

reviews.body: Says it's not compatible with 5g. Most cities and some rural towns have already switched to 5g. I know Verizon has in our area . Make sure you don't have 5g before purchasing.
reviews.title: 5g vs 2.4 g
reviews.author: Ruralforever26

reviews.body:
So a little over a week ago I ended up choosing to go with the Ring Battery doorbell after an issue I had with my old Nest doorbell. I mistakenly lost the removal key decided to take it as an opportunity to try something new. Right off the bat, I appreciated that this model is completely battery operated. I didn't feel like messing with wiring, so being able to mount, charge it, And get it online in a matter of minutes was a plus for me. The setup process through the Ring app was pretty simple. It walks you through everything step by step, from connecting the Wi-fi to adjusting motion zones and notification settings. The app itself feels polished and easy to navigate and I like being able to pull up a live view or check on the activity from in front of my house from anywhere.

What really stood out though was the image quality. The Retinal Vision 2K camera is sharp. I was Impressed by how much detail it captured especially because I initially sought out a 4K camera. Your faces are easy to make out, packages are clearly visible, and the wider field of view lets me see more of my front porch than I expected. Motion alerts have been quick and reliable so far and the two way talk feature has been cleared during conversations with FedEx and UPS.

The only thing I wasn't a huge fan of was that some features required a ring subscription and I'm still trying to figure out how to connect to my Google Home (ioT). That said my first impression has been a positive one. Some ways it's actually an upgrade. I'll just be sure not lose the key this time.

4.25/5
reviews.title: Great choice for a replacement.
reviews.author: Drew B

reviews.body:
Initial Thoughts
I will say that Ring has made good stuff for a long time. While their products may be predictable, they have also been reliable. I see this repeating that sentiment.

My expectations
I expect the Ring battery doorbell to be easy to install, easy to add to my current sub, and easy to use.

What’s in the box?
Out of the box you get the doorbell camera, a back plate mount, a tool for removing the camera from the mount, wall anchor/screws, and inserts along with the QR code that you need to set it up.

Try it out
First off, I will say this… I was embarrassed that it took me longer than I thought to find the USB-C charging port on the back of the camera. I figured, I’ve installed enough of these, I know how to do it without relying on the QR code… and I was wrong. Little did I know it was a rubber nub that I had to remove to expose the port.
Other than that little hiccup, it was easy setting it up.

The installation was easy as well, I ended up adding the doorbell to my back door. I couldn’t use the provided screws considering the type of wood I was installing it on, but other than that, no issues.
The 2K really does provide a nice clear crisp video. The audio is great.
Despite the fact that the camera offers a nice wide view, I wish that the hardware/software still gave you the option of panning.

Thoughts
I want to use this as a battery powered one since I don’t want to go through the hassle of adding wires to an area that doesn’t have existing housing. The only “annoying” part is taking off the doorbell completely to recharge it.

The likes
I like how easy the whole set up is. The new doorbell looks sleeker and the build quality feels significantly better.

The dislikes
I do not like the engineering behind the recharging.

What’s one thing I would change?
I wish that Ring created a type of wireless charging plate where the doorbell could be mounted to. This would still eliminate the need of wires, but wouldn’t have to remove to recharge.
reviews.title: The king of doorbells
reviews.author: EthanH

reviews.body:
The Ring Battery Doorbell (2nd Gen) is larger and heavier than earlier Ring doorbells. It is approximately 6” long and about 10oz in weight compared earlier models. When installing, make sure it is anchored correctly, as it is heavier than earlier models.

The Box includes - Battery doorbell (2nd Gen), Back plate, back plate removal tool, (to remove the doorbell for charging), Screws with anchors, Ring Sticker, and Pamphlet with barcode to scan for completed setup. The entire Doorbell needs to be removed for charging unless it is hardwired (which it is compatible with). The hardwiring hardware is NOT included, neither is the USB-C charging cable. The Ring Batter Doorbell (2nd Gen) does NOT have a removable battery. The battery is built in. Therefore, it needs to be removed to be charged with the USB-C cable.

The Doorbell (2nd Gen) comes 30% charged and should be charged completely before installation. It took me 10-12 hours to fully charge. I charged it overnight. This doorbell is replacing my older front door Ring Doorbell. This new Video Doorbell gives me better viewing angles, clearer videos, and full person viewing.

Specs briefly:
- Retinal 2k with up to 6x enhanced zoom
- Head to Toe video
- Live view and 2-way talk
- Crisp true-to-life video with more clarity for low light conditions
- Can be connected to Ring Chime or Chime Pro, Or Standard Router
- It can be hardwired for constant charging and for use with standard indoor chimes.
- 140° horizontal, 140° vertical viewing angles, with 173° Diagonal viewing
- 2.4Ghz WiFi only (not dual band)
- Can be charged with doorbell solar panel (sold separately) for continuous charging if not hardwired.

Observations:
- It takes a long time to charge if low charge below 50%. I charged it when I got it (at 30%) and it took 12 hours just to reach 99%. I’m not sure if it would have eventually reached 100% as I gave up at 99% because I wanted to install it.
- Back plate is plastic and on the flimsy side. Not sure how many times the doorbell can be removed before it breaks or the removal tool (also plastic) breaks. Therefore, I hardwired mine, so I did not have to worry about that.
- Needs to be hard wired or charged by solar panel to constantly trickle charge.
- 6x zoom is ok, not as sharp as the standard 1x-4x zoom where the video is still nice and clear. After 4x zoom the video starts getting pixelated to view clearly.
- There are 2 ways to save videos, download on your device, purchase a Ring Plan on the website, and download them to your device from there.
- There are 4 Ring Plans to choose from:
o Basic plan (Ring Solo) – One camera only
o Ring Multiplan – all cameras at the same location.
o Ring Pro – includes familiar faces, 24/7 active monitoring, and more.
o Virtual Security Guard – includes everything in the above plans plus Live 24/7 video monitoring, intruder deterrent in Real-Time, Proactive verified dispatch, and more.
- Each plan is higher in cost either per month or per year. I just have the Ring Multi plan which is perfect for me. You can check the Ring Website for a detailed description of each plan.
- My suggestion is to at least get the Ring Solo plan for just one camera as you can save and download videos from the website. If you decide to get more cameras, then I suggest the Ring Multi plan minimum. This way, no matter how many cameras you have, you can save all the videos for each camera in the website cloud instead of just the one camera.
- I have 4 cameras at this time, and I will be getting more, so the Multi Plan works perfectly for me.

The Ring App
- The Ring App is available on several devices, including iOS, Android, iPad tablets, and Amazon Fire tablets.
- You can check your plan on the app but can only make change to your plan on the Ring Website.
- The app also has a dashboard where you can see all your cameras at the same time and just click on the one you want to check the videos on.
- The App has many functions that you can use, modes, mute cameras, check battery charge, etc. Exploring the App is easy as it has a menu (3 bars) at the top left of the dashboard that lets you choose which device you want to see, general settings, updates, new products.
- There is also a tab called Neighbors. This tab allows you to set a specific area that you want any type of notifications on. The site is free to subscribe to.

Negatives:
- Be advised that when you set up the Ring Battery Doorbell (2nd Gen), the setting page will display “hardwired” even if you have only on Battery. It seems to be the default, and you can’t physically change it. It will, however, let you know when the battery is running low.
- Since the battery is permanently installed, it can’t be swapped out to charge the older Ring Doorbells. The entire doorbell must be removed to charge it up.
- It can be hardwired to your existing chime system where the doorbell with keep trickle charging constantly. If you can hardwire it, I suggest you do so. It’ll make your life easier. You may have to purchase a hardwire kit from the Ring website. That depends on your doorbell system.
- When you charge the Ring Battery Doorbell, there is a small plug in the back of the main bell, that has the charging port. There is a plug in the port to keep covered and protected from the elements. The problem is that plug is not attached to the doorbell so you should make sure you put it in a safe place, so it doesn’t get lost.

I recommend this doorbell with reservations due to the negative aspects listed above. It’s OK if this is your first Video Doorbell and it can be hardwired or attached to a solar panel, but personally, I prefer the older models where the battery is removable and can be swapped out with a full battery while the used one is charging. This way, you don’t lose any video of events at your door.
reviews.title: NICE, COULD USE SOME IMPROVEMENT
reviews.author: dstracker

reviews.body:
Specs
The battery-powered version of the newest Ring doorbell has 2k video resolution with a viewing area of 140 degrees. It is compatible with the Ring app, can record audio as well as video, and works by motion detection. It connects wirelessly to your existing internet connection and offers two-way audio through the app. There is an optional subscription service but it is not required, nor is it included.

Pros
The resolution and viewing angles keep rising with each model! The night vision is solid as well. This battery-powered version comes with a USB-C rechargeable lithium-ion battery, which is easier for me than getting a wired model. This model works with both Android and iOS systems and is compatible with Ring and Amazon Alexa.

Cons
This is simply because I live in a place where it regularly gets below -5 degrees F, but that is the minimum operating temperature for the unit. The maximum temperature is 122 degrees F, which might become a problem with direct sunlight. It also takes 5-10 hours to charge the battery fully, but I have seen recommendations for small solar panels to keep from charging this model. I think I would like to look into that to have that 24/7 security at my door.

Conclusion
Although it takes some time to charge, I feel safer having the surveillance at my door; I have lived in too many crummy apartments where my packages have been stolen. I would recommend this model to anyone who does not have the ability to hard wire a model into their existing electrical system, as that seems to be the only drawback – the battery life and time to charge fully.
reviews.title: It just keeps getting better
reviews.author: vollmer2010

reviews.body: As it stands, I have to give this a 5 out of 5, simply the grounds of seeing a recording of a delivery person, making a drop-off at my front door and the description said, "bloop, bloop, delivery driver tripped at the front door." I'm not being mean, but boy, oh, boy. That was hilarious. It told me what I was seeing. I love that. The box houses a simple reward of [The Ring Doorbell, unmounting key, mounting bracket, & a couple of mounting screws]. That's all you need. But if you have a smart speaker IE* Alexa speaker, plus your smartphone, you've got everything that you need to have a functional home notification system. Also, if you already have a Ring camera or cameras, this will integrate perfectly into your plan. It doesn't cost anything extra to add this. Installation took no time at all. Just 2 screws (ankers are optional, in most cases) and you're off and running. [ KEEP YOUR MOUNTING KEY SOMEPLACE SAFE & MEMORABLE]. You will need it to recharge your camera at least twice a mount. It could be more, depending on traffic and the settings that you've chosen. The older model has a charging port that is hidden behind a wall that needed to be unscrewed, but this model, has a type C port, right in back after you've unmounted the doorbell. The sound is clear and the latency is great. I could ramble on and on about this thing. I love when I get a product that I find to be 5-star rated. I hope this makes you as happy as it made me. Getcha one.
reviews.title: I liked It So I Put A RING On It
reviews.author: hitsuyoo

reviews.body: This Ring doorbell was easy to self-install. It's quick and simple. Everything needed for installation was in the box. I downloaded the Ring App on my cellphone. This Ring doorbell & app makes it easy for me to see packages being delivered, and any visitors who arrive...from head to toe, there's good vertical coverage of my porch area. I also like the "live view", 2-way talk, and "real-time' alerts which are very reliable. I can definitely see when someone is on my front porch/front doorway for any reason, whether visiting or delivering a package/mail. The video and images provided are crisp and detailed. I'm also able see my front porch area at night, with zero lights on, if the camera detects anything. And I actually love that it's battery operated because our front doorbell electrical hookup doesn't work properly and a battery doorbell is all we can get to successfully work by our front door. And the push-pin mounting system makes removing the doorbell for charging the battery...tool-free and fast. Love that! The doorbell is easily recharged with a USB-C charging cable. Installation of this new Ring doorbell camera has been a game-changer for our family. We love being notified when someone steps onto our front porch. An extra layer of security is certainly nice to have.
reviews.title: Great quality, rechargeable-battery, video recording doorbell from Ring
reviews.author: DeeM

reviews.body:
I switched to new Ring doorbell from an older Kangaroo and the difference is like day and night. The video (live feed as well as recordings) at 1080P is sharp and crisp. Even the night videos are very good. The setup was super easy. I downloaded the ring mobile app and it walked me through the setup step by step. All steps were easy to follow and worked. I mounted the doorbool on my storm door in the battery mode with the help of screws that came with the door bell. I think it took me around 15 mins to set it up. The doorbell snaps on to the mount effortlessly. There is an included tool to remove the bell from the mount. Make sure you keep it safe as without it you won't be able to unmount the bell when it needs charging.

In terms of the features, it has lots of them. For example, you can customize the alert zone, and all different settings via the mobile app. I have integrated it with my Alexa and the integration was also pretty straightforward.
The battery is supposed to last 4-6 months after a single charge. This I am yet to test.

I haven't bought any additional devices (like Chime) yet as I am using my phone to get the alerts when it rings.

There is a 50$ annual subscription plan that gives you additional features like upto 180 days of video backup etc.

Overall it is a perfect video home doorbell and the price seems to be right.
reviews.title: Perfect video home doorbell
reviews.author: Shail

reviews.body:
Ring is pretty much the gold standard of doorbells at this point and this version builds on all the old great features. First it’s super easy to setup using the ring app on your phone just scanning the QR code, the doorbell itself talks to you the entire time giving a play by play of what it’s doing to setup.

Even though this is the battery doorbell you can also apparently hard wire it, though I use it as battery this is pretty cool to have the option. Since I use it as battery mode you basically just have to charge it every so often (usb C I used my phone charger) and the rating is over 3 months of use between charges. You can always check battery status in the app. When you need to charge you use a special tool to pop it off a mounting plate which it securely locks to.

The whole retinal tuning and abilities in this camera are basically what sets it apart from the old model with the whole 6x digital zoom you can actually see details in stuff now which is super nice for those 3am sketchy package deliveries or creepers you normally could barely make out their face you can now see fully. Not that you couldnt before but it reminds me that I really enjoy the ai description of a recorded video to read what went on before actually seeing it.

This does come with a trial and without the sub you can still access live view, real time notifications and arm/disarm features you essentially lose the optional stuff and recordings without but its so good your going to want to always be subbed anyway.
reviews.title: Gold Standard Doorbell Camera
reviews.author: Manny

reviews.body:
This is not our first Ring Doorbell. We like them very much.
It was very quick and easy to go from box to mounted and being used.
Perhaps most of that was from having been there done that with previous Ring Doorbells and other wireless devices in the home..
But its pretty much, charge the device, put it on your WiFi network, mount it outside the doorway you wish to monitor and be alerted from, go through a few easy setup routines guided by the app you previously installed on your smartphone and you are in buisness.
We are currently running this one in the battery only mode as my wires for the inside 1950's Westminster CHime Doorbells, broke off in the wall so for now, I am just being alerted by my iPhone. I will restring the wires later on in the year as right now I am on multiple restrictions following back surgery for a ruptured disk.
You can enable several additional features if you sign up for a plan, but some of those are already included with a free 30 day trial from Ring.
The quality of the images and videos are really great, and these days I wouldnt even think of opening my door without the ability to first see who....or what is on the other side!!!!
I would have given this 5 stars but for such a nice device, instructions were not enclosed in my box, but the app is somewhat helpfull after you eventually find out what app to download.
reviews.title: Nice Device, Easy Setup
reviews.author: PapawJeff

reviews.body:
The ring Battery Doorbell Retina 2K is a great go to doorbell for those who do not have a wired doorbell or do not know how to wire a new one.
I love mine and the new A.I. features with the Addition of the yearly subscription is a great option.
It recognized people, animals, vehicles, package deliveries etc.
It’s nice to get notified and not have to check the camera when the Ring tells you exactly what it is.
The neatest thing I’ve experienced with my ring during the test was a Quail on the wall staring at the camera…(see pic) the video is crazy, he hung out for 5 minutes while his mate watched nearby.
The subscription opens up so many options, it’s crazy. The A.I. alone describing the alert is worth the price alone. I opted for yearly pass for multiple cameras.
The day and night viewing quality is top notch. The 2K is more than sufficient. I have a different brand security camera that’s 4k that isn’t even as good as the ring. The available 6x zoom really brings things in focus. You are able to set zones up so you can drill down to an area you are most interested in and with a focused area this will cut down on false alarms.
The quick response is all you need if you like the unit to speak on your behalf to visitors. You can also have a 2 way chat with visitors.
The settings are too numerous to mention, but rest assure if it’s an option you want. It will be in there.
I highly recommend the Ring to friends and Family.
reviews.title: Ring hits another Home run
reviews.author: Fordman9870

reviews.body:
Having had two previous gens of the Ring Doorbell, I'm familiar enough with the product and as such wasn't expecting to be as blown away this newest model as I was.

Picture quality is beautiful, day and night. Zoom is crystal clear across my entire driveway and front yard. Improvements in notifications/on-screen recognition is amazing. Getting a heads up that something as specific as "Delivery driver with two boxes approaching" or "landscaper is mowing your yard" is a welcome addition as it saves me from even happening to open the app. Long gone are the days of "motion detected".

Slightly narrower and higher quality finish than previous models, the mounting bracket now requires a special key (orange so it's easy to see, but small so it's easy to lose) to remove for charging. As soon as I saw this I thought, "great...something else for me to keep track of." But that aside, nothing much to gripe about.

The app interface is simple and straight forward, if you have other cameras with Ring switching between them is as easy as clicking the drop down and selecting it. You get a 30-day free Premium trial, which mainly gives you access to your archive of clips and is well worth it, imo.
reviews.title: Noticeable improvement over previous Gens
reviews.author: BillnMish

reviews.body:
Great doorbell!

I have a combiniation/hybrid system between the Ring ecosystem and the Nest system. They both are great systems in their own regard, but one place where this beats the other, is in the mount for removal and recharging of the bell cam. The nest uses a plate that can be pretty finicky, but this one, is a cinch.

The mounting was simple. Two screws, and then snap it right on. Great!

Already having the Ring ecosystem, adding the doorbell was also simple. Simply go to your devices, hit the blue "+" button, choose your product, name it, and you are good to go.

The camera quality itself is great. Between the two systems, the Ring has slightly better digital zoom. As for motion detection, they are both very good. I do always move the motion detection to the lower end of the range on my battery products. End of the day, I really only care about mammals and package delivery. No need for it to go off when a bee flys by.

The battery life has also been in line with the other system. I chose to mount this one on the garage door, where it wouldn't be constantly triggerd by passing cars and the battery has so far barely budged.

End of the day, great product, whether you already have the Ring system or would like to use this as your base to build around.
reviews.title: Great Doorbell Camera
reviews.author: Posted1

reviews.body:
Ring Doorbell cameras have been the standard door security and awareness solution for a number of years now. With the growth of DIY wifi home security offerings, you have more choices today than ever. Thankfully, Ring continues to upgrade their products - and add additional features and solutions. This newest model provides the standard, basic features expected from Ring with a few improvements.

Set up was easy. We already have a Ring Camera account so it was simple and straightforward adding it to our account. The camera is clear - similar to earlier versions - but it seems to have a slightly improved wide-angel view. A key feature with this newest model is the fact that it’s battery operated and easy to recharge using USB-C. Power was at 89% after 5 days.

Audio for listening in general - and for conversations with people at our doorstep is generally the same, though it does seem to be improved for the person talking at the door.

Another nice adjustment is the fact that this model is narrower than our previous model, which makes it suitable for thinner doorframes.

All-in-all, you can’t go wrong with a Ring Doorbell Camera.
reviews.title: You Can't Go Wrong with a Ring Doorbell Camera
reviews.author: JBCTECH

reviews.body: It allows me to peak in @ my resident while at work .,the wide angle & clear video is definitely a plus!
reviews.title: Money well spent!
reviews.author: connese1

reviews.body: I love this ring door bell ! It was so easy to set up, probably one of the easiest things I’ve ever had to set up in my life. It was super easy to access using the app on my phone. I love that you can check the camera in real time. I also like you can change the motion detection settings so you’re not being alerted of cars driving by. It also saves the battery a bunch by not doing that. My favorite part about this product is the picture quality and the fact that it’s charge able so I don’t have to waste money on batteries! You just take it right off the mount with a key and plug it into a universal charger! I can’t believe I haven’t gotten one until now because it’s very needed. Thanks ring
reviews.title: Amazing video quality!
reviews.author: CourtneyL

reviews.body: I’m very impressed with this Ring Battery Doorbell. The Retina 2K video is incredibly sharp, and the wide-angle view captures everything at my front door. The 6x zoom makes it easy to see important details, and the two-way talk is loud and clear. Installation was quick, the battery lasts a long time, and the motion alerts are fast and reliable. The matte mocha finish also looks modern and blends in nicely with my home. If you’re looking for a high-quality wireless video doorbell with excellent features, I highly recommend this one.
reviews.title: Excellent Video Quality & Easy Installation
reviews.author: DOnotBuyPhones

reviews.body: I received a Ring Battery Doorbell (2nd Gen) in exchange for my honest opinion. I love this doorbell. It’s easy to install and the battery is simple to charge. The app is easy to follow and download. A voice recording lets people know they are being recorded. Is it quick with two-way talk so you can speak to visitors and they can speak to you. You can use live view mode or check reported motion. Smart detection notifies you when an individual or package is within the alert Zone that you set. images are sharp and colorful during the day, and the camera uses incurred at night to capture images
reviews.title: Day or night
reviews.author: PattyD

reviews.body: I’ve been really happy with this Ring Doorbell (2nd Generation)! It has been very reliable and gives me peace of mind knowing I can see who is at my door even when I’m not home. The video quality is clear and the motion alerts come through quickly on my phone. The battery life has been great too! I don’t have to charge it often which is great compared to the 1st generation. It was simple to set up and the app is easy to understand. I love being able to talk to someone at the door through the doorbell especially when I’m away from home. This feels like a good quality device that works exactly like it’s supposed to.
reviews.title: Easy to use and works great!
reviews.author: LaTashaW

reviews.body:
I have their Wired Doorbell Plus (2nd Gen) Retinal 2K at my front door and got this one to add to my back deck. I also have a wireless chime that I have in my man cave area so that I can hear the doorbell when I'm not on the main floor. I also have a floodlight that I have yet to install, but that will also go in my backyard on the deck. The Ring product lineup continues to evolve and improve from their earlier offerings. They definitely make some quality products with a lot of features.

This doorbell couldn't have been easier to setup. Since I already had existing products on my network, I was able to get up and running in minutes. I was surprised that I didn't have to connect to my network first to set it up. It connected to my wireless chime, and I guess it ported the info over automatically or just uses the chime for its wireless connection.

I completely charged the doorbell and mounted it by my back door. It's recommended that it be mounted four feet from the ground, which will allow me to see packages left on the ground and the full silhouette of anyone in the back. Since it faces my neighbor's house, I like that I can set up zones to prevent a lot of notifications and drain the battery. The images are extremely clear and provide great detail in such a slim package.

The plans can end up adding a few dollars to the setup. Well, maybe more than a few. The Solo plan that I was using is $50 per year. That seems a bit high for one device. If you have multiple devices, the cost doubles to $100 annually, but you can add as many devices as you want at one location. That seems to be the better deal if you are heavy into Ring devices. The Ring Pro service was provided for a 30-day trial period and while I like the service, it adds an additional $200 per year on top of the $100 for Ring Multi. That's pretty steep in my opinion, so when the trial runs out, I will let it lapse.

The only thing I would have preferred is that the battery was removable and I could have a backup charging while one was in use. This way I wouldn't have to be without coverage for the back door while it recharges. I looked it up and it is said that it will take between 5-10 hours to recharge, so that is a good amount of time to not have it in use. It is pretty simple to remove with the included tool. I also wish that the chime could have different ring tones for each doorbell. I didn't see a way to do that in the app, so there may be a way to set that up. I also have the older generation chime, so maybe the newer model has that option.

Overall, I am really impressed with the doorbell as I have been with all of Ring's products. This is a great addition to my smart home setup.
reviews.title: Ring continues to impress me with their lineup
reviews.author: TechFan

reviews.body: I’ve been really happy with this doorbell so far. One of my favorite features is that it can recognize different types of motion, whether it’s a person, an animal, or someone approaching with a package. The alerts feel much more useful because I’m not getting notified for every little movement. I also love the wide view. I can see my entire front yard, which gives me a much better idea of what’s happening around the house. The video quality is clear, the app is easy to use, and it’s nice being able to check on deliveries or see who’s outside even when I’m not home.

reviews.body: Eufy knocked it out of the park again. I have several of their indoor pan/tilt cameras already (and love them) so I definitely needed to order this new one when it came out.The build quality is great, and the appearance of the camera is top notch. It is a much more modern/futuristic appearance, and less of a "security dome camera" appearance.The picture quality is fantastic, and is a huge upgrade from their older indoor cameras. You can zoom in and still maintain great picture quality.I love that I can have it set to record 24/7 and automatically track motion. I currently have it setup based on geofencing from my wife's phone (she stays at home). So I only get notifications when she is away from home, but it still records 24/7.I will say that you need to either mounting base-down or base-up. I tried mounting it horizontally on the wall and it was difficult to impossible to steer the camera in this orientation, it also could not look "up" far enough. If you can make it work, installing it upside-down on the ceiling definitely provides the best view.I think the price tag is still a bit steep. I will likely wait until the price drops below $100 before buying another one.But I honestly can't recommend this camera enough, it is really great, especially if you already have other eufy cameras.
reviews.title: Best indoor camera on the market

reviews.body: First of all, I like the exterior design of this indoor camera. It looks like a cute kid's robot.Setup was a breeze and quickly added to my existing Eufy app and the firmware update took a few minutes to apply. For me, I also set it up to connect to my router directly and that worked fine. If you have the eufy home base 3, you can have it connected to that instead. I would also note that it supports some more modern wifi features such as wifi 6 and wpa3.Since I set it up in a stand alone mode without the home base, a micro SD card (not included) is recommended to store video playback and event recordings. I used the SD card from my previous generation eufy indoor cam.There are 2 cameras on this device. One 4k wide angle lens and one 2k telephoto that's a 3x optical. It can go an addition 8x zoom digitally. Quality-wise, these seem to look better than the previous pan and tilt (e220). The quality of low light video is a bit better, but still not as great as camera's using starlight sensors that can do color night viewing. A nice new feature is the privacy mode where the camera will point itself at a wall and stop recording.
reviews.title: great upgrade over previous one

reviews.body:
Seems to be working just fine now for a few weeks. It does a good job identifying people vs dogs passing through the room.
It is a bit too sensitive to human motion detection as it keeps picking up motion from our TV about 10 ft away and off to the side slightly. Seems to be more an issue when watching soccer games. The camera is connected to a HomeBase 3, so I will see if reducing the sensitivity helps. I could mark the TV as a privacy zone, but then a warning came up seeming to indicate that there would then be no more motion detection recorded by the camera which seemed inconsistent. I could just turn off motion detection for the same result.

It is functional.I have several security cameras installed in my house for both indoor and outdoor. This eufy is the only one has 360  feature. The 360  pan and tilt capabilities ensure a complete view of your space without blind spots.I set this camera for the purpose of watching my kids and pets near the living room and kitchen. The picture quality is great. It provides clear images during both day and night vision.The app is easy to setup. Easy to zoom in for a better view. It s easily to view the notification or the video clip through the app. The camera can use memory card record the videos. Memory card is not included.Overall I m satisfied with this product so far. The cute appearance is like the ET.
reviews.title: Clear images during day and night. Nice app control.

reviews.body: This camera is very impressive. I needed an indoor camera for when I'm on a road trip. I particularly used this to keep an eye on the basement since I've been getting some random flooding lately and I needed to document when and how it happened. The 2K telephoto lens on the camera was VERY helpful and I was able to pinpoint the cracks in the basement wall where the water was seeping through during heavy rainfall. The camera PTZ capability was also very helpful so I could keep track of other areas in the basement.The app was very easy to use and worked seamlessly when I needed to scrub through the footage stored on the SD card. Since the leaking wall wasn't part of what the camera's AI was programmed to detect, it was great that the app worked well enough for me to quickly find the footage that I needed. The night vision looks great as well and the high-resolution camera allows me to see all of the details.If you need an indoor security camera for your home that is easy to use, provide great image quality, and an intuitive app, I can't recommend this camera enough.
reviews.title: I'm very impressed!

reviews.body: For whatever reason, indoor security cams just haven't kept up with outdoor security cams in terms of technology and performance. This one might not deliver cutting edge innovation but it's a definite upgrade from most indoor cams. For one thing, it has a decent f/1.6 aperture sensor. This gives it superior low light performance and the 8 IR lights help make details super clear. The AI powered tracking is solid and the image quality from the two cameras is better than most indoor cams. One camera has a 4K wide angle lens, the other a 2K telephoto lens. It has dual band wi-fi 6 meaning you'll get decent speed from the 5Ghz band. As is the case with most security cams I highly recommended getting the cloud storage. Maybe we'll start to see some innovation in indoor security cams now that eufy has got the ball rolling. Highly recommended!
reviews.title: Decent indoor security cam

reviews.body: Wow, just wow! The performance of this surveillance camera is just amazing. Easy to use and set up, quick and responsive, and the Ai features are powerful. Software is excellent, but because it is so feature-rich, it does take a little time to uncover and unlock all the features. I recommend the HomeBase 3 with this product, as it extends its capabilities and provides local video storage on an internal SSD (SSD not included). I have just purchased a variety of Eufy cameras and am installing them one at a time. The outdoor cameras are next for installation, I can't wait! Go Eufy or go home!

Not only does it have nice upgrades like 4K resolution and 5G Wi-Fi, but the 3x optical zoom is amazing! I just recently switched from Arlo, who so for don t have any cameras with optical zoom. Eufy seems to be ahead of the game with their security tech. So glad I switched to Eufy when I did!

reviews.body: I have been using Eufy webcams for a long time. The C120 is a good basic indoor cam. When this S350 came out, I wanted to compare the two:There are three unique features in the S350. The dual camera of course! The 3x zoom does give a much clearer view of something the distance. I can zoom right into a person s face 20 feet down a long living room. However in practice it is more of a fun thing to do than to make it extremely useful. If this is used outdoor it may be different.This camera supports dual band WiFi 6. The video streaming seems to work much better in my home network. This is a real plus.Finally   the motorized cameras   it will follow a subject, quite accurately, using the motor. This gives a true wider view.All the hardware feature is great. The local AI also works very well. It can detect a person accurately.What is the not so great thing? Eufy cannot design good software interface. Each camera they introduced, the view on the Eufy Security app is a bit different. Because the S350 has more features, the button bars are not scrollable. Between my C120 and the S350, key feature  buttons  are moved around. All this make using the system as a whole more troublesome. Please improve the apps!
reviews.title: Really good video quality, wish software is better

reviews.body: Nice camera easy to set up and install. Very clear picture and I especially like the telephoto mode to get a closer view. The software still needs some work. The app is sometimes a little awkward to use and the human/pet/car detection gives lots of false positives. Especially the pet detection really likes this one chair we have and sometimes gives tons of alerts until I turn the alerts off. Night vision is black and white, but clear. I would expect color at this price. But I guess better to have clear without color.Overall I’m satisfied
reviews.title: Good camera. Software needs work

reviews.body: This indoor camera is actually pretty neat. It has two cameras; one 4k wide angle resolution camera, and one 2k telephoto camera. The best part about it is it s a PTZ (Pan, Tilt, Zoom) camera. This means you can physically rotate the camera around on it s base 360 degrees. It won t spin in a complete circle, but it will rotate pretty much all the way around one way and then the other. It can tilt up and down as well. I don t believe it has a optical zoom, but it uses a combo of both the 4k and 2k cameras to give a decent quality zoom. It has a follow feature which means it will follow the subject around a room, panning and tilting as the subject moves around. I don t know for sure if you have to have the S380 Homebase for this functionality to work or not, as I do have one and it is connected to it, so not sure if that s what gave it this functionality or not. One thing to mention is the instructions are not the clearest when you are connecting it up first. I attempted to connect it to my homebase first, but it said I should connect it  as a router  and then to the HomeBase afterward, but I wasn t sure what it meant,  as a router . I think what it was meaning was to connect it direct to WiFi first, then connect it to the HomeBase which is what I ended up doing and it is working fine.The camera itself seems great. The Eufy app that is required to use with it could use some help (allow me to set a schedule as the Home mode!) but that is not really about the camera, but it is something to note.It actually looks like a little robot with two eyes, and as it follows you around, it almost feels like you have a robot in your house with you lol.
reviews.title: Great camera! Looks like a robot

reviews.body: This security camera is better than expected and I could not be happier for the price!The build quality is great (wish it came in black also) it works smooth! Quiet movement when camera is tracking, picture quality is great and with options of wide and zoomed it’s better!My only issue is with the sound, I don’t know if maybe I set something wrong but the sound works great but there are times I get static sounds instead of voice or whatever it’s picking up. It’s ok though as long as the video is good and it is!
reviews.title: Great for the price security!

reviews.body: I'm extremely impressed by this camera system! My collection includes a total of 12 cameras, 7 solar panels, and a variety of camera types. Among them are 2 doorbell cameras (E340), 2 inside cameras (S350), and a combination of 8 outside cameras (6 S330 and 2 Solo Cam S340). I can't emphasize enough how satisfied I am with this company. The camera quality is crystal clear, the setup process is straightforward, and the cameras can be easily integrated with the home base3, even from a considerable distance.
reviews.title: Best camera system ever love the no monthly charges

reviews.body: I only just received my two S350 eufy security cams yesterday (10/01/23) so I m not very experienced with this device or any other eufy devices as I was exclusively a Wyze cam customer for several years. But I can t believe how much I had been missing now that I have these eufy S350 cams. The device itself feels quality in every way. They are small but sturdy and they feel built to last. The software is intuitive and eufy seems to want you to find everything comfortable to set up. What a concept! Both cams were up and running without a glitch or hitch in minutes. The cams even automatically formatted the microSD cards. What? Yep. It s the little things that make using tech feel good to use and few other companies get this. The video is crisp, the cams use Artificial Intelligence intelligently and you can use 4K, 2k or 1080p depending on your network capabilities. Also, no monthly fees! I highly recommend the eufy S350.
reviews.title: Finally a quality home security camera

reviews.body: I've tried several of the 4K cameras that are available on Amazon and settled on Eufy's because it has the best clarity and the best zoom out of any of the 4K cameras I tested. The design is beautiful, the night vision is impressive, the Eufy App is great, and you can save video on a memory card (unlike the cameras from other different brands, which force you to pay for cloud storage). The deciding factor on me choosing this camera over the several ones I tested, besides the crystal clear resolution, was how friendly and responsive the Eufy team are.
reviews.title: Excellent 4K Camera!

reviews.body:
I have been slowly replacing all my dated security system with ALL Eufy Cameras both inside and outside. Purchased just one of these to make sure it fits my needs indoors before getting a few more.
I am very impressed with this camera and do recommend it highly. Gotta grab a few more to complete my indoor portion of the system.
Initializing this camera to the Homebase 3 was easy and only took about 5 minutes (not counting updating the camera firmware). Combining the Homebase3 (with added large storage SSD drive) and the cameras utilizing the Eufy Security app for IOS and the Alexa integration makes a great and flexible system.
The only suggestion I would make is for Eufy to think about adding 4 to 5 feet on the included USB C power cableas 6 foot is too short.
Eufy, in my opinion, is by far the best system I have installed over the years having changed our security system 3 times in the past 31 years to keep up with the technology.
reviews.title: Loving the Indoor Cam S350
reviews.author: Robert M.

reviews.body: I had the opportunity to participate in the beta testing of this product, and I must say it exceeded my expectations. Its sleek design, the UI intuitive, and its performance are solid. The video clarity is also excellent, which makes it very useful for my garage deliveries. Eufy showed great responsiveness to feedback and made necessary improvements. I highly recommend this solution to anyone needing a reliable indoor PTZ camera. Its engineering and customer focus are outstanding.
reviews.title: Innovative and Afforable

reviews.body: I'm already in the Eufy ecosystem with about 8 other cameras, so this was a nice addition to cover a wide angle view of an interior room.Setup is a dead simple as any other Eufy camera. Just scan the code as you are setting up with the app and it adds it to the system.Quality of the image is good and the detection features seem to work pretty well. This is definitely an upgrade option over the older Eufy PTZ cameras, which I have and still use.
reviews.title: I like this little came...nice addition to my Eufy setup

reviews.body: This thing transmits 4k video easily, and I'm pretty glad I get to have it at home. It connects easily and setup is simple, especially right after you install the Eufy app. I have a 50mbps upload, so it's no problem sending out 4k video. It's got Wifi 6 so it's even faster than older cameras. Pretty happy. Plus there's no subscription fee with the basic setup.And it does a good job at detecting the scenes. I leave this on 24/7, and it hasn't been a problem at all. My old Arlo is being retired as we speak.
reviews.title: Amazing upgrade to my old 1080p camera

reviews.body: I love all my Eufy cameras and I just added this one to the set. Overall, it works great. The object detection really works well and it tracks me and my pets just fine. But the zoom lens on this is a bit of a gimmick because in order to record with both lenses you have to drop the resolution of the wide angle lens to 2K. It's really not much better than just recording the wide angle at 4K and digitally zooming it. Instead of saving 2 separate movie files (a wide and zoom video), it creates one single movie with both lenses stacked on top of each other which I guess is a good option, but I wish it would record them separately too. Also, the zoom version seems to not be aimed quite where you'd want most of the time, so it might record a closeup of someone's face, or, more likely it will record a closeup of their chest or waist.
reviews.title: Not sure if zoom lens is really helpful.

reviews.body:
Camera hardware seems well built; however, I had to return the device. Eufy is alienating majority of the market by refusing to add HomeKit support and/or Google Home support. Eufy is currently taking advantage of the consumer base, lack of knowledge of the advantages of having these systems integrate into third-party apps.
For instance, I can run automations based off a person being detected between a certain time for the lights in the bathroom to go on and eventually go off.
I will say something that Eufy will not tell you directly. Eufy has no plans on integrating HomeKit and once the current products are discontinued that do have HomeKit, they have no plans on replacing those.
My goal was to integrate the whole house with Eufy but I had to stop when I found out they had no intentions of adding HomeKit support.
reviews.title: Lacks Integration
reviews.author: Eufy_Honest A.

reviews.body: I really like this camera. It works very well. It controls well over the phone. I have an iPhone, but using the speaker to talk through the camera does not seem to work properly. There’s a constant clicking noise or high-pitched sound that just doesn’t seem to go away. I’ve looked up information to try and stop it from doing that, but it just does not seem to stop, there’s a problem with the speaker or the hardware or something but overall it’s a good camera good quality and worth it for the money once they fix the chirping noise that it makes.
reviews.title: Clicking noises!

reviews.body: The eufy Security Indoor Cam S350 is a game-changer in home security. With its 4K UHD resolution, 8× zoom, and 360° PTZ capabilities, it offers unparalleled clarity and coverage. The advanced Human/Pet AI and dual-camera setup make it an ideal choice for not only home security but also as a reliable baby monitor or pet camera. The seamless integration of dual-band Wi-Fi 6 and easy plug-in installation further solidify its position as a top-tier option in the smart home security landscape.
reviews.title: Works Great

reviews.body: I am new to Eufy, was very exciting trying out this new dual camera setup. It was very easy getting everything connected, just follow the app instructions. Everything connected less than 5 mins. The video quality is pretty nice, and the dual camera with standard and zoom image is very helpful. I am able look around the room look for my pets, or some small items on the table/desk. The auto follow setting is not bad, not perfect, but usable. The only problem I don't like is in the UI notification setting, there is not set schedule when to turn on the notification and when to turn it off. When I am home or day time, I would like the notification auto off, and night time I would want the auto notification on. Hope there can be more features and customizations in the future.
reviews.title: Nice video quality, but UI need some improvement.

reviews.body: The camera works fine. However, the range of filming and the motion detection are both very limited. You can only get video of very near areas. Based on the website description and movement of it, we thought it could detect motion and record film in a much greater area. I painstakenly ran the wires and built a mount for it that was perfect for a camera that can see more than 10 feet away. But, this camera can't and so it is pretty useless where I put it. If it could catch 25 feet, it would have been perfect. Just know this camera is very limited.
reviews.title: Not as good as promised
reviews.author: Graham

reviews.body: I really like Eufy. I bought this and added it on to my system. It connects easily with home base 3. Easy to set up. Nice clear picture. Sounds good. The only thing I wish I could change is it only records in 2 min. Increments. That doesn’t have anything to do with the camera itself. That is how eufy is set up. There are no extra subscription fees either. Great system.
reviews.title: Great camera

reviews.body: I got this to keep track of my five kitties when I am at work, and this works like a charm! You have the option to get notifications for human or animal movement, and also an option to record the video to a local microSD card. The app is also very easy to use and intuitive, and allows you to pan/tilt the camera angle as well as zoom in. Also love the fact that this camera does not have any monthly subscription fees, so although the price may be higher than some of the other pet cams, no subscription fees means that this camera will actually be cheaper in the long run. Highly recommend!
reviews.title: Great pet cam!

reviews.body: The ID is top tier, it looks high tech and feel really good to the touch, like a robot instead of the look of camera. Only worry I have is when young kids coming to our house, they might attempt to toy with it thinking it is a robot.Other than the modern design, the dual focal lens is really a leapfrog from the many 2k eufy pan/tilt camera that I have deployed all around my house, now I can see clearly optically. As a long time Eufy user i really appreciate the Eufy team working hard to make innovative and useful products.
reviews.title: Elegant and functional

reviews.body: UPDATE: So after a lot of troubleshooting, I was able to get the camera on my network and update the firmware. It was quite difficult because the camera/app aren't really compatible with mesh networks. In my case, my phone kept trying to access the 5Ghz band while the camera was locking in on the 2.4Ghz band. And it refused to play nice with my guest network. So once I got it online, and confirmed every device was on the same band, it updated the firmware and it's been smooth sailing ever since. I wish there was some kind of heads up about mesh network issues during onboarding, but it worked out in the end. Great camera now that it's got a stable firmware!-------------------------Original: I bought the S350 to replace a very unreliable HomeKit camera and this one doesn’t seem to be much better. It frequently disconnects from the WiFi network despite my network being a very high end mesh network.I will say that when it works, it’s amazing. The tracking is very fast and accurate, the video quality is great and I love the optical zoom. But none of that is of value if the camera doesn’t work. I frequently have to unplug it so it will reconnect. Pretty sure I will be sending it back.
reviews.title: UPDATE: Be sure to update the firmware.

description: A plethora of users, moving beyond their initial use for simple pet monitoring, have integrated these cameras into robust smart security systems that prioritize security without the need for cloud storage. This focus on privacy, with data being stored solely on a local 128GB microSD card, appeals to many who are wary of traditional cloud-based systems with potentially questionable data management practices. Installation of the Eufy cameras is notably user-friendly. This has drawn praise for its seamless integration with existing home network setups, whether through Wi-Fi or wired connections. The cameras deliver impressive performance, with excellent picture quality and highly responsive motion tracking, outperforming many older models and competing brands. The two-way audio functionality adds a playful dimension to the experience, facilitating communication with family members and charming pet interactions. The cameras' design and features have been well-received, and many users express excitement over their potential uses, from monitoring pets to providing care assistance for loved ones. This blend of functionality, privacy, and ease of use makes the Eufy Indoor Cam S350 a highly recommended choice for home security.

reviews.body:
Most current update : Battery life suck!.....(just saying) Had to pull out the battery to recharge every month, regardless of settings. (BUT) I still like this doorbell.

Original review:
Eufy's latest doorbell. It looks great, nice and sleek, and sturdy, and very well put together. Also great for the price. Charging the battery unit was not a big deal. Setup was easy. Wifi connection was quick. Apps navigation was also easy.

The Cons: IMO, was (1). Battery life. After one week of using it. The life percentage dropped by more than 10%-15% with what I believed an average motion detections. (2). Night lights on the bottom and top cannot be turn off, without turning off the night vision option. It is not "On" all the time but only comes on when motion is detected and only at night with night vision option selected. Would be nice if "OFF/ ON" option is allow when night vision is turn on without interfering with the night vision ability. It is annoying when the lights come on when motion is detected. (3) Most importantly, the doorbell chime. The chime from the device can only he heard only from outside on the device itself. You cannot hear the chime when you're indoor if and when someone rang the doorbell. Existing indoor chime would need an upgrade on to increase voltage capacity, only if you know how to DIY. So you do need an add-on Chime device. Eufy should have included one without additional purchase or add-on purchase. I gave it 3 stars because of these nuances.

reviews.body: Excellent video and much faster response time than my Arlo. I love the two cameras which show the person and directly down for packages. I'm having trouble keeping it connected to my existing door chime but I think the problem is the chime not Eufy as it would not work consistently with the Arlo. I will probably purchase the separate wireless door chime that also allows for an SD card for extra video storage.

reviews.body: I specifically asked before i bought this doorbell about it being in the sun before i purchased it and they said it wouldn't be a problem. As soon as it hits 80 degrees outside and the sun hits it. The doorbell overheats. Keep in mind my placement is away from the sun up untill 6pm at night. When the sun goes down, until that time it's fully shaded all day. I asked the questions before i bought the doorbell because where i live it get all over 100 degrees outside during the summertime. I will add photos for proof if it allows me to with my review, that being said i have had multiple brands of video doorbells and none of them overheated.

name: Security SoloCam S340 Solar Pan & Tilt
bestFor: 360° continuous solar-powered tracking without running power cables

specifications.name: Highlighted Features
specifications.value: Spotlight, Dual Views, Pan / Tilt, Solar-Powered

specifications.name: Indicators
specifications.value: Tiny LED indicator (blue when charging, off when fully charged)

reviews.body:
If you’re in the market for a camera that doesn’t require any wiring, this is a very solid choice.

Cons:

In low-light conditions (around an hour after sunset), the AI struggles to detect people and cars beyond 50 metres. Anything within 40 metres is detected reliably, but between 40–50 metres it becomes inconsistent. As a result, I get very few recordings during the night unless the activity is close to the house. Ideally, I’d like a bit more coverage further down the street.
The pan-and-tilt elevation could benefit from an additional 5–10 degrees. It’s fine for the wide-angle view, but when using the telephoto zoom at longer distances (50+ metres), that extra elevation would make a noticeable difference. (more a preference than a con)

Pros:

Overall:
The camera performs very well across the board. It reliably detects people and vehicles moving along the street and stores recordings locally on its internal memory. Both the wide-angle and telephoto lenses are effective, with the latter offering a true 3x optical zoom (which is far superior to digital zoom). The unit gives you the option to see either a wide angle view, a split screen with wide angle and telephoto view or just the telephoto view.

Audio quality is good—you can clearly hear and speak through the unit—and it includes a built-in alarm that’s impressively loud, easily enough to alert neighbours at night. The integrated light is also a useful addition. Image quality is excellent on both lenses.

Connectivity:
WiFi performance is excellent. The camera consistently shows around 4 out of 5 bars and was extremely easy to set up—probably the simplest WiFi connection process I’ve experienced. This is a big improvement compared to my Ring doorbell, which required a signal extender and still struggles with connectivity.

Solar Power:
This was initially a concern, but it turned out to be one of the strongest features. The camera uses about 5% battery per day and only recharges when it drops below 97%. Despite limited sun exposure (mine only gets morning sunlight), the solar panel recharges it fully in about an hour. The app also provides detailed charging data, including milliamps generated. If you’re worried about solar performance, there’s no need—it works very well.

Durability:
The camera itself feels solid and well-built. However, the wall-mounting bracket is less impressive and feels like it may wear out sooner than the camera unit.

Subscriptions:
Optional subscriptions are available, but they’re not necessary. All footage is stored locally and can be accessed at any time. Recordings are overwritten after about 5–7 days, depending on your settings. Mine is configured to continue recording for 45 seconds after motion stops.

Installation:
Everything needed for installation is included (screws and wall plugs). You’ll need three screws for the camera and two for the solar panel, although the solar panel can also be mounted directly onto the camera.

Advice:
Install the camera as high as possible—ideally at or above 15 feet—for the best coverage and performance.
