I'm sending the RTSP stream to an NVR for monitoring, and the steram stopped working in the middle of the night. Manually connecting to the stream from another player also didn't work, so something with the device itself is breaking. The stream to the Reolink app was working fine.

I already checked that I was on the latest firmware when I first installed the camera, and it was when I used the Reolink desktop app. Despite the app stating "you're on the latest firmware update", it definitely wasn't. Reolink's Download Center had a newer version months ago, so I downloaded that and it's currently updating...except the update is stuck. It's been 10 minutes now, the app is stuck "uploading files", it's moving every so slowly.

Firmware and RTSP aside, installation was pretty simple and instructions were clear. The 2-way voice communication is super quiet and seems to be poor quality. Also, the POE didn't work at all, luckily I was powering by the doorbell connection.

I paid for this via PayPal and it was PayPal who fought for me and got my money back!
I have a paper trail and receipts of everything that happened.
DO NOT BUY! AND BE CAREFUL WITH THE SUBSCRIPTION YOU PURCHASE!

-Also, I had to turn the night vision off. It works better off. For the first month it was great.
-Does not capture everything. If a person walks out to your driveway, the camera will not record them walking back to the house. I've had this happen a countless amount of times with animals, people walking, cars, etc.
-Has a mind of its own, will turn off audio volume off when it wants to.
-Camera vision is blurry and not high quality visuals.
-Sound quality is distorted.
-Battery life also has a mind of its own. Sometimes it will last a month while at the next charge it only lasts for 2 weeks.
-Software used (app) is extremely delayed. Sometimes I won't receive the notification until 2-5 minutes later. While other times I won't receive anything.
-Sometimes the program itself will not load.
reviews.title: Don't Buy
reviews.author: Amber

reviews.body: I have owned four google nest cameras for the past two years, and they have been an absolute disaster. They randomly shut off and cannot be remotely turned back on. I have to get a ladder, go outside, and manually cycle the power. Of my four cameras, two are usually offline at any given time. The event detection algorithm is awful. 24/7 history is a paid feature, and automatic event detection routinely misses critical events. If you didn't pay for 24/7, you're out of luck. Event missed. Does not record based on sound events, only visual. So if someone out of sight is blowing an air horn at your house, the camera will not record it. The new AI features are aggressively useless, given the lack of competently-designed basic features. The camera has a green light on it that flashes when you are viewing its stream online, showing potential criminals and robbers that they are being actively watched while they try to break into your house. There is no way to disable the flashing green light, other than putting black tape over it. The Nest app is worthless. And best of all, the cameras are only able to record 3 minutes of event at a time. So if someone trespasses on your property for more than 3 minutes, then it is possible that your camera will fail to record the entire event. 3 minutes is the max. The default event length is 30 seconds. You have to MANUALLY set it at 3 minutes. This product is horrible. Horrible. It is overpriced, functionless garbage. Google makes awful hardware, and the app and software that support it are similarly awful. After two years of fighting these cameras to get them to do basic things, and two years of chasing them with my ladder every few weeks, I am giving up. I give up. I am going to go play baseball with them and buy a useful model. Never again will I buy a Google device. As far as I'm concerned, Google Nest outdoor cameras are a scam.
reviews.title: Terrible product that does not work
reviews.author: Airpower

reviews.body: pretty decent clarity and battery life. There are 2 things about it that I dont love. 1- Its not as sensitive as I thought (meaning it takes a min to start recording when anyone is in view). But the reason I would not recommend it is because they try to force you to buy a subscription to keep your videos. If not, it only saves a few at a time and then resets sometime during the night. So I cant even see what it picked up that night (which is why I got it in the first place!)
reviews.title: Pass
reviews.author: Ray

reviews.body: First off DO NOT RUN THESE USING BATTERIES. Second if you have connection issues with these cameras it isn't the camera its your subpar router. I love these Google cameras. All of my smart home items are integrated into the Google environment and my wife and I use pixel devices so it all works cohesively for the most part. Now as for the camera I have never had issues with connecting. I have no lag however I have invested heavily in my own home network. I have 2 gig fiber internet with a cat8 line from my ONT feeding two Asus be88u routers with a 10gig sfp+ Ethernet backhaul between them. I ran cat6a runs to all bedrooms and the living room to reduce the number of wifi connecting devices. These cameras connect to the 5ghz band which is awesome considering most smart home devices only allow the 2.4ghz. for those of you who don't know the main differences between the two here is the most important to remember. 5ghz is stronger but will go shorter distances. 2.4 ghz can reach farther distances however the signal is less reliable. I subscribe to the nest aware for 80 bucks a year which allows me to set it and forget it as far as saving vid clips. I purchased the 30 ft power cord extension which is a must for these cameras and ran them down my j channel siding into an open outlet in my crawlspace. These devices are only viable if they have constant power and a good router to connect to as with most consumer security cameras. I have 3 of these and the door bell cam which covers the main outside areas of my entire home perimeters. The only times I have ever had any warning about camera function is during our extremely cold winter weather season and even at -10 this past winter not once did I loose function just a warning in the app about the cold temps. If you have problems with these cameras I highly suggest educating yourself because these are the most user friendly cameras I have ever used and over two years I have yet to have a problem that could be blamed on the product.
reviews.title: You get what you pay for
reviews.author: Bman567

reviews.body: Despite owning two Nest Outdoor (Wired) cameras which had worked flawlessly for years, I'm returning this indoor/outdoor battery camera after less than a week. After fully charging the camera, I placed in on our lanai. It worked fine from 1pm until the middle of the night, where I discovered the camera was completely dead. After bringing the camera in and charging it, the battery would only get to 27%. Once again I placed it outside, and despite a great wifi connection, the resolution is grainy at best. As much as I enjoy my original Nest outdoor cameras, this one was a total bust for me.
reviews.title: Completely dissasitifed
reviews.author: VinoPro

reviews.body:
Google may be a good software company. However, after buying the Nest outdoor camera six months ago, it now will not power up. Charging it doesn't seem to help. I scanned the code on the box for assistance, and only got a timeout waiting for help. Telephone and chat were unresponsive as well.
The device has six months of warranty left, but of course returning it with refund is not an option.
I am therefore generously giving on star to this review.
reviews.title: Faulty Outdoor Camera with no help
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.body:
It was purchased to use as a baby cam as it was highly rated. Does not connect to the Google hub with any volume. Unfortunately, there's no help available to get it to work with volume. Google Hub rarely accepts verbal commands to stream the camera while being used as a baby monitor. While using it on my phone, the picture only stays on the screen for a max of 2 min before I manually have to reactivate it. So if you are considering this camera for a baby monitor, I highly recommend you don't.
The camera quality when it is on is great. When I finally get it to stream on the Hub, the picture is great, but like I said, no way, no how, can I get the volume to work, so you have to watch the camera to know if he wakes up or not. keep in mind my review is for a baby monitor. Lots of reviews say its good for that, but not in my experience.
reviews.title: Bought to use as a Baby Cam
reviews.author: Kelly

reviews.body: I bought these cameras because I had bought google nest cameras years ago and they were way better than Ring cameras, which was their only real competition at the time... oh how they have fallen! I installed these cameras and I was severely disappointed. these cameras are battery powered with no silicone plug to keep moisture out of the port, the range sucks... I moved my router literally right next to the wall next to the closest camera and I changed the settings to maximized bandwidth and signal still isn't constant, the picture quality is of the same quality of a 1st gen camera phone so if I need photo evidence it's going to be completely useless, the battery has dropped 3% in just the first 45 minutes of the cameras being up. for almost $400 I expected to be able to live view my cameras while I'm away from home. that's not possible while the camera is in battery mode. I will be returning these cameras at my next trip to Lowe's
reviews.title: Terrible cameras all the way around
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.body:
Very dsappointed with camera, I started the return procedure in the dead of the night on day of purchase and took it back the day after.

Intened use: monitor childs nocturnal seizures

Pros:

It's Google; magnetic effortless placement; sleek design for indoors; super HD picture and super zoom-in; no delay live streaming on 5G wifi; 2-way audio; free cloud storage; can clear all recordings in google home app, easy setup and controls

Cons:
Misleading operations, a subscription is required to receive notification and save recordings beyond 3 hours not that you can store 3 hrs worth of recording at a time! Because even after I cleared the footage from the day time durning my setup of device and lounging around fiddling with it the camera only functioned as live stream with no more notifications before I subscribed to their trial. (researched confirmed in google community support forum post that this is intended)

Cannot simply detect any motion by change of "pixles" and only detect by preset categories of person, animal, or vehicle etc.

Does not record intial detection and records too long after detection. examples: Notification when child sat up in the middle of the night but only recorded as they were laying back down. Notification when child woke up and ran out of the room in the morning but only recorded an empty room not even a blur of child.

We are required to set max length to limit individual recordings (10s, 15s, etc). Therefore unfortunately if an event is longer than the max recording limit, it just stops recording the event. You wont be given a series of notifications and clips for the duration of the event.
reviews.title: Disappointing captures and misleading performance
reviews.author: Troya

reviews.body:
Never have I bought a more poorly working product that not supported by the manufacturer in my life.
I installed 3 of this particular outdoor cameras before I left Florida for the north, the very day I leave they won’t work. Battery issues when they are plugged in. So all summer I had almost zero surveillance around my Florida house. Once in a while one of them would work for a bit but mostly not at all. Anyway Google said we would troubleshoot upon my return and we have done that now 3 times. Still not working consistently, intermittent reliability. I asked to speak to a manager at google some 5 days ago and still no one has called.
Do not buy google security, buy anything else but google it’s just junk and the support from google is worse than poor!
reviews.title: Worst product ever
reviews.author: Tony

reviews.body:
Have had this for about a year. Generally been ok, the battery is average after a good first stint it now needs charging fairly regularly. The main issue is the one time we needed it, it didn't capture anything. It pings me all day when the neighbor across the street is walking by, but when someone broke into the car on the drive in the night woke up to nothing.

I expect these will soon be discontinued anyway like Google nest smoke detectors and you'll be left with another stranded piece of tech. My advice - buy from a dedicated security company.
reviews.title: Failed to detect cat theft - avoid
reviews.author: Richard

reviews.body: I have several Nest cameras, and we were excited to see a wireless version so we wouldn't have to drill through our outside walls. I knew there might be some lag with the new camera being wireless. There definitely is a lag (over 30 seconds sometime), but my biggest problem it that they have stopped using the Nest App! Set up was through Google Home, which was easy, but I like seeing all my cameras, thermostats, and the doorbell all at once without having to click on different icons to view them. When I called, I was told future devices will not use the Nest App. Google Home does not offer one screen to view everything or preview the cameras. In Google Home, you can click on cameras and WAIT awhile for them all to load. Google Home needs a lot more development and is not user friendly form your phone. With the Nest App it was fast and always available. I could also find Nest Aware a lot easier. This wireless camera did not connect to Nest Aware automatically, so my subscription is currently useless with the new camera. Support was unable to help me, and said, "this is new for us too, and none of us know how it works yet." I think this a push to buy their Google Home screens. Not cool Google! I was excited for the new line up, but I will probably get a whole new systems that is more user friendly. Having the Nest name and needing multiple apps is no user friendly.
reviews.title: Does not work with Nest App...
reviews.author: MarylandBound

reviews.body: Absolute garbage. If I could give it ZERO I would. Battery won't charge once it's -5C and you have to take camera down and do a head reset only to have the same thing happen once it gets cold again. No video since January 8th so far and I'm not climbing up a ladder to reset it. Doesn't matter if it's plugged in or not. Contrary to what the company says, the battery died not lag. It dies. It will not even attempt to charge unless you take down the camera and reset it. Absolutely useless customer service and if you send in your camera for issues, they send you a refurbished one as a replacement.
reviews.title: Doesn't work once it's -5C ZERO STARS
reviews.author: Nestisgarbage

reviews.body: I love these cameras, but the battery doesn't last very long in my neighborhood cause they get a lot of clips so I run a constant power wire to them which isn't hard to do and not very expensive but besides that they work great and they're very versatile with their mounting awesome picture awesome wide angle and sound
reviews.title: Love them
reviews.author: Kevin

reviews.body:
Worst camera for the price! After 3 yrs it takes 18 hours to charge, freezes all the time, doesnt pick up on small animals (skunk, racoon etc) which is what I purchased it for! I would not recommend this item. When I called they said my battery is done! 3yrs, and the item is garbage? you cannot replace the battery. Much better options out there that last and pick up on animals also clearer picture.
I have the door bell as well and would say its just ok, but again for the price its not worth it. So disappointing.
reviews.title: Google Nest Camera wire free outdoor
reviews.author: JM

reviews.body: Sleek camera and it has good quality footage, but it was a NIGHTMARE to set up. The actual mounting was pretty quick and easy and I like the strong magnet to where you can set it up at any angle you need. However, setting it up in the app took at least an hour. So many hoops you have to jump through just to complete set up. Then, I wanted to sign up for Nest Aware, and it was horrible just to figure out how to buy it and set it up for the camera. I'm a pretty tech-savvy person, so I can't imagine how insane this would be for someone who isn't. I somewhat regret buying this because of how difficult it was, but hopefully it'll pay off now that I finally have it set up. I miss the original Nest and wish Google wouldn't have botched this brand!
reviews.title: Nightmare to Set Up
reviews.author: Rachelle R

reviews.body:
I bought two of these due to the google branding but turned out to be an absolute waste of my money.
The reasons I bought
* Google customer service
* Ease to start/stop subscription
* wireless
* Facial recognition
* Event based notifications

Subscription is a scam:
* They bill yearly but if you cancel anytime in the year, you will get $0 refund. So put a reminder and cancel it right on the year bill cycle end else be ready to the hit.
So unless you are ready to pay $100/year for nothing don't buy. Without that there is only 3hrs recording you would get so no point buying without subscription In other words, DON'T buy, thank me later.

Product is of C grade quality
* Facial recognition sucks, after two years of learning it get confused between man and woman, GOSH. Did google really made this facial recognition software, I doubt.
* Event based notification doesn't work, it missed the two important events for me which my neighbours' wyze camera caught it else I would have paid $1200 from my pocket. In Nest's yearly subscription you can buy two wyze camera, what a joke, and they are better than this... AMAZING
* Battery backup, again a big thumbs down. If you expect 0 movement in the camera zone, then yes battery life will be 6months else it can be as low as month. so better buy a wired one 24x7 recording and no subscription
* Every time you take out camera for charging, you would need to reset the zones so that it aligns. I.e. camera needs to be in exact same positon as before.

After two years I realized that's nothing is good about this product. Hence putting it in it's right place "TRASH"
reviews.title: Complete Waste Of Money, DON'T BUY it's A SCAM
reviews.author: MSH

reviews.body: I was so excited to get this but was extremely let down. Long story short it requires a subscription, the battery life is a joke, and it is absolutely TERRIBLE at detecting & recording movement AKA not helpful for security at all. First off, you need a subscription to do anything except view the live feed. There’s one level where you pay for restricted recording and history that auto deletes at a specific amount of days, or you pay more and get unlimited recording and saving. Second, if you have all notifications/recording on, the battery lasts MAYBE 2 days. If you have half the notifications/recording on, you get up to a week if nothing happens. I had to turn off all notifications and really restrict the movement it records to get this to last 1 week at a time before I have to recharge it. I purchased this BATTERY camera because the ideal place for it does not have access to a plug unless I trail an extension cord along the floor or ceiling. Another big con is with the limited recording AKA can never and will never record the entire time, it will ONLY record when there is movement. This thing is so so bad at “detecting” movement. I will be moving all around my apartment for hours and the camera will MAYBE detect my movement once, unless I’m super close to the camera. When I try to use it to watch my dog, it doesn’t detect his movements at all so I can’t see anything since there is no recordings to watch. Do not purchase this camera. If you are set on getting a camera from google, get the regular plug in kind since the battery barely adds any life. Even better, to purchase a cheaper version on a big marketplace website (hint hint) that’s actually worth the money. Also if you do decide to keep this plugged in, you’ll have to purchase additional pieces for it to stand upright, another non-win for the item. P.S. I figured since this is so easily portable I could hook it up and use it at other places. NOT the case, trying to make it work has completely wiped the history and now it won’t even work with my regular home Wifi/google devices and is now a piece of junk taking up space.
reviews.title: Such a bummer
reviews.author: Squid

reviews.body:
So excited to get these new cameras - that was short lived. I am still impressed with the hardware. Good picture, rugged design, simple install.

First disappointment was that these can only be set up in the google home app. This doesnt have nearly the functionality or ease of use of the Nest app. You can view all of the cameras right up front in a good dashboard view.

Since they are battery, they go into a low use mode to conserve energy so you have to "wake them up" each time you want to have a look. Not a fan of this but maybe its necessary.

the worst is that I have a cadre of Nest products of the older generation and the integration of the two is awful. It took the Google support guy 1 hour and 15 min to talk me through a completely unintuitive migration process ( including such stupid features as you must add the nest hello doorbell before adding the nest thermostat otherwise you wont be able to add both??? Do they test this with users? Is that really so difficult to solve?). How would a consumer ever figure out a process that takes a trained expert so long to explain??? Then, once set up, you can only really configure and manage the "old" devices through the Nest app!! Redic...

Hey Google - use the tech your acquisitions bring cause they are way better than the junk you halfway threw together to replace it.

If I didnt have all the legacy hardware, I would definitely go a different route...
reviews.title: Google ruined a great product
reviews.author: DisappointedNester

reviews.body:
This camera is quite useless for motion detection more than 10-15 feet away when being used only in battery mode. And worse, the recording only starts about 3-5 seconds after detecting motion - so the recordings miss way too much to be useful. The camera works fine in live mode but who wants to watch live all day and then run the battery down!

However, if the camera is connected to power with the charge cable, then the camera and motion detection is excellent for instant recordings at substantial distances. But then why buy a battery powered device if it only really works effectively when hard wired.

Google does not tell you about this until you call the tech support to find out if the camera is defective for missing too many events.

Hats off though to Google support - very easy to access.

Buy the wired model and forget the battery one. My ratings would be 4-5 stars if I rated the camera in wired mode.

Shame on google for misrepresenting this camera. They know it’s limitations in battery mode, that’s how I found out about plugging it in. But they don’t tell you in the product description.
reviews.title: Misrepresentation of capabilities

reviews.body:
Sure! Here's an improved version of your review:

---

**Disappointing Performance – Not Worth the Money**

I regret purchasing this camera. It doesn’t record anything, and despite adjusting all settings, it still fails to detect motion or alert me when someone walks by. I’ve tried troubleshooting, but nothing seems to work. Save yourself the hassle and invest in a more reliable option, like a Ring camera. This has been one of the worst purchases I’ve made. Don't waste your money on this product.
reviews.title: Disappointing Performance – Not Worth the Money
reviews.author: Love0505

reviews.body: Product ordering and delivery went smoothly. Th camera itself is easy to install and functions flawlessly. I have it outside with a solar charger. So far I have not had to remove it to recharge inside. I suggest it be installed where you can access it, though, for times you may need to recharge it.
reviews.title: Works as advertised
reviews.author: Gary

reviews.body: We just added this battery powered camera to our subscription… great picture quality etc. But it will only trigger and record events within an hour or so after we open the app and view a live feed. Those few events are recorded and and saved consistently as do the other 7 cameras in my subscription. But after an hour or so, the camera turns off completely and is only revived again by opening the app and triggering a live view. I am sure that somehow the camera is still operating under the “free” features that come without a subscription. But I’ve added this camera to my Nest Aware account and it's still a no-go. I am sure the problem will be that somehow I haven’t upgraded or selected some convoluted new “plus” or “plus plus” or “super plus” or “premium plus extra super googly nesty nest” setting or add-on to my subscription… Please help.
reviews.title: camera won’t trigger and record events
reviews.author: nickname

reviews.body: Easy to set up and well built product. Complements Nest doorbell. Battery life is unknown at this time, in its favor, back yard has very little activity to trigger the cam recording so that should help. It has been very cold, so that will reduce life. It will likely take 8 or 9 months to really assess life over several seasons.
reviews.title: Well built quality product, easy to set up.
reviews.author: JGS5607

reviews.body: Bought this Google Nest Indoor/Outdoor Battery camera on Lowes.com. Many issues here. First of all, this new Nest camera battery version does not work with the original Nest app which is ridiculous. You have to use Google Home app for the battery powered Nest camera. No more 24x7 viewing either. Only "events" are logged and you have to connect to the camera via Google Home app to view live feed which stops after a few minutes via phone viewing and shows as idle (see photo). You cannot view video from the web which is ridiculous. My Google Nest Hub display device keeps losing signal for the battery camera feed as well. And no, the camera is not too far from the wifi router. You can't keep a specific video clip that you create...only the "events" logged by the camera. If I want video of a deer that was out of range of the motion detector, forget that. Right now, I have the Nest Aware subscription with 10 day 24x7 video history. Nest battery camera doesn't work with Nest Aware subscription either. Go figure. This camera appears to only have video history when connected to electricity (as I was charging the cam inside my house before installing it outside) so I ordered the 30 foot electrical cord from Google and waiting on that. Not sure how I can keep watch on my backyard when there is no 24x7 video history. I have a large backyard which means an intruder would have to be within 10 feet of this camera. I stood within 5 feet of it, waving my arms around, and no event was logged. Trying to decide whether to keep this Google Nest battery camera or send it back and get the Google Nest wired camera before other retailers sell out. I have two original wired Nest cams that are great (although the video clarity went down after Google bought Nest) and a Nest thermostat that works great as well. Google took a fantastic product (the original Nest cam) and ruined it. There are a lot of comments like mine out on the Google forums. Poor rollout and sorry I didn't look at the Google forums and instead relied on the "five star" promotional reviews on Lowes' site before I bought this lesser item.
reviews.title: Piece of junk replaces original wired Nest cam
reviews.author: LisaLisa

reviews.body: As the title states; this camera has great picture quality, is easy to setup, and even easier to use! The only reason I've given it 3 stars instead of 5 is due to it's motion sensing. When it detects someone, it doesn't turn on (it sleeps until motion is detected) until they are half way across it's field of view which usually means the angle is wrong for face detection. This means the camera almost never recognizes anyone (even me and my family) and I can rarely see who was in my yard. I can still see that "someone" was there. Just not "who".
reviews.title: Great picture quality and easy to setup/use
reviews.author: AdamG

reviews.body: I had two battery-operated cameras, and eventually, they would no longer charge. Additionally, I had perfectly functioning smoke detectors, but Google decided to support no longer the product, which forced me into buying new smoke detectors (my mistake). Then, Google decided to stop supporting my perfectly operating generation 1 and 2 thermostats, so I could no longer use the app to control my thermostats. I will no longer be buying any Google products.
reviews.title: No more Google products
reviews.author: stevenw

reviews.body: Disapointing.. I'm a google fan and supporter. My phone, ear buds, speakers and smart home devices are all google / nest hardware. These cameras look great! The quality feel is great. The setup was easy. The video quality was great for what I need. So why am I disapointed? Sometimes Google fails on execution, and this is one of those times. As I noted, I was able to quickly setup the camera in my Google home app. But later I tried to streem the video to my TV with google Chromecast... "the device is not setup for streeming" What? yeah can't streem to my TV. Then I notice after a few days I no longer see notifications that my camera spotted someone? Let me check... Yeah, it's off... Batter OK? Yep! Let me look online. Many complaints of the same. poor wifi, maybe wifi was interupted is the main guess. OK, well my wifi signal is great where the camera is. Could there be an interuption? Definitly. Who doesnt occasionaly have an internet interuption? What, the camera doesn't try to recover? Every other device in my house does? OK, simple fix. I'll setup a routine to turn the camera on so if it goes off at least I know it will eventual get turned back on, without me having to do it manualy. Nope, even though it's in my Google home app, Google assistant says it's not setup? Wait, what? So I try to set it up under assistant settings. Nope, says maybe try the Nest App? So I try the Nest App. Nope, says setup with Google Home app! So I can't setup a routine. Frustrating and Disapointing!
reviews.title: High hopes followed by disapointment
reviews.author: Sean

reviews.body:
These work best when plugged in full time and with the 24hr recording subscription. Otherwise, some features are disabled. Like animal detection and 24/7 cloud-saved video. The lower tier subscription records motion events, but these don't always detect motion from animals even when plugged in. We used to have the lower tier sub (with the camera plugged in full time), but even when an eagle flew 30 ft in front of the camera or a deer walked past, it didn't detect the motion. In those cases, you can't go back and see it in your history. So, we upgraded to 24/7 recording. The camera also does not record 24/7 if you are running it just off the battery.
The camera loves bugs. It doesn't turn on when a deer walks by, but moths fly by for all of one second, and it detects and records that. We added a camera to monitor the hummingbird feeder so we could catch the raccoons climbing the post and tearing it down at night (they just recently found it). However, we ran this camera solely on battery. Despite being less than 10 feet from the feeder... the camera didn't detect any motion, and the raccoons ravaged the feeder without being recorded. So, we have ordered the cable to have it powered full time, and even if it doesn't detect motion, at least we have 24/7 video history that you don't get with just the battery.
Another thing you should know is if you live in a place with below-freezing temperatures in the winter. The battery does not hold its charge well and drains incredibly quickly. This was another reason we added the cable. In our experience, though, when we lost power one night in the dead of winter, we found that the battery also hadn't charged during the cold temperatures, despite being plugged in 24/7. The battery didn't function as a backup during the power outage as hoped.
reviews.title: We have 3 of these
reviews.author: Art

reviews.body: I replaced my older one which lad lasted 10 years. It still worked but felt like I could use a tech refresh, and I am super please with this one. The picture and sound are so much better, and it was very easy to setup.
reviews.author: IKE

description: Keep a watchful eye on your home with the Google Nest Cam Indoor/Outdoor Wire-Free Security Camera in stylish Snow. Model GA01317-US offers unmatched flexibility as it operates without wires, making installation a breeze in any location—indoors or outdoors. With its advanced technology, the camera differentiates between people, animals, and vehicles, ensuring you receive alerts that truly matter. Enjoy 24/7 live streaming capabilities directly through the Google Home app, allowing you to check-in anytime, from anywhere. If you miss a notification, revisit the action with 3 hours of free event video history. Equipped with a motion sensor and night vision features, this camera provides reliable monitoring, even in low-light conditions. Its battery-powered operation and wireless connectivity mean you can place it almost anywhere without the need for an outlet. The Nest Cam is compatible with Hey Google and Amazon Alexa, ensuring seamless smart home integration. Invest in security with the innovative and user-friendly Google Nest Cam today!

name: Nest Doorbell (Battery)
bestFor: Tall 3:4 aspect ratio video doorbell with 3-hour video history built-in

reviews.body:
The Google Nest battery doorbell looks great and has a clear video image. However, the maintenance issues are incredibly non-user friendly and counter-intuitive. First, if you change your wifi router, you have to disconnect the doorbell, return it to factory settings, and reinstall as-if-new (whereas the Google thermostat just has you re-enter the new wifi address).
Then there is the process to recharge. Instead of a removable battery, you have to take the doorbell off its wall mount, and this is difficult to do. Sometimes, when you pull on the bell housing it pulls the top of the bell off its base, which disconnects the small coupling wire. The only way to recharge is to disconnect the doorbell from the wall mount so you can access the small port on the underside of the doorbell. Why don't they have an external charging port? VERY FRUSTRATING AND TIME CONSUMING!
reviews.title: Complicated and NOT user friendly!
reviews.author: roggordon

reviews.body: This is a nice camera ( I got the green one but review says snow) . I know it’s a doorbell technically but I got it as an indoor camera as my cats kept on setting off my window burglar alarm by jumping against my window and setting it off . This always stressed me out as the security company would call saying there was a burglar attempt at my back window. I decided to get this camera to keep an eye on that window so I would know if it was an actual break in or just my cats ( this has happened twice). Yes there are actual indoor cameras , but this one is wireless, small , and matches the color of my walls and looks pretty . Plus I have other google devices, so was easy to set up. So far , best decision ever!
reviews.title: Nice !
reviews.author: Aleksandra

reviews.body: Battery life is comically short, lasted < 5 days in a city setting before needing to be recharged which is completely impractical. The consistent need to take the doorbell off to recharge, then reattach wore out the locking mechanism, which should be an easy replacement of a part worth cents but the product design is so poor there is no option to fix (a quick internet search shows many other users experience this issue). Google customer support is maybe the worst I've ever experienced and once out of the 12 month warranty just tell you to buy a new product. I'll never buy another piece of Google hardware again after this experience.
reviews.title: Terrible product & even worse customer support
reviews.author: user1372

reviews.body:
This is great doorbell. I originally bought the wired version, but I learned that the transformer connected to the originally doorbell in my house (really old building) didn’t supply enough voltage to operate the doorbell, which was a really big bummer. I wanted a system I could plug in and not worry about. Come to find out that the low voltage was enough to charge this battery powered doorbell when it wasn’t recording. While it can operate on a battery charge, it will charge if you connect the doorbell wires from the house. Meaning you don’t have to pull it off the wall if you don’t want to.

Install was straight forward, set up was mostly straight forward. I’ve leaned that google home product typically take 2 rounds of software set up for it to work correctly (go figure).

It is worth noting that I have a staircase that is perpendicular (90 degrees) to my front door and the included 15 degree wedge frames the stairs really well.

The good:
-Charges on low voltage transformers
-You can preview the recording from your phones Lock Screen
-After a few years the battery has held up really well

The bad:
- There is no additional external storage, meaning if you want any history from more than 2 hours ago you need to pay for the subscription
reviews.author: HomeDepotCustomer

reviews.body: I tried the Ring doorbell cam that closely resembles the product I'm reviewing now, and while it cost about half as much, it became utterly useless when there was no subscription attached to it. I want a product that still functions on a basic level without a subscription, which this device seems to. Everything else is great: solid construction quality, beautiful appearance, and a much longer battery than my old RIng cam.
reviews.title: Great doorbell cam!
reviews.author: Techjunkpile

reviews.body: After my Ring doorbell stopped connecting to my internet and I found out it was not compatible with 5Ghz WiFi, I had to figure out a replacement. I was disappointed with the fact that this happened so I did not want another Ring doorbell. I bought a different, cheaper brand doorbell off Amazon that claimed it was compatible with 5Ghz. After spending most of my day trying to install it and connect it to the internet, I returned it. I then bought this Google Nest and am I so glad I did! ITS AMAZING! It immediately connected to my WiFi and hasn’t lost connection since. Easy set up, clear video, easy to use. I hardwired mine but I’m also excited that should I need it to be just battery, that’s an option too. It connected easily to indoor mechanical chime (the one that was installed in the early 80s) which is an option if you want but not necessary. All in all, I am so happy I switched. Highly recommend!
reviews.title: The best doorbell
reviews.author: Ashley

reviews.body: Very satisfying with these cameras! Google nest is very user friendly and provide several great features to secure my home and make me feel safe. Camera set up is very easy simply plug and connect through the Google home app. The battery is also very good and can last up to a month or more depending on location and video sensitive
reviews.title: Great buy
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.body: The Nest camera is a really great cam for indoor/outdoor uses. Like the title implies, if you are new to the Nest/Google ecosystem, then you will be good. If you are already using older Nest cams and use the old Nest App, then you might run into some frustrations. The camera itself is built solidly. Feels like a premium device and has the performance to back it up. Magnet is super strong to hold it in many different angles. Inside the box you will find the cam, charging cable, mounting hardware (there is also an optional sold separately indoor stand you can buy) and the quick start guide. Video and Sound quality are great as with all of other Google's line of cameras. HDR and Video quality was always sharp, day or night to see what is going on. Sound sensitivity can be adjusted to record all things ranging from dog barks, insect activity to people/cars. Sound is loud and clear. After getting over the fact that I can't use the Nest App and started training myself to just use Google Home instead, I found myself not caring so much about it. It really does a nice job on what it is supposed to do. All in all, the Nest Cam is a great camera and worth it.
reviews.title: Great camera at a great value
reviews.author: Nelson M

reviews.body: I love my new Doorbell, really easy to install, no wire needed. The battery lasts like 3 months. The image is really great during the day and night time. Once the App is installed all the setup process was really simple. The only thing to keep in mind is that you also need to purchase a Google Nest speaker or the Google nest Hub, otherwise you will not be able to hear when someone is ringing as this doorbell is not wired.
reviews.title: Awesome camera

reviews.body:
The directions given for the Nest wireless video doorbell are not easy to follow when trying to install the device. It took me multiple attempts to be able to install it correctly and link it to our phones and to a Google Hub.
It keeps the videos for only 3 hours, not 3 hours of video as I mistakenly understood from the description. I did not need the wireless feature as I did a hard wire of the device. I had chosen this over the hard wired unit because of the 3 hour memory.
The doorbell does not chime on my phone, rather there is a sound just like any other notice I get on my phone for emails, messages, etc.
The motion sensor is not very good, if I set it to detect everything there are constant sound notifications on my phone. When I set it for people and package notifications it does not record many people who come and go. I have had people walk up got the door and not trigger the motion detector unless they ring the bell. There are times when it catches people walking along the sidewalk past the house, but, at other times, it totally misses people and or cars in the driveway. There are times when the wind sways some branches and that sets off the motion sensor.
Overall, I am not pleased with this device and would not recommend it to anyone, it falls far short of expectations.
reviews.title: Falls short of expectations
reviews.author: David

reviews.body: I have ring doorbells and decided to try the google video doorbell battery. The battery didn't stay charged for very long so I purchased an ac adapter so it could run on power rather than battery. That worked for awhile and then it quit working with the power chord. I did the same thing with Ring and zero issues. Google as been more work to get things right. For the money I think Ring is a far superior product! I am going to purchase another ac power adapter and try one more time .... but truthfully I am ready to take the google doorbell down!
reviews.title: Not impressed with Google's doorbell!

reviews.body: Alerts, video quality, notifications all top quality and very useful. Integrates with Google Hug and speakers like the Google Nest and the New Google Home Speaker. The only concern is the device can be easily stolen by a porch pirate! Suggest to try optional methods to help prevent theft of the item!
reviews.title: Excellent, but with one important concern!
reviews.author: anonymous

reviews.body:
We got this doorbell as soon as it was released. I wanted something easy to install & I didn’t want to mess around with wiring. Que this doorbell.
It was easy to install. It was more tricky setting up the family Google accounts so my husband & I both can view who’s at the door. Once we figured it out (we needed Gmail emails) it was smooth sailing.
Im looking at getting my parents one. The picture is great. Sound is clear. We can see down the street even. It alerts us if someone is there. I really like that you can change the doorbell sounds. Currently it’s a Halloween themed one. You can pay for a subscription to store the video footage. We opted not to for now. I don’t really see a need. It’s easy to save footage to your cell phone as well.
reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.author: Trixyt

reviews.body:
Was able to get mine early on launch day, IveWas able to get mine early on launch day, Ive had all the top brands Including Arlo, ring, eufy and more.
I love this gives you a horizontal view which I can see my packages if theyre laid on the ground or if my cat decides to go out, and want to come in.It comes with many types of an alerts, package, and pets are two of my favorite. The battery is great I haventIt comes with many types of an alerts, package, and pets are two of my favorite. The battery is great I have used it very much in the past few days.the design is just beautiful. This one definitely is a keeper Im notThis one definitely is a keeper Im not going to change again.The set up was extremely easy and theres nothing to do except screw it into the wall. And click it into place.I have a package bin outside, I can see it clearly Im extremely happy with it give it a try Im sure you will be too.
reviews.title: Tried them all,this is the best.
reviews.author: Sandy

reviews.body:
The Nest has a lot of great features, but a doorbell it is not. I was surprised at the difficulty in connecting an actual chime to the wireless version (I incorrectly assumed I could connect to Sonos or some wireless speaker). “Ringing” on the app works OK but makes the Nest useless if adults with phones aren’t home (or charging somewhere), or a guest is at the house. The chime on the Nest itself is so quiet I can’t even hear that in the adjacent room.

Further, the filters allow me to not alarm on motion or animals, but there is no “button” option to only alarm on someone pressing the actual doorbell button - so I get notifications every time a family member comes in or out. Finally, it doesn’t look like a doorbell button which means people don’t know to press it.

So far it has done everything but act as an actual doorbell for me.
reviews.title: Not a doorbell
reviews.author: TV Bob

reviews.body:
It gets the job done if you're looking for a camera to track packages. I like the function, which you can tailor notifications for packages, animals, people etc. Easy to install and tweak the settings.

However, it isn't the best for complete security monitoring. On maximized sensor which uses more battery, it fails to capture the entire shot. Also, the app and camera is slow at times when you truly want to see something instantly, in which laggy WiFi was not the issue.

With the free subscription only, it records snapshots of the last 3 hours; it is not continuous recording of the 3 hours. Don't expect to use it for middle-of-the-night recording. You could always buy a subscription, but I feel other doorbell cameras have better options with the free plan.
reviews.title: If you want a camera to only track your packages.
reviews.author: swng

reviews.body:
It does have a lot of plus points which others have already covered. I do like the third party integration support with my Brilliant Control Panel which allows the video to stream through when the doorbell is pressed. I wish it would do the same to my Sony A80J android TV (maybe it does; i still havent figured out how).

What you really need to know is that the doorbell is driven out of the battery even when it is wired *directly*. This is ok for most situations except Canadian winters. When the temperature drops below -15 deg C, the doorbell battery drains very fast. The wired connection is unable to charge the battery below -15 deg C. The battery would last you about a month. Be prepared to go out in the freezing winter and fiddle around with the tools to disconnect the doorbell and cables. You will have bring it in for charging every couple of weeks and it would of course not let you charge immediately because the device temperature is too low.

First time the battery drained on a wired doorbell in dec 2021, i thought it was an anomaly. But then it happened again in Jan 2022. i called Google customer care and they did the usual "oh it might be the settings which got corrupted.. do a factory reset". I followed their instructions and reconnected. Battery drained again in Feb 2022. Called them again. Same routine. I was suspicious of the product design. I asked them to confirm whether the battery was on a serial circuit path. No response. Just an offer to replace. I rejected that offer as what good would a replacement do if it had a product flaw.

Finally they did admit in the spring that their product had a problem in winter
https://support.google.com/googlenest/answer/11830989?hl=en
reviews.title: Great product but not for Canadian winter
reviews.author: DTK

reviews.body: I am happy with my doorbell. The only thing I wish that was different was the three hours of looking back on videos I had misunderstood when I bought this. I thought it would keep Three hours of time (Meaning that if you had a 30 second video now and a mini video later and another 30 second video all this would just add up to three hours before it would remove it) But I have come to understand that it means if you had a video at 12:30 and it’s now 4 o’clock at 12:30 video is not there. So that’s the only thing I’m disappointed with Yes, you can look at the video when it happens but if you happen to be busy and away from your phone and don’t get a chance to save something or whatever and most people do work at least an eight hour day. I thought it would keep the videos longer and for everybody to review the videos later in the day and delete them if they wanted So so far other than this misunderstanding On my part of the three hours It is working perfectly fine
reviews.title: Google doorbell
reviews.author: Erie Beach58

reviews.body: I purchased this on sale in store for an unbelievable price and I'm glad I got it. We needed something to deter solicitation and keep an eye on packages. The video quality is really clear and the audio is great. I'm using a third party door mount and the battery life is about 2 weeks. It fully charges in about 3 hours. I like that I can set it to recognize all activity or just people, animals, and packages. Animals in particular since we have skunks and I don't want to be surprised. Overall I'm please. I do wish it came with a separate chime and was more ios compatible but still, 4 stars easy.
reviews.title: Great find
reviews.author: JustNatalie

reviews.body: the camera is well made, great picture and technology. There is a problem with the mount. It will pop off, fall to the ground and shatter the lens. I bought mine 6/22/2022. within days the video captured the ups man leave and after, within a second it fell to the ground, broke lens. Easy returns, well no. I bought a 2 year warranty. I didn't drop and break it and it's new with a couple weeks so they denied coverage. if I had dropped it myself it would cover. so Googles warranty says return to the store, well that's a problem, 2 weeks abo I threw away the box..eventually it became easier to order another. so I did. I would recommend a strong exterior velcro set up...much safer. it does a wonderful job when working and blends with my set up
reviews.title: falls off of mounts
reviews.author: gmf479

reviews.body:
I have hundreds of pieces of smart home tech all centered around Google assistant and our various Google homes throughout our house. When our old Ring doorbell died, I was very excited to preorder and get the new Google Nest Doorbell Battery edition as soon as it came out. It was super easy to install and setup. It looked fantastic and we always got comments about how good it looked.

After two months though, the problems started.

Eventually, the retractable part that holds the doorbell to the base (so that you can remove it to charge it) stopped retracting. Luckily, Google Support was right on it and I got a new one in a few days.

The new one was just as easy to get setup. Unfortunately, in another month, I received the dreaded "Your doorbell is offline due to a battery issue. Please contact Google Support." I contacted Google Support and they helped me out right away.

I received the replacement in a few days and it was easy as can be to setup like before. This time, I received the "Your doorbell has a battery issue" message in 7 days... I called Google Support this time and they were not so helpful anymore. They drug things out for weeks and ultimately they said that there is nothing they can do because I am out of the support window.

This unit clearly has quality control issues. I am at a loss now. 5 months later and $200 spent - I have nothing to show for it. Never have been as disappointed with a smart home product as I have been with this one.
reviews.title: Promising but disappointing
reviews.author: James

reviews.body: ….the battery life is nowhere near what they suggest. Especially if you have a busy front door (kids in and out, traffic, etc.) but you can make adjustments to decrease battery wear. My biggest single complaint is the move to Google Home app for the access platform. Compared to the Nest app (which I loved) it is like returning to a DOS prompt. Simply too cumbersome and not intuitive. Come on Google you can do better than this. Bought the wireless indoor/outdoor camera as well. Love the look and lack of wires but same complaint - battery life in two days is noticeably draining and the Google Home app is NOT designed for security camera usage. Hope that improvements for both are on the way.
reviews.title: Wireless is a plus but…
reviews.author: SpiffyCaper

reviews.body: While the resolution may turn people off there are reasons to why this is the best solution for wirefree door bells. Resolutions beyond 2k takes too much bandwidth to transmit, especially using the 5Ghz band which is suitable for this much data it also has the weakest signal. The 1080p or 2k of 4:3 ratio taller does allow for a full view without optics to see packages. Although most doorbells are only for doors and not surveillance purposes the 4:3 ratio is quite sufficient to see who's at the door and see if a package is left. Unfortunately the reason for the 4 stars is the battery life when set to motion or any time the dour senses a presence. If set to identify people it will trigger the camera and notification hence using battery power. If set to push only then it's not so much an issue, being so large battery life should of been longer. The unit does perform better than expected and since having the very first gen skybell which was atrocious so having this doorbell as my second attempt at video doorbell I'm quite happy with the performance.
reviews.title: Great but with some short comings
reviews.author: Gary

reviews.body: This is my second smart doorbell, my first one is the nest doorbell wired. I really like this doorbell. It’s sleek and very modern unlike other offerings. The battery capabilities are a plus for sure, but if you live in an area like Canada or the northern US, the battery life will suffer. I wouldn’t recommend using this in -15 or below on battery ONLY as you’ll have to charge it nearly every week depending on the activity level. When wired, this thing is awesome. It wont 24/7 record, only 30 days event history which is a bummer but the event recording has been really reliable to capture a lot of things. One thing to note is that this doorbell has a very tall aspect ratio, which means if you want a wide view, you wont get it with this camera. If you want to make sure that you can capture people head to toe, this is for you. The only reason this gets 4 stars is the software. The google home app can be buggy with regards to viewing the camera history at some times. These cameras are pretty new and so is the interface in the app so there is plenty of time to fix the bugs.
reviews.title: Great hardware, software could use some work.
reviews.author: James

reviews.body: I installed my video doorbell. Mounting the doorbell on its mount was the problem. I thought I had it securely in place, but later found it on my porch pavers with the lens completely cracked. I got very little use out of this device before the break. It stayed on its mountain for two weeks and then I found it on the ground. If the camera lens had a little protection, I probably wouldn’t be out all that money, but the lens pokes out from the mounting, not recessed.
reviews.author: Katie

reviews.body: I was excited to link this new battery powered Google Nest doorbell to my existing Google Home. I have several Philips Hue lights, Chromecast devices, and 4 other Nest Cameras on the same Google Home location. I'm a pretty advanced user, and these Google product setups are usually a piece of cake since they're designed for anyone to easily set up on their own. Not the case here. The simplified set up was ultimately the reason it failed to set up. Every attempt to add the Doorbell to my Google Home network resulted in a "Can't connect to assisting device" message. I contacted Google support after an hour of troubleshooting. I tried uninstalling/re-installing the Google Home app, resetting my router, moving a Nest Cam device closer to the Doorbell, moving everything closer to the router, using a different smartphone, etc. Nothing worked. Google kept hand holding me like I must be the problem. No, the device software is the problem. It shouldn't be this hard, Google. Anyways, long story short I've returned the Doorbell. Hopefully they improve for the next generation so that there is an override for the "easy mode" set up, and I can enter in my WiFi details manually to avoid a silly troubleshooting dance.
reviews.title: Unable to set up, Google support was not helpful
reviews.author: Brent

reviews.body:
Don't buy this if you have cold winters and want to use it as a wired model - get the 2nd gen wired model instead. I bought it before the 2nd gen wired model came out, and I wish I hadn't.

I live in Vermont, and the battery will not charge below 32F, even if the doorbell is hard-wired in to keep it charged 24/7. Reddit is full of people from other northern states and Canada with the same complaint. Google advertises this as being able to work wired OR on battery, but if the battery is too cold to charge or the battery drops below 20% or so, it will stop responding to motion/faces/packages/cars/animals, etc. and all you can do is bring it inside to charge to get that functionality back. Even above freezing, wiring this device in only kept the battery around 30% or so. If most functionality stops around 20%, why keep it that low? Wiring this in is a a useless "option" with way too many drawbacks.

I couldn't be happier with the device's operation when powered properly, it just doesn't work as a wired doorbell in northern latitudes. I used it in a Homekit setup with the Starling hub, and it functions well. I'm also very happy with my 2nd gen wired model so far.
reviews.title: Don't buy if you're going to wire it in
reviews.author: Peter

reviews.body: I do like the quality and concept but the battery life and the zone setting is terrible even if you choose not to pick up people or cars etc...out of your zone... it stills notifies you of everything you dont want and drains the heck out of the battery. I literally charged it 100% yesterday and now it's 68%. It will not last 1 week. They should of at least made a detachable battery pack and swap it instead of putting it off line for hours to charge. Something so simple yet there's no practical use or thought put into engineering this. If your home has zero traffic than it's for you. But on a semi busy street it's a no go for this.
reviews.title: Terrible battery life for semi busy road.
reviews.author: Jay1392

reviews.body: Very easy integration with existing Google Home. Love being able to see live video on the Google Home display (but not history... that's only on the phone app for some reason). For some reason people don't seem to understand how to ring the doorbell. They are still rattling my screen door. And when they do ring the doorbell, half the time we don't get a notification. Battery has lasted about 2 weeks from fully charged. The unit is really large... maybe thats what is throwing everyone off. Video quality and sound are great.If I didn't use Google Home I probably would not go with this.
reviews.title: Works alright, good for Google Home users
reviews.author: Google Home user

reviews.body: We were hoping to hardwire this for faster response time, but because it's so much larger than a regular doorbell it wouldn't work with our siding. Instead, it's mounted to the doorframe and running on battery. The camera is good, clear pictures and never alerts us other than to people. The battery holds a charge for a long time, which is great. It also is easy to remove the unit from the mount to charge it. The main downside is that it takes so long to respond that people are gone before we can use the microphone. If it fit in the old doorbell's spot, and that made it quicker to respond, I'd give it 5 stars.
reviews.title: Does the job, just a little slower than expected.
reviews.author: Mrs V

description: Keep a vigilant eye on your front door with the linen Doorbell Battery (White) from Nest. This state-of-the-art, dual-band Wi-Fi doorbell is designed to ensure the utmost security and peace of mind. It can be powered by the included battery or can be connected to your existing doorbell wiring, providing a seamless integration into your home. The doorbell is capable of capturing high quality video with a resolution of 960 x 1280, making sure you don't miss any important detail. One of the key features of this device is its 145° diagonal field of view, ensuring a comprehensive coverage of your front door area. It is also equipped with a night vision of up to 10', allowing you to monitor your doorstep even in complete darkness. The doorbell is fitted with a mic and speaker that facilitates two-way communication with noise cancellation, so you can speak to your visitors from anywhere. Moreover, it also features a Passive Infrared (PIR) motion and proximity sensor that alerts you when someone is at your door. It is compatible with the Google Home app, making its operation simple and user-friendly. The doorbell also includes LED status indicators that provide you with real-time status updates. The device is designed to work with an 8 to 24 VAC; 10 VA Transformer, providing reliable performance and durability. One of the most user-friendly features of this doorbell is that it allows you to choose the areas you want to monitor the most. It follows the 802.11a/b/g/n Wi-Fi standards, ensuring a stable and fast wireless connection. The motion-activated alerts notify you instantly when any movement is detected, enhancing the security of your home. So, with the Nest linen Doorbell Battery, you can talk to who’s there, from anywhere and at any time.
