reviews.author: R.

reviews.body:
I mainly purchased this C1000 for use during power outages, to run the fridge, charge devices, and to power lights.
I also found that the C1000 will run my 1/2 hp. Sump pump and my 1/2 hp garage door opener.
So far I am very please with the functionality of this model. I am also impressed with Anker’s customer service. On two separate occasions within the first month I noticed two price change reductions. I contacted Anker each time and they honored the 30 day price guarantee and quickly refunded the difference, including tax.
In terms of build quality it is excellent, and feels durable.
I do, however, think the power cable is too short.
It did not turn on by pressing power switch initially, unlike my Ecoflow unit. A notation in the user guide would have been helpful to avoid some anxiety. Once I plugged it in it started the charging, unit came with 89% charge.
reviews.title: The C1000 is extremely versatile and a pleasure to use.
reviews.author: Anthony L.

reviews.body: I wanted to try this as a replacement for a gas generator I have that I just put our fridges on. This works amazingly. I’ve used this to be able to run my work from home desk and setup for about 3 days before needing to be charged again. The battery capacity is good and works well for my needs. The screen is grams and having the app allows you to see how much power things are using. I love how versatile this is to just be able to bring around the house to plug things in when I need to. I don’t have to run a long extension cord anymore for my fridge in the basement or run a loud and smelly old gas generator. These frequently go on sale and are a great grab for the 700 price point. You can use this for anything. I even was able to get a solar panel to charge this. While it does take a long time (somewhat because of the area I live in) it does work great with a 100w solar panel. If you don’t have a solar panel it can charge up to 1000w with the included cable, you can adjust that in the app. I keep it at 600w charging and it takes about 2h from dead to full which is great. I would buy this again or buy a larger one for my home in the future when I have the budget.
reviews.title: Great power generator
reviews.author: J.Y.

reviews.body: Works good nice to use it in the house instead of gas. The solar panels take a while to charge with direct sunlight “one 200 watt panel” can do 175 watts but any little obstruction cuts the charge down to 60-70 watts “shadow the size of your hand for example” it’s typically cloudy here in upstate NY but I get some charging by loading it in my car on the way to work 20 mins there 20 back I get about 6-8% charge back. I can hook this up to my tv a couple LED low watt lights , home theater “without subwoofer on” and it runs about 200-450 watts for about 4 hours. I enjoy it just wish the solar charging was faster and I know I could do that by acquiring more panels I just don’t want haul and setup that many in my yard. Maybe a more powerful inverter for the car would be better for me since it’s not always sunny here. Great product though
reviews.title: I like it but a 300-600 watt inverter for the car would be nice
reviews.author: A.j.

reviews.body: Anchor solix c1000 with 100 w solar panels. Quite a little powerhouse that will even run my air conditioner in my conversion van. It is silent when hooked up to the van and charging the battery or running appliances, which I really like that it is silent. It does make a little noise when charging from the house current. The 100 w solar panel takes too long to charge it. I got it up to 87 w and it still was very slow in charging so I am going to try another 100 w panel to see if it helps. Overall a great little unit and I am not bothering my camping neighbors with a generator noise.
reviews.title: Lightweight powerhouse
reviews.author: P.

reviews.body: The power station is small enough for me to carry and powerful enough for all the appliances we need to charge during a power outage. We feel more secure being able to recharge phones, fans, lights and other small emergency appliances without having to rely on others. The solar panels did come with a different set of cables than we expected from reading the manual. The cable that connects the power station to both ports on the solar panel is rather short, but it works.
reviews.title: Perfect size and power for what we need
reviews.author: L.M.

reviews.body:
-Anker C1000 - It is a trendsetter and will suit many due to its robust build, ease of portability with x4 AC sockets and host of other good features that tick all our boxes.
This should really come with a 'Quick start guide' - There is nothing in paper format. There are pages of Warranty paper waffle and safety sheet - The User App guide is very minimal and when paying £749 one expects better information with some hints and tips direct from the company rather than exuberant 'Red Setter' Youtubers pushing the product, who did not read / the minimal App User guide!
Apparently, you can also use this from WI-FI but precious little information anywhere about this, some vlogger says you can start it up and shut it down from anywhere in the world, but without any further explanation.
Additionally, there is very little explanation about the Powersurge - The US Version has a socket stamped with it, and the UK version has nothing. Is it inbuilt rather than using a dedicated socket as some users show on the US version?
A pity that Anker lays emphasis on the extra fast charge which is not good to frequently do and they should explain the best battery charge input rate which is adjustable via Bluetooth and recommend the best option.
It is important to recognise the capabilities of this excellent unit. We bought a campervan and can 'Top up' at the Anker C1000 at home or in sunlight via solar or an amenable inn power socket with their permission!
We will use it to act as an Outside Own 'Hook up' if necessary to run a fridge or run appliances from the Anker C 1000 sockets to use e.g. air fryer and microwave 800/ 900w and a 600w Travel type kettle with ease. These lower-wattage units negate excessive fan noise. There is a software update already in place to mitigate this. Lower wattage appliances will be better for the power bank, however, the Powersurge can take up to 1800w. that may rule out use via a UK kettle.
There is a long lead for DC charging and modern XT 60 connectors for adding solar panel(s) up to 600w. The kettle-type charging cable rather than a Power brick is also a good feature and you soon will be able to double the capacity with an additional battery. This Anker C1000 is also much smaller in dimensions and weight and can be an important consideration for us in purchase over other older, much heavier competitors - In our opinion this Anker C1000 power bank is now the 'Leader of this particular Pack' and deserves to do exceedingly well.
reviews.title: So far so good and this is almost 40% lighter than Bluetti AC 180 makes a huge difference in portability . No Paper Quick Start -App only USER GUIDE

reviews.body: I was looking for a power station that can help us survive some natural disaster, e.g. hurricane, or take for camping/picnic. I tried a smaller Anker 521, and EcoFlow River, but soon realized you need one that supports at least 1.5kw, since that's where a normal home 5-15 outlet max out, which means it should be able to support any normal home appliance. It turned out the C1000 fits those needs very well!The good:1. Great power/size&weight balance. At ~20lbs I can single-handedly carry it around the house with ease. that also means I can pair it with my electric leaf blower without worrying about the extension cords --- Another use case!2. App is quite useful. I like the turn-off timer feature, but I particularly like the fact it supports both bluetooth and wifi --- Bluetooth is extra helpful when you are in the wild.3: I like the light! Very thoughtful. I can imagine when you are out camping, it can not only help light up things, but it's also just bright enough so you can even write/read under and it's just at the height of a small table lamp.The ok:Fan noise -- Tons of people complain about the fan noise on reddit. Indeed the pitch sounds like a small jet engine but it's not that annoying. For the unit with such a small foot print I can understand Anker had to use small diameter fans which are inherently more noisy. In my test connect it to a 1.5kw space heater, and the noise level is very acceptable.I also wished the app can allow me to set a SoC limit. Even LFP batteries can take full charge, it still prefers 50% SoC for maximum battery life. Hope Anker can hear my voice and add that feature in the future.The bad:Really there is none.The interesting:Solar charging. I have tiny 18V/20w diy solar panel so I tried to trickle charge it since by Anker specs it should work. After connecting it via the supplied cable -- bingo! after a couple of clicks, it started reporting an 11w input power, and the input voltage dropped from 20V (voltage when open) to 15-16v ---- Great! that means it does have an built-in MPPT (max. power point tracking) controller! Good job Anker!But the problem is after a whole day, the SoC didn't change at all. I reached to Anker support, and not surprisingly they gave me the standard answer "oh you need a more powerful panel" So I decided to do my own investigation. By using a DC power supply, and emulated different voltage & amp configuration and found it seems the threshold is at about 13W --- under which it will simply not charge at all, but it is able to take the full charge power beyond. Indeed interesting.Conclusion:Why I give it 4 stars? I've only had the unit for 1 week, and will come back with an update after subjecting it to some real camping/picnic challenges. Hopefully, then I will update it to a 5.
reviews.author: X.T.

reviews.body: I've been using this daily for a few weeks and really enjoy it. It has done everything it says it will do and the build quality is solid.Two things to note are, first, the fan, which can be a bit noisy under heavy loads. This isn't an issue for me because I usually use it just to run my TV and few other small devices that together pull less than 200w, and at that level, the fan isn't too bad and only kicks on every so often. My heavier loads are mostly power tools which are loud enough that I don't care how much noise the fan makes. The second thing is the 600w solar input is a bit misleading because the max 60v/12.5a maximums makes it pretty hard to find a way to get the full amount. That said, I run two 200w panels in parallel that charge this thing up pretty quickly, so I don't really need to get the full 600w input.The 200w portable panel is well made and easy enough to position, though I just use it if I'm away from home because it's a bit of a pain to reposition, like most portable panels. In practice, it's about a 160w panel because that's all I can get while my regular 200w panels are pulling their full power in the same position.Overall, very impressed with this powerful little device.
reviews.author: C.W.

reviews.body: It's rare that I review items bought from Amazon, but because I am so pleased with this purchase, I had to share. I bought this not out of need, but because it was on sale with the 200w Portable Solar panels. Portables cost around $200 for 100w, so I thought this was a great deal. What SHOCKED me was that I was producing about the same Watts as my 400w Renogy on my roof. Simply by angling properly towards the sun, you can produce as much power as DOUBLE the wattage. Setup is a breeze once you get a hang of it and I consider this so much better than a roof setup. It would cost me less than half the cost of my Renogy system and roof rack if I bought another one of these. You can't compare your recharge power unless you have another system to compare it with and with this, I was able to do so. You don't need a controller or inverter. The Solix does it all. Some keen features is that it is Bluetooth smooth and the unit is light enough to toss around. To have the ability to plug in to recharge as you shower is a luxury you can't even imaging for a stationary solar system. If one person reads that this is the way to go for solar systems in your van or RV and acts on it, all this would have been worth it. My Renogy cost me $3,500 and two of these costs $1600.
reviews.author: T.

reviews.body: The items shipped very fast, got them 3 days after ordering. These work exactly as expected. In direct sunshine they panels produces about 145 watts of power out of a possible 200 watts. You will never see the max number but this charged the unit 33% in about 3 hours. It takes the better part of a day to do a full charge. The software works as expected and there is NO documentation. But I knew all that before I bought it and a dummy can make this work. It's so easy. So, no issues so far....In the picture uploaded here it is possible to see how it looks hooked up. The stands on the back are a little tough to set up because the whole array is awkward and these panel are actually pretty heavy. We had 20-30 mph gusts of wind, and they didn't budge or move at all. I am very happy, these will work great in sunny Arizona!Update:I did find a user guide online and I am successfully using the app on my Android phone. The documentation is not very robust but it at least gives some more information as does running the app.
reviews.title: Works as Expected
reviews.author: R.i.A.

reviews.body: I’ve only had this power station for a while, but it has already saved me from a long power outage that started from 9am to 3am the following day. I was able to use my 1500w kettle to heat up water for my coffee and 1500w microwave to heat up a TV dinner, power my internet router and landline phone all day, watch TV for a few hours, and charge my phone.WHAT I LIKED:-Can easily view remaining battery charge + input/output levels from the power station itself.-Has an easy to use app that allows to modify settings.-I was even able to use this as a UPS for my internet router when the power kept going off and on. My internet router switched to the power station without rebooting.-Although heavy, it is still light enough to move from one area to another without a problem.-Includes wall plug and solar panel plug (solar panel to be purchased separately).GOOD TO KNOW:-Can get a bit noisy when powering high wattage appliances.-Charge goes down quite fast when powering high wattage appliances like a microwave or kettle.
reviews.author: L.

reviews.body: I have 4 batteries in my bassboat. with an onboard 3 bank charger that's 10 amps per bank. I'm an hour away from my storage so I wanted to use that time to charge my batteries. So I tried The Anker C1000. When I put my boat back on trailer, after fishing for 6 hours on a windy day, I immediately hooked up the charger. I put my tackle away and wiped down the boat. Before I started back to my storage, I thought that i would check the state of charge of my batteries. To my surprise, three batteries were charged before I even left the ramp in less than an hour. And there was still 80% left in the battery pack. This will save me a lot of time. No need to lug around a generator.
reviews.title: For use charging my bassboat
reviews.author: A.

reviews.body:
I bought my first Anker Solix C1000 a few weeks ago. The second unit I bought about a week later, with an expansion battery pack. On the app it says Solix C1000X, although I bought the C1000. Not sure what the difference is, but they seem identical. I came across Anker Solix as I was researching for a good replacement uninterruptible power system (UPS) option for my network/audio/video "cabinet", which has high end network gear, PoE video security setup, as well as audio/video equipment. Works perfectly. So I bought a second unit with the expansion pack to have available for any critical power needs around the house in case of power outages or other outdoor needs. Works great as well. The battery pack is easy to connect and is seen in the app, with its own charge state and temperature readings. I set the unit timeout to never, just to see how it behaves. It has been sitting unused for almost two weeks now, with no power loss at all.
I have my units set to the lowest charging power (200W), especially when using as an always-plugged-in UPS since I don't need the unit to ultra-fast charge up again. No need to stress the batteries to charge quickly. Also, after some research, always being plugged in and charged to 100% doesn't seem to be as big an issue with LiFePo4 batteries as it is with typical Li-Ion. What I myself will be doing though is, a slow drain every so often, and let it run down to 60% or so. Then plug it back in to recharge with the slowest charging rate. I feel that this should keep the batteries healthy. But take that for what it's worth, and do your own research.. I definitely recommend Anker Solix.
reviews.title: Second time purchasing Anker Solix C1000 - this time with BP1000 expansion
reviews.author: J.

reviews.body:
So far, the Solix C1000 has been a good performer. There have been two firmware updates since my purchase and both went smoothly. The App appears to be pretty stable and provides enough simple information and control of the unit.
I like the fact that the C1000 is fairly lightweight and compact. It is easily transported in my vehicle or moved about the house.
I've used the unit to power chest freezers, portable floor fans, LED lights, charge phones, charge HAM radios, and run devices off of the 12V accessory (Cigarette lighter) port. All work fine.
I also have connected an aftermarket 200W solar panel to the unit and it charges just fine. No issues
As far as charging from AC, it charges rather quickly and as it gets near to full charge, the current draw automatically decreases. Personally, I would not suggest charging it every time using the Ultra fast charge setting in order to maintain actual battery life. No need to rush it.
reviews.title: Top Notch Gear
reviews.author: Michael S.

reviews.body: Update:After purchasing the solix C1000 and then partnering it with the BP1000, I have doubled the output watts I desire to power my northstar sc650 truck camper over a longer offgrid experience.Although I've not tested it on a multi day trip yet, but testing over several hours and running the things I normally would on shore power, I am extremely happy with what it can now power over extended periods of time.Literally running multiple items from our microwave, furnace, hot water heater, and more, when plugged into the surge pad socket with a 15 amp cord I am essentially runningeverything I need when I need it.The BP1000 discharges first and then will consume power from the C1000 and Vice-versa when charging the system back up.I believe that the system is setup this way so that the user will always have control over power charging and dischargingThe system does not have a pass through charge function but rather works like a UPS system in the sense that when plugged into shore power and backcharging, if power is needed to run something, the system will stop charging and immediately switch into ups mode and power what you need in the moment.Our plan is to use this system in campgrounds during quiet hours when gas generators cannot be used.Based on our particular wants & needs, I Would highly recommend.I wanted something small but that packed a high watt output when I need it.So far, so good. Boondocking in my northstar truck camper I am able to backpower the entire camper with the Solix C1000 for about a 24 hour period.This depends of course on what I am running. Occasional microwave oven use, my fridge on propane setting, lights, water pump, even the hot water heater and hot air furnace, again, limited high use items.Only used so far on 2 overnight trips.Next morning I use an 1800-2200 watt generator to power the anker back to full from about 15% only drawing a set watt charge of about 750. The generators rpm only increase a little bit and the anker is charged in about 1 hour and 30 minutes.I could increase my charge watts to 1000 and be done inside of 50 minutes or less but I want to break the unit in several charge cycles first and I like running my generator on eco mode.The anker is not heavy at only 28 lbs and I can set it up on my campers kitchen counter or just about anyplace else inside my rig.I bought it for $650 from amazon, anker Direct, and it shipped to my house in under 5 days and came in just under $700 total, a great buy in my opinion.I am looking to eventually buy the expansion battery to give more power in depth but am in no rush at this point.I am 100% satisfied with this small yet powerful unit. It definitely lives up to what it says it can do, also, the app is simply incredible.Great job to the folks at anker.Highly recommended, just do your homework on what you plan to use it for.I've been a goal zero fan for years but it's the older led acid yeti 400 and 1250 units.Great products and they still work great, I also have the ego nexus system and run 7.5 amp batteries on it, again, great units all around but this anker system takes the cake.Size, weight, power output, and charge times is what sold me!!Happy shopping.
reviews.author: D.S.

reviews.body: This provides enough power for most appliances (but not my Panasonic vacuum cleaner), with a great form factor, port options, and great design.There was a firmware update to v1.2.7 available out of the box, and the app required WiFi credentials before it would update. Not sure why it's required since other power stations can update with Bluetooth.Although the Anker SOLIX C1000 is compact, the cooling solution might its biggest weakness because it can be very noisy. It's easily audible when charging at 600W. After fully charging it, the fan also turns on in pass-through mode with a 600W load when it gets hot enough (79F ambient). At lower ambient temperatures of 74F, the fan doesn't turn on with the same 600W load. At high loads such as powering a 1400W water kettle, the C1000 sounds like a hair dryer.For emergency backup power the noise is probably not an issue, however this might be a problem for people in warm climates who want to use this as a supplemental UPS. Note the switchover time of the C1000 is too slow for sensitive electronics.
reviews.author: M.

reviews.body: We have experienced multiple severe storms, including Harvey, Uri, and Beryl. These experiences have taught us the importance of preparedness, focusing on essential supplies rather than luxuries. A diverse power supply is also crucial.For brief power outages, our primary needs are lighting, ventilation, and security. The Anker Solix C1000 UPS effectively meets these requirements, powering an LED light, pedestal fan, and Ring alarm base station. This eliminates the need for a gas generator in such instances.While the Solix C1000 can accommodate higher-wattage appliances, we prioritize energy conservation during outages. Given the unreliability of internet service during power disruptions, powering a home router is generally inefficient.For cooking, we rely on a single-burner propane stove. Our food storage strategy emphasizes non-perishable items such as dry goods and canned foods. We also maintain a supply of bottled water.To address extended power outages or localized heating/cooling needs, the Honda EU2200i generator is indispensable. By pre-positioning fuel in vehicles, we ensure a reliable power source for the gas generator or potential evacuation. We tested the Anker Solix C1000's ability to be charged from gas generator while simultaneously powering multiple devices. This enhances its utility.Due to the frequent inclement weather associated with power outages in our region, solar panels are not a power source in our emergency plan.Our vehicle, can transport the Anker Solix C1000 and Honda EU2200i for emergencies or camping.The mobile apps for both Anker C1000 and Honda EU2200i are fantastic to see how much is being generated by gas generator and how much is getting pumped/charged into Anker C1000 while how much is consumed out of Anker C1000.I would strongly recommend Anker Solix C1000 !
reviews.title: Anker Solix C1000 with Honda EU2200i for Outages
reviews.author: A.C.

reviews.body: Note (Original review for main unit at end - most recent (about expansion batteries) top).8/7/24: With everything automated I've had absolutely no complaints. For whatever reason power goes out at 7am now quite regularly for about 10-15 seconds - this battery keeps my office going like nothing happened. I continue to offload power during peak hours without even a thought (automated plugs scheduled to turn on/off). The Anker app continues to work amazingly. Couldn't ask for better. I rarely hear the fans unless it is charging (and even then it's not loud if you keep the charging around 400w).I did end up getting a C800 - just cuz I loved the 1000 so much. lol. I have it (acting as an UPS) for our ISP router and lamps in another room during peak hours - and it's a bit more mobile when I need power in places away from a plug. Also works nicely with the Anker App (both show up side by side).My little place is ready for the rain and storms this fall/winter! I am planning on using these batteries for their full lifespan or until something major comes out.6/3/24: Have had 0 problems with these batteries. Been using them almost every night to power my office from 4pm-9am. Excellent product - very happy with it. It's comforting knowing that I could power my place (fridge, internet, TV, computers) for at least 24 hours if we lose electricity again. Meanwhile, they function as power surge / protection and offload power to cheaper off hours (actually saving some money doing this - albeit very little but it's adding up every day). I bought some automated plugs that my phone turn on/off when it's 4pm-9am so I don't have to do anything to "offload" my power to cheaper times. LFP batteries are great - Anker is great. Hope y'all have a great 2024!4/14: Finally - Firmware Update Fixes External Battery IssueA few days ago Firmware 1.4.3 came out - looks like this has fixed the issue where when using the battery as an UPS and pull power for long periods of time then reconnect power - charging would refuse to happen unless one powered down/back up the external battery.Been using my C1000 + external battery now for awhile to power my office from 4pm - 9am (averaging 70% of the external battery to 100% of external battery). Been working great (got in the habit of manually pressing the external battery button to power it down/back on every morning - so it would charge at 9am - looks like I don't have to do any anymore). :DVery happy with these batteries! Got my power setup for years to come.3/10: Latest UpdateExternal battery still needs me to press the main button on/off for charging to happen almost every day (running on batteries all night, then smart switch turns power back on, the unit won't charge till I turn on/off the expansion battery via front button), which is a little frustrating but not a deal breaker since it's right next to me. I bought a set of 120mm silent fans to cool both units, they seem to keep the fans off for the most part while running on battery or UPS pass through power (internal fans always run when charging - but very low). Most of my usage is around 200w even during gaming nights. We'll see how it does in summer when my room gains 10-15F+.Been using this battery as an UPS offloading my entire office power from 4pm-9am with smart plugs. Very happy with it. Works well. Comforting knowing if we have another day or two power outage, I'll be able to keep everything running during then.3/3: Notes on Expansion Battery. Still Happy With Unit!Been using this device with a smart plug to automatically cut power at 4pm to 8am and for the most part it's been working flawlessly. Every few days it'll get in a weird super slow charging mode where it says remaining charge 4 days and never enter UPS mode (I use this as an UPS).Usually restarting the expansion battery works for it to "reset" and charge then enter UPS mode. Only a small inconvenience with the Expansion Battery (using it as an UPS).App is amazing. Batteries are amazing. Device works perfectly as a home office backup system. I plan on using this setup for a long time until a new battery technology comes out. Will report back if I ever get to use this thing in a long outage (powering the fridge, TV, other rooms).2/24: Expansion Battery QuirksNoticed some interesting behavior with the Expansion battery. If I plug the C1000 and the expansion battery into an outlet that fails to provide the power that the Anker C1000 is asking for, the entire thing goes into a weird passthrough mode and will refuse to charge (no matter how many times I plug/unplug from power) -- until I turn off the expansion battery and then turn it back on (lucky to figure this out). Initially I thought I broke it, but just turning off expansion battery (press holding expansion battery power button for a few seconds) and then back on returned charging to normal. I see how this has affected some other reviewers. Either removing the massive cable for a few seconds or pressing and holding the...
reviews.title: Amazing Power - UPS Mode - Great Utility (Update)
reviews.author: P.M.

reviews.body: I ordered the C1000 + 200W solar panel bundle, which seemed like a great deal. The gear arrived ahead of schedule. No damage, all good.But when I unpacked the solar panel it had a VERY strong mildew odor. It's noticeable ten feet away from the panel. There's no sign of mildew on the outside - it's coming from inside the panel assembly. This suggest some moisture was still present in the panel when it was packed. But the panel does work.My concern with this is mildew on the panel's internal electrical parts could lead to corrosion and eventually premature failure of the panel. So I opened a support ticket with Anker requesting a replacement panel. They sent a canned response asking me to supply information about the issue, including a video. I am not skilled enough to photograph a nasty smell so how am I supposed to supply that. Lol. Meanwhile Anker has not responded in any way except for the original canned email. They have been useless.Nothing I try seems to reduce or eliminate the mildew smell. So I guess since the panel works, I'm stuck with that.Seems to be a very good product except for the rank smell from the panel. Forget getting any assistance or even an explanation from Anker Support on an issue like that.The panel is sitting ten feet from me right now and I can smell mildew.EDIT: Anker Support did eventually reach out to me and offered to replace the panel. The replacement arrived 8 days after I returned the original one. The new panel seems to be a later revision of the one I returned.This one doesn't have even a hint of mildew smell. Yay.It's a partly cloudy day here with lots of full sun breaks. I'm getting a steady 180W of charging from the panel during sun breaks, with occasional peaks >200W. Angle & orientation are obviously very important to getting the best out of it so every half hour or so I adjust the position for optimal sun exposure.The panel is VERY sensitive to even the lightest cloud cover. Output falls seriously. But with full sun it delivers what is promised.The overall capacity of the unit is not sufficient to run anything that draws a lot of power for a long time. I'm thinking of a 2nd 200W panel and the expansion battery.The C1000(X) seems to be performing very well. No glitches to report. The app seems to work well too.I'm raising my rating from 3 stars to 4 stars because everything is working as promised. Just don't be overly optimistic about how long a package of this size can power your "everything". Charge your phone dozens of times? Yes. Run your computer, internet system, and maybe a couple appliances like say a TV? Runtime will be relatively limited.All in all I'm happy - got what I paid for.
reviews.title: Product seems very good, but be aware of its limitations
reviews.author: C.L.

description: Unmatched Power and Versatility The Anker SOLIX C1000 Portable Power Station redefines the way you think about energy solutions. With a powerful 1056. Wh capacity and a robust wattage of 1800W, this solar generator provides an endless supply of energy for all your needs. Whether you're camping in the great outdoors, hosting a garden party, or managing essential devices during a power outage, this unit can handle it all. Its AC/DC current type ensures compatibility with a wide range of devices, meaning you can charge your electronics, run small appliances, or power tools effortlessly. Thanks to the advanced Li. FePO4 battery technology setting new industry standards for safety and longevity, you'll enjoy reliable, durable performance without the worry of traditional battery risks.

name: HomePod (2nd Generation)
bestFor: Audiophile room-filling sound with integrated Matter hub, Thread router and temperature sensor

name: HomePod mini
bestFor: Compact Siri smart speaker & Thread border router for every room

reviews.body:
My HomePod Mini was great in the first year, love the awesome audio coming from this tiny little speaker. It really punches above its weight!
After the first year, I've been having trouble with firmware updates. Automatic "updates" fails 3/5 times and failed update requires the unit to be unplugged and replugged before it works again.
This is very concerning as my HomeKit depends on this HomePod Mini to control all my HomeKit devices! I disabled auto-update to prevent bricking the HomePod Mini with regular updates and only update when it's essential. Unfortunately even updating just once every few month is too much for it to handle.
My HomePod Mini bricked 3 times during firmware updates and the unlucky 4th time, it died for real and won't even respond to hardware reset or plug in USB-C repair.

After doing some search online, ALOT of users experience the same issue where the HomePod Mini bricks itself during firmware updates. Repairers identified the cause : the HomePod Mini hardware not being able to handle the increased processing and power required during 'larger' firmware updates and it blows the components inside. My HomePod Mini requires a mainboard swap / intricate capacity replacement before it will function again.
Therefore... it's an expensive ornament now that the warranty period has just passed.

If you own a HomePod Mini, I would reframe from updates if your device is the main unit controlling your HomeKit devices.
If you are thinking of purchasing a HomePod Mini, I would recommend holding off and wait for a 2nd gen unit. Fingers crossed that Apple has figured it out and decide not to cheap-out on components.
reviews.author: BruceL52

reviews.body:
I picked up a grey Apple HomePod Mini from CEX recently and I have been seriously impressed! The sound quality is incredible for such a small speaker, clear, rich, and with a deep bass that really fills the room. I have paired it with my Apple TV and together they create a brilliant, seamless Apple experience that makes watching films and shows even better.

The one I bought was rated as B quality, but honestly, it looks and feels brand new. I was really surprised by how good the condition was. I have also been using AirPlay from my iPhone to stream music from anywhere in the house, which works flawlessly. On top of that, Siri has been really handy for turning on my lights and setting shortcuts, making everything super convenient.

I honestly did not expect to enjoy it this much, but I am hooked now. I am definitely planning to buy a few more and have them in every room.
reviews.title: Not all about the bass but.....!
reviews.author: Wussaki 25

reviews.body:
The sound of this tiny device is amazing however after a couple of weeks it has stopped streaming Apple Music playlists or radio via Siri. To stream from Apple Music you will have to manually select the device in the airplay/bluetooth devices list. A little annoying but it's still worth the money. You just can't use Siri with it. I couldn't find any help online regarding that issue.

The HomePod mini is a super sounding product and is easy to use via airplay and bluetooth. It's good value for money and is well made. I can certainly recommend it (I have three in my house).
reviews.title: Great sound and well made product
reviews.author: Ralph

reviews.body:
I've bought cheap speakers in the past, so I can listen to radio channels and podcasts when I go to bed. Unfortunately they started intermittent 'beeping,' which I could not resolve, despite keeping them fully charged, etc.
I looked at the Apple speaker online, and found one at a good price. So far it is doing everything I wanted it for; and with a few extras I hadn't considered. The 3 months free subscription to Apple Music lets me play tunes I haven't heard in years; so now I want to move it from the bedroom to my "exercise" room(!)
I'm happy with the sound quality and the unobtrusive look of the speaker. I'm very happy with it so far.
reviews.title: Great Little Speaker
reviews.author: Anonymous

reviews.body: I purchased two HomePod minis in the Blue colour as the Blue really stood out to me the most. In the image above, you can see my two Blue HomePod minis paired with my Apple TV 4K and placed on both sides of my TV stand. The main reason of purchasing these was for the stereo pairing functionality, which I have to say, the stereo pairing of the HomePod minis is incredible for a small room like my home office. Compared to my TV's own speakers, I'd say the audio quality of the HomePod minis is significantly better. The difference is almost night and day with the TV speakers sounding more hollow and echoing, and HomePod minis having more balanced sound. Plus, what I love about the stereo pairing of the HomePod minis is it truly immerses you into whatever kind of content you're watching. Thus, the HomePod minis really complement an Apple TV 4K. Plus, with a setup like this, you're bound to get the best experience whenever you watch a show or movie because you're getting the best picture quality with the Apple TV 4K, and the best audio quality with two stereo paired HomePod minis.
reviews.title: Best speakers that complement an Apple TV 4K!!!
reviews.author: Danysch

reviews.body:
Some intermittent issues with internet connection if I change my wifi settings, seems to resolve after rebooting and waiting maybe 10 minutes.

Quality is good for certain types of music but not so much for heavy bass like EDM or metal. Might be better if pairing with a second.

I use mine for on low volume for mood music that turns on/ off automatically when I leave or come home (the automation is the best feature in my opinion).

Have also setup for smoke alarm detection.

Considering sound quality and internet connection hiccups, but with the cheap price, would prob give 3.5 stars but rounding down to 3 as this site doesn’t allow half stars. Can’t quite justify a 4.
reviews.title: Pretty good, 3.5 stars if site allowed half stars

reviews.body: I love this - small but has good bass, crisp and clear sound, and good volume control so you can get just the tier you want. Paired it to my iPad Mini 6th gen in seconds. I love that it's always 'on' but waiting, so it only connects when I open Music. I found also that if it doesn't support the app you want to airplay to, then on my iPad I swipe down from the top right to get the 'share' icon, then tap that. I can now stream HK radio through the app on my iPad, but it comes out of the HomePod Mini. Perfect.
reviews.title: Small but powerful, easy to set up
reviews.author: mardybob

reviews.body:
Having moved to a cottage that doesn’t really lend itself to hi-fi separates and the accompanying mass of shelves and storage for CDs and vinyls, I’ve been looking for some time for a decent sounding small speaker for streaming. The HomePod Mini is just that. It has a great range of bass and treble and barely noticeable on the shelf. I would highly recommend the purchase of two speakers (as I did) for stereo sound though as this vastly improves the overall experience. I’m very impressed with the overall sound quality.

However, listeners of BBC Radio can only use it/them through their iPhone (through the BBC Sounds app), whereas before we could ask our previous smart speaker to play 6music, Radio 5Live (or whatever) this now has to be done through our iPhones whilst nearby to the speakers. Also, the HomePods are naturally geared towards the Apple setup, so I’ve ditched the other music streaming service and signed up to Apple Music. No bad thing as the stream quality is far superior.

So, all in all, I’m very happy with the sound quality and the functionality but a little surprised that it doesn’t have the range of services (ie, radio) of other smart speakers.

Still, I highly recommend this product.
reviews.title: Great speaker for the low/mid level hi-fi convert
reviews.author: Henry24

reviews.body:
It is great for playing Apple Music, many radio stations and for streaming. Easy to set up and to operate the voice activated system.
The sound quality is superb for such a small device. The only drawback is that it doesn't work with BBC Sounds except in streaming mode, which is disappointing though I understand this a BBC problem rather than an Apple issue.
reviews.title: A really excellent product
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.body: The Apple HomePod mini has ended up being a surprisingly satisfying little speaker to live with: compact, unobtrusive, and far more capable than its size suggests. The sound is warm and full with impressive bass weight for such a small enclosure, and after enabling the “Reduce Bass” setting it became much more balanced for podcasts and everyday listening.
reviews.title: Set and forget smart audio
reviews.author: captaineos

reviews.body: I like this but I don’t love it. It was very easy to set up, just pair with iPhone and it’s done however, it doesn’t respond like a smart speaker with requests like “Siri play bbc radio 1” The home pod doesn’t do this. You have to go into the bbc sounds app to choose your station then pair with the home pod, which for me is a pain as I’m used to asking Alexa to play anything. So for me only 3 stars as far as “ smart speakers” go. Otherwise, it has great sound and is very easy to set up.
reviews.title: Like but don’t love
reviews.author: Sam 15

reviews.body:
I was given a gift card for my birthday and I had an idea of what I wanted to buy.
I already have two Amazon echo dots in various parts of the house and they are great.
I also have apple products which include a Mac, IPad, IPhone and and Apple smart watch and I thought it would be really good to buy an Apple HomePod so they can all be synced.
I spoke to an assistant in the store and I asked two questions which would decide whether or not to buy the device.
Firstly I asked does it do exactly what the echo dot does, the answer was yes.
My second question was is there a subscription or any other costs relating to this product, the answer was no.
I got home set up the device and my first instruction was to play Radio 4, the answer I got back was I can't find it the Apple Music library.
I then gave another 6-8 instructions and each time I got the same reply.
If I had realised that I would need to subscribe £10.99 per month I would never have bought the product.
I feel let down buy John Lewis as I had asked a specific question about additional costs or outlays and was told there weren't any, I think some additional staff training may be required.
reviews.title: Oh the disappointment!
reviews.author: David

reviews.body: I bought two of these to add to the one we have already set up, love them, they are so easy to set up and use and are responsive. We can even listen to different music in different rooms for all the family's enjoyment. The sound is great and can be controlled via Iphone or handsfree and even has a intercom feature to connect to other rooms/speakers.
reviews.title: Great. We love ours
reviews.author: Jodi8

reviews.body:
If you have an Apple ecosystem this fits in very well. Conveniently small with reasonable sound and easily controlled with Siri. I have a few of these mixed with Bose Soundbars to distribute music throughout the house.

If you’re looking for the absolutely best sound this is not the way to go. If you can tolerate’reasonable’ at a low price this might be your answer. Because these are not battery-powered the are less portable than their small size might imply. There is, however, at least one third-party battery adaptation which works well.

Not perfection but reasonable function and price.
reviews.title: Tiny Speaker - Reasonable Function and Price
reviews.author: Douglas

reviews.body: Absolutely amazing. My echo speakers have been acting up. I use them to control my smart home by voice, and many other things. I have a HUGE investment in echo speakers from multiple studio speakers to echo 2 and echo 3 speakers to echo dot (multiple gens) and echo auto in three cars. They have absolutely failed at all things mart home in the last couple years. Given that everything I have is HomeKit enabled or HomeKit accessible through my smart home hub, and I have been using Siri in my phone anyways to work around Alexa I decided to buy to of these — for my Office and Bedroom. I’m sold. I will be replacing all my speakers with HomePods now. If you’re on the fence, and you have Apple TV, or HomeKit enabled TVs and iPhones, this is a huge recommendation. Siri never messes up and has direct integration with my calendar, todo lists and other iCloud services. I can use it as a conference speaker for my iMac when in zoom calls, Ior as a speaker for my Apple TV. Way more versatile than Alexa.
reviews.title: Exceptional smart speaker — replaced others with these

reviews.body:
Okay, so it takes between 1 - 2 minutes at some stages to develop a formidable connection.

This can be a huge hassle, should you be in a rush or perhaps if you're using this item to create atmosphere in the workplace? I would highly suggest not purchasing this item - should you be looking for consistency, effortless connection and a stress free experience. Think twice about this purchase making your life MORE comfortable.

I would not suggest this item to anyone. An "old fashioned" connection requires a once-off functional connection and then proceeds to play seamlessly.

This item can be activated by "voice control", similar to Siri/Alexa, however, repeats back to you ever so eloquently that it cannot understand and is unable to complete a basic request, should it be struggling to develop a formidable connection.

This is a gesture that can almost be described as petty by the individual attempting to enjoy the device or even using the device in a professional capacity. I would suggest, so as to remain stress-free while entertaining and even when creating an atmosphere in a professional environment, to perhaps choose a device with a wire you can plug into your device. OR a more traditional wireless connection like a classic old fashioned speaker that connects using the basic bluetooth function.

Waste of time? Yes, 100%. The speaker sound quality is certainly not superior. There are many other brands out there.

If you aren't willing to sacrifice an unpredictable amount of time each occasion you would like to play something - do not purchase this product.

If I bought this speaker for my mom? For Christmas. I'd have to stay home all year to help her work the thing. Unlike the traditional Bluetooth connection which requires a moment of patience while developing a connection at the beginning of the day/music session.

This device requires continuous patience.

I would urge a group of participants to record the time it takes to get the device to function each time and then work out what your hourly rate is? Try these two things mutually exclusively, obviously, unlike the Siri/Alexa feature, we can distinguish between two tasks, and even two people, and we can even record the time it takes us to do things?

If you're spending too much money on this item for the next few years after you buy it, you can always try a little less harder to keep up with the latest in undeveloped technology and maybe see if the UX Design team or the Engineers need a donation for an online school or a University/College?

You can help everyday people like Tom or Harry for example to improve their skills and abilities.

My neighborhood, the brick and mortar neighborhood that is. We had a civil engineer commit suicide after failing to complete a project and not meeting basic user requirements? This was allegedly prompted by shame.

While I am sure the HR team can support every single one of their employees.

I can't - I will definitely opt for supporting an Engineering and Design team that keeps user experience at the centre of their work.
reviews.title: Its a no from me - you should be benched for a season and come back when you're fit maybe?
reviews.author: Ruby

reviews.body: I bought two of these and WOW the sound quality is clean and loud! I asynced them to my existing larger Apple HomePod to create a stereo sound system for my TV and I am very satisfied with how they’re working! They’re easy to set up, to control and very convenient for those with an all-Apple ecosystem in their homes.
reviews.title: Small but mighty!
reviews.author: Andres

reviews.body: I've loved every second of using this Apple speaker. It is the best speaker I've had since JBL. I absolutely love it with everything I have! The sound is immaculate. The size always is able to go into spots we use normally and daily. The Ease Of Use of it is also the best like it's not too hard to control and it's not too much to handle. I've used this thing in four different bedrooms already and my favorite spot is my bed room i’ve loved every second of using this Apple speaker. It is the best speaker I’ve had since JBL. I absolutely love it with everything I have! The sound is immaculate. The size always is able to go into spots we use normally and daily. The Ease Of Use of it is also the best like it’s not too hard to control and it’s not too much to handle. I’ve used this thing in four different bedrooms already and my favorite spot is my bedroom but I would like three more for the others but I would like three more for the others.
reviews.title: BEST THING EVER
reviews.author: Ayden

reviews.body:
Fast review:
Pros: Great sound no complaints, iPhone Home app can play music when you come home which is nice, subjectively cool design with top display

Cons: Siri is god awful and only useful for asking the time and weather, don’t ask Siri any hard questions because she won’t tell you anything without having to, “open your iPhone” because she, “found results on the web” that she won’t tell you out loud because she can’t read simple articles. Good luck trying to use Siri on your iPhone if the HomePod is near because Siri defaults to HomePod so you can’t even ask questions on iPhone without the HomePod defaulting to Siri and you can’t answer questions on the iPhone because she keeps interfering with the iPhone Siri and won’t even give any answers.
reviews.title: Great with Home App on iPhone, Siri still sucks
reviews.author: Ryan

reviews.body: Apple products just work seamlessly with other Apple devices. After having the Alexa devices across the home for a few years , I completed the switch to these Apple HomePods . So pleased that I did they work perfectly with our other iPhones and iPads. Our daughter finds them easy to use. It has lots of handy features such as intercom, temperature as well as the ability to link them and unlink them easily to play music.
reviews.title: A great Apple product
reviews.author: Darrendgw

reviews.body: I purchased a white HomePod mini, I’m pretty text savvy and I know how to work Apple products. When it came to setting my product up with the home app, it kept giving me error messages and telling me to try again. The only thing I was able to do was play music via my phone through the speaker. I could not get it to work with my matter enabled lights. I went with a goggle home display, same price, with a screen.
reviews.title: Connectivity Issues
reviews.author: Noah

reviews.body: Have fallen down the rabbit hole of updating all my smart speakers to Apple. So far from CEX I have purchased a Blue, Yellow, White and now Orange Homepod Mini. Grade A and it arrived really well packaged and in its original box. Indistinguishable from new. Took only a couple of minutes to setup and as with all the others I have purchased it looks great and sounds amazing. Seemless integration with Apple music and a room filling sound that belies its mini size. Highly recommended!
reviews.title: A lovely musical orange!
reviews.author: JerryAtrik

reviews.body: great sound , easy to use. once i got it that this is a home pod, not an ipod, it was easy. i wanted it play my apple itunes catalog, i set up with download. then, selected a song from playlist and it instantly started the playlist when i clicked the airplay symbol on the song. wonderful, huge , deep and clear sound i hear all over average size condo. in fact i have to turn it down. amazing. it has a complete suri home whatever set up but i am not much interested in asking suri the weather or room temp etc.
reviews.title: great
reviews.author: cass c

reviews.body:
I bought two of these to work as a stereo pair in my study. In the interim I have set them up in my lounge as a test. This is three times the size of the study. I am listening to Apple Radio on its classical station and the sound is very good especially as most tracks on Apple are now lossless. I've got the pair working at 40% volume and the sound can hold its own in a large lounge. If you crank them up further they don't distort unlike cheap Bluetooth speakers. Gives the better Bose models a run for their money at half the price. Cleaner sound than the basic Sonos too.
Pros - very small, well made, cute, large and effective stereo soundstage when set up as a pair, now available in several colours, high quality sound compared to the competition.
Cons - non if you use the Apple ecosystem, you do need mains power. Some of the comments on this site are almost certainly people thinking such a high sound volume can be generated from plugging into iMacs etc. there is definitely not enough current to do this. Hence each pod gets a 20w Apple plug. It's physics....
Recommended for Apple folk. Better sound quality than all but HiRes Bluetooth. Apple lossless is at least CD quality.
Photo shows the scale against the MA radius 90 mini reference speakers. Visitors think it's them playing. With their REL subs, and a top end hifi amp the MAs are 15x the price but maybe 2x the sound quality which says a lot. Clearly sub bass cannot compete with a 170w a channel set up with two subs but it's still pretty good. If Apple brought out a matching sub it would be a superb lifestyle set up.
Still great for normal volume classical music as is.
reviews.title: Great Sound For its Size
reviews.author: Andy C

reviews.body:
I bought the minis and the big ones

Garbage and would never recommend
reviews.title: Absolutely garbage sound
reviews.author: Dontech

reviews.body: I bought 2 - one for the kitchen, the other for my bedroom. I was able to connect the HomePods to all my Apple devices easily. I use it mainly to listen music & audiobooks, and ask for cooking measurement conversions endlessly (among a bunch of other things). The sound is better than I thought it would be - considering how small it is. A bit pricey compared to Google Nest and Alexa, but I like the idea that the HomePods are Apple and seamlessly integrates with my other Apple devices. I’ll definitely get more for the other rooms in my home.
reviews.title: Great product
reviews.author: AmaliaD

reviews.body: After over a year of using this I can confidently say that it's about as useful as a 2010 Bluetooth speaker. Siri is not as good on this device as it is on my phone, it can't do half the stuff you would expect it to do and it's useless unless it has access to your phone. It also can't understand instructions. "Play my x song" comes out with some other random song that has a completely different title in a completely different genre. Ask it a question and it says "I can't answer that" even though the phone version can. What's worse it I'll be asking my phone and it decides I'm asking it. Only purchase I've ever regretted from Apple (and I have them all).
reviews.title: Biggest waste of money ever
reviews.author: Usually a fan

reviews.body: Product quality as you would expect from Apple is very good.Price is a little high would sell more units if better priced against competitors. Integration with my other Apple products is good, Siri as everybody knows is not the best compared to amazon and google, one area apple need to work on. Sound is ok for a little speaker I have paired it up with another to get a stereo pair and sounds a lot better. Set up with the home app is very straight forward.
reviews.title: Review of APPLE HomePod Mini Smart Speaker with Siri - White
reviews.author: Reviewed by Currys customer

reviews.body: The HomePod mini was easy to set up. The sound is quite pleasant and soothing but cannot play as loud as the JBL Charge6 speaker if you want to throw a party. The bass from the later is also deeper and tighter. The JBL Charge6 can play using its battery while the HomePod mini needs to be connected to an outlet via the USB cable that comes with it, thus the latter is not portable.
reviews.title: Nice sound but ...

reviews.body:
Good Points: It’s very compact with a clean minimalist design. The sound quality is very good considering how small it is. Definitely better than the small albeit cheaper offerings from Google & Amazon. You really need to already be in the Apple ecosystem at least with an iPhone for it to be suitable. Although it’s not as loud as it’s big brother original Homepod it doesn’t have a great big bass driver and I prefer the less bass heavy sound. It’s also good that you can pair and interconnect these speakers in your house and I like the facility that music playing on your iPhone can be seamlessly transferred to the Homepod Mini just by holding the phone above it.

Improvement Points: A bit more cross platform compatibility would be good. Siri although improved with the ability on this device to set multiple timers is nevertheless a bit dim compared with Google & Alexa and needs further improvement. A rechargeable wireless water proof version would be good as well. Although this one is a lot cheaper and better value than the big version it’s probably just a little expensive for some who are primarily interested in the smart speaker side of things and aren’t too bothered about audio quality. For me it’s the sweet spot though.
reviews.title: Review of APPLE HomePod Mini Smart Speaker with Siri - White
reviews.author: Reviewed by Currys customer
