specifications.name: Output Level (SPL)
specifications.value: Two to three times less than Sub (Gen 3)

specifications.name: Audio Configuration
specifications.value: 5.1 system (with Sonos Beam and two Sonos One speakers)

reviews.body: It is my first subwoofer. When you set it up with trueplay it almost becomes imperceptibly quiet as Sonos tries to prevent boominess and reverb. The subwoofer can be felt and heard at volume above 40%. It sounds very clean and tight after trueplay tuning. A change in the EQ of +8 to the bass and increasing sub audio volume by +1 makes the subwoofer come on much sooner, it fills and complements the music much more noticeably even at lower volumes and it never sounds distorted or loose. I don’t dare turn it up louder than 60% volume but it is definitely a very capable unit. Without trueplay the sub woofer placed in the corner (as per Sonos suggestion) sounds very boomy, loud and inelegant but this is not because it’s a bad sub it’s just the physics of how sound travels, bounces and the acoustic property of my room. Ceiling speaker world has been an excellent business to deal with as well. Thank you [****] and Ceiling speaker world!
reviews.title: Great sub.
reviews.author: Neshoan M.

reviews.body: Bought the Sonos sub mini to supplement the Beam and a pair of Era100’s. Although called a mini it is larger than you may think. That said it complements the system really well with lower bass notes and an added richer sound. Films are great as is music. Why not 5*? Because I tried to connect the sub mini to the system using Bluetooth and failed. Tried factory reset a number of times and also initially connected by Ethernet and then when disconnected (as advised on Sonos web site). Would initially connected and then dropped out. In the end connected sub to an internet booster via an Ethernet cable. I’ve heard of quite a few people having the same issue with the sub. Apart from that pleased with purchase.
reviews.title: Very good, but …….

reviews.body: Research done i decided to get the Mini Sub to enhance the Sonos Beam for my smaller family room system. When first plugged in i thought i had made a mistake the bass sounded boomy and a little out of sync with the Beam, did not sound good at all. So i decided to run the Truplay option on the Sonos app then everything changed now the Sub Mini sounds super smooth and blends in perfectly with the Beam. As other people have observed because the Beam doesn't need to do the heavy lifting now of suppying the bass it sounds even better now, more open more spacious and three dimensional. I have a full theatre room in the basement with large speakers and a 110 inch projection screen so i know what a good sound system can produce but i am so very impressed with what the little Beam and Sub sound like, gives me the movie sound experience when i'm not in my theatre room. Will add two Sonos Era 300 speakers for the rear surrounds when the budget allows.
reviews.title: Add on Sub.
reviews.author: Sam D

reviews.body: How such a deep, rich sound can come out of a small, round rather odd looking speaker is surprising but rewarding. Coupled with the Sonos Beam Gen 2, the system is great for music, movies or watching tv. The setup is seem less and quick. The mini didn't really come alive until after I had the opportunity to conduct the True Play tuning session and find some suitable music but the difference was immediately noticeable and impressive! Yes, it does vibrate the floor but in a good way and always produces clean, clear bass which works well in conjunction with the Beam Gen 2. Now if Sonos will just keep working on the squirrelly app!
reviews.title: As good as advertised!
reviews.author: RonL

reviews.body:
..if you already own a Sonos Beam - do not hesitate - press the buy button Now!

Paired with the Beam this brings a more cinematic experience to your living room, it leaves the Beam to handle the mid and highs whilst the Sub Mini handles the low ends - it really opens up the sound

I tested it straight away by watching Dune, turning the Sub Mini off and back on, my god you can hear it punch out those sound effects and music and in a good way too, it's very tight and controlled, like good HiFi that presents a nice soundstage, not some cheap flappy bass that makes your doors rattle

Lastly - form factor - it looks good, modern sculpture like and it fits in well with my modern decor

9/10 from me
reviews.title: A must buy..
reviews.author: SkyFlyer

reviews.body: I put off buying the mini sub for over a year, as you can't find specifications on the unit itself. After eventually purchasing one I am now in a place where I'm constantly asking why I didn't purchase it earlier. The sub mini delivers more than enough bass, my neighbours have complained about their windows rattling on a Saturday morning spring clean. Once the unit is fine tuned. The window rattling goes away and clean undistorted bass fills your music and movie needs. This unit has turned movie night into THEATRE night. Don't waste your time if you're thinking of one buy one. I have the unit in a 4x9 metre room and it performs really well.
reviews.title: Packs a punch
reviews.author: Cypher

reviews.body: I purchased an Arc Ultra and wanted to add more base to my system. I live in a one bedroom apartment and didn't have the space for a Sub4 + I wanted to stick to a budget limit. After reading several reviews I decided to try the Sub mini even though many advised against it. I have no regrets. The Sub Mini has made my system sound complete and the amount of base it brings is perfect for my space. I did have an issue setting it up but the steps to resolve it were easy to follow. The delivery experience was outstanding. 4 weeks in and it's love!
reviews.title: Works amazing with my Arc Ultra
reviews.author: Robbie80

reviews.body:
I am an old school, big powerhead, big speaker and subwoofer type guy… That said I was looking for a surround sound system. That would work well for both movies and music. Space is limited so I went with the beam and mini sub.
By themselves they are very good, but I would recommend adding the Era 100 speakers to complete the system.
The minisub provides all the bottom you need to make this a great sounding compact, wireless and Alexa or other virtual assistant, friendly!
I definitely recommend it. Sonos is awesome!
reviews.title: I’m a believer!
reviews.author: Rich

reviews.body:
The final piece of our entertainment 5.1 setup and its made the most difference, not only has the Sub Mini added the extra thunderous deep punchy bass, but its transformed how the Arc and One surrounds also perform too, so mach clarity, mids and bass hitting you from every direction.

When its party time I love that we can move the Sub Mini to pair with our Five Stereo pair, now thats a totally different level of sound on its own.

Our living room is fairly large 12x25ft and the Sub Mini fills it and then-some, couldn't imagine what the full size sub would sound like but the Sub Mini is more than enough for us.
reviews.title: Outstanding
reviews.author: RAW

reviews.body: This is a Christmas gift for the family, however, I have already setup, connected to SONOS Beam. It is amazing product, design is simple and elegant in black color, also very solid, but the matt finish has some disadvantage as well, due to fingerprints and dust collection. A far as it clean which supposed to be, it is really nice product. The sound quality is brilliant, but still I do not have enough experience due to fact, that I just make a fast setup. Let see after Christmas. The wall mounting set would be really appreciated, this was really missing to me.
reviews.title: Nice and good Sub :)
reviews.author: Robert

reviews.body:
I bought the Sonos sub Mini from Crate & Barrel about a month ago, and it’s been a total game-changer for our home entertainment setup. Despite its compact size, this sub packs a serious punch—deep, clean bass that instantly elevates everything including quiet dialogue and explosive action scenes.

We’ve hosted a few movie nights with friends and family since setting it up, and everyone comments on how immersive the sound feels. It turns our living room into a mini-theater—no exaggeration. The setup was incredibly easy (Sonos app makes it seamless), and the minimalist design fits perfectly with our décor—sleek, subtle, and sophisticated.

Compare this to a friend of mine who bought a large subwoofer, sound bar and speakers from a different brand, this mini sounds way cleaner paired with my Sonos arc ultra. The price was unbeatable on Crate & Barrel at the time.

Highly recommend for anyone looking to transform their at-home audio setup without taking up too much space!
reviews.title: Small Size, Huge Impact!
reviews.author: AliG

reviews.body:
I have bought the full Sonos sound system (Beam Gen 2, Sub Mini, and 2 Era 100 speakers).
The connection of them is very painful, as they lose connection with each other, or doesn't even show up in the app. If you unplug one of them, you need a full restart on your WiFi router, and sometimes even when you haven't done anything with the speakers.

I must add, if it works, it is really great, especially for a small room, but man oh man the setting up is painful.
reviews.title: Review of Sonos Sub Mini trådløs subwoofer (sort)
reviews.author: Reviewed by Elgiganten Denmark customer

reviews.body: These speakers are easy to settle up connect the HDMI arc to port number two on LG television and if you look on the back of the TV it will be displayed which port is the arc port once connected it sets up itself in respect of following the SONOS instructions they are self-explanatory and easy to follow. I am not a tech savvy person but the speakers are extremely good value for money and the true sound is excellent. I am a genuine purchaser of a beam symbol, two era, 100 speakers and a sub mini subwoofer fabulous
reviews.title: Quality product with beautifully balanced sound.
reviews.author: PJ

reviews.body: This smaller size bass, is powerful. We have a family room 24 x 17' and you can feel the deep bass! It paired well with the Ikea bookshelf speakers, that act well as the rear speakers, as we already had them. The sonos arc acts as the center and side speakers. The bass adds a nice full, rich, dimensional sound quality, especially when watching newer movies or listening to music. Use the YouTube surround sound tester to hear it in action when first setting up.
reviews.title: Pounding deep bass
reviews.author: Pds

reviews.body:
So impressed that I've purchased more Sonos products since. The mini sub is paired with the Beam gen 2 (I'm in the process of adding era 100s as rears). I'm no audiophile but I am fussy. The sound is stunning! Playing Atmos/ultra hd via Amazon is rich, warm and punchy. The app is clunky as hell. Also to get the most of the speakers you need to use Trueplay which is iPhone only (I used the wifes) although it's only needed once for setup Overall if you can tolerate the Sonos apps quirks and iPhone need I'd highly recommend. Hence the missing star.
As for Richer Sounds. They're still my go to for tech' and long may they continue to be.
reviews.title: Excellent.....but.
reviews.author: Jayce23

reviews.body:
So I bought the Beam gen 2. Massive upgrade. Bought some sonus one to expand.
Amazing sound!
My mate you need a sub. I was like 'i don't need more bass'.
He called me silly and to just get one.

So I did. Wow! It changes everything.
Cleaner crisper sound on all fronts. Beam doesn't have to work as hard ones don't have to work as hard. Let's them focus. On why they're good at. Clear precise sound without having to over produce bass.

Game changer! Amazing!
If you're in the 'do I really need a sub' place.
Yes you do! This one! Buy it! Don't either like I did.

Looks cool and like a feature in the room too.
reviews.title: Get one!
reviews.author: Johnsel

reviews.body: I purchased this to go with my Sonos Arc plus hoping it would add the much needed bass and holy did it deliver. Out of the box setup was ridiculously easy, preset configuration was surprising with the amount of bass it added. Once you start fiddling with settings... HOLY CRAP! This lil thing knocks, I've had several people look confused because the bass but not seeing a typical subwoofer. Well designed Sonos.
reviews.title: This thing thumps
reviews.author: Mr Rogers

reviews.body: I started our mountain condo with a Beam 2 that was a great start, but found myself wanting something closer to my home experience. I added two Sonos ERA' 100s for surround which helped but still felt a little light. When I added the Sub Mini, things fell into place. Since we share a common wall with a neighbor, I've found that I can keep volumes at a reasonable level and still enjoy the full movie and listening experience where before I kept wanting to crank up the Beam. None of it is overwhelming, but just full, rich sound directed where it needs to be.
reviews.title: From sound bar to home theater
reviews.author: Scott

reviews.body: Deep, rich bass from a sub that's not very large. I wa surprised how good it sounded, to be honest. Being SONOS, I knew it would sound good and be a quality addition, but was surprised nonetheless with how great it actually is. Perfect for the apartment I live in with giving enough bass, but not too much to disturb my neighbors. Couldn't be happier!
reviews.title: I would buy this product again.
reviews.author: Duke

reviews.body:
I came in looking for a wired subwoofer, told the associate this and she direted me to the sonos mini sub, it looked great but couldn't
check the sound or look at the actual hook up but could get it in white which was a bonus, i asked her if it was wired or a cable and she said both as i explained that my mother had a wired Yamaha surround system and wanted to get her a new wired subwoofer for Christmas as her old one failed, clearly she steered my in the wrong direction because the sonos mini sub is wireless and seems to be only compatible with the sonos wireless sound bar which i stated that im dealing with a wired surround sound system
reviews.title: Misleading
reviews.author: Misleading

reviews.body:
Incredibly happy with this subwoofer.

I'm no audiophile and I don't listen to D&B but I can appreciate the depth this adds to the sound.

Even though it was B rated it included all packaging and had a few light marks making it a bargain. Especially with the 5y warranty compared to the 1y if bought new.

Speaker looks smart and was up and running within a couple of minutes after unboxing!
reviews.title: Excellent Subwoofer
reviews.author: SamN96

reviews.body: This product is a must have for owners of any soundbar. In combination with Sonos Arc makes perfect match for bold music and astonishing sound of any movie. Its design fits any type of your room. Music gets 3rd dimension with Sonos Sub-Mini. It is easy to use and easy to set-up. true-play feature is one of the best on the market. For the money it costs you will get more than that. I got 2 new Sonos users when I presented it to my neighbors. Sonos is not only about superb sound, but also about perfect software that you need to run the system. It is regularly update and it is working smoothly as my Apple Devices. Combination of Sonos Arc and Sub mini is the best price/value ratio you can get on this planet these days.....
reviews.title: A must have for your full feel of a music and sound in gener
reviews.author: Patrik

reviews.body:
Primarily, for TV, however, the sound is awesome that I now will listen to more music.
As I alluded to earlier, the setuo is not easy and assistance from other countries is horrible. You can't understand or hear them. I had Great help from a man from Costa Rica that was articulate & you could understand . I used to be able to turn system off & restart. Now I have to raise the volume control after starting, it's a pain. I just hate going through the process of calling for help to outside countries and the battle of trying to understand & hear support help! For an American made product why have outsiders work in support that can't mesh with this Great American made product ! I get you're (Sonos) is trying to save $$$, but can't you find good young or retired American help? Bet you can ? I want to purchase some wireless speakers to go with my Beam, Mini Sub, but setup and support make reluctant !
reviews.title: The product itself is great, however, the setup is not e

reviews.body:
We did a $5k purchase & we’re very impressed with the sound quality but frequently while watching TV the sound cut out. Then we noticed switching from AppleTV to our Bell receiver would end the sound. Sometimes we opened the Sonos app & the message would read “unable to connect to Sonos ARC ultra.” The fix’s…unplug it all & plug it back in!

The issue was so bad we returned it all.
reviews.title: Great HW, Poor SW
reviews.author: Red

reviews.body: I use it to watch videos, movies, television, and listen to music in the living room. It's just great. As a plus, I can say that the wireless connection is much better than Bluetooth because when I'm listening to Spotify and someone calls me, I can talk to them on the phone while the music keeps playing, which is much more convenient than just using Bluetooth. The design of the Beam 2 and Sub mini is perfect-together they are simply superb.
reviews.title: I would buy an additional Era 100 - 2 pcs.
reviews.author: DK

reviews.body: Substantial lift in the audio quality in our apartment. The subtle design means blends in to its surroundings and doesn't take away from the decor. Obviously ideal for music. Love it with a good movie and drama series too, and even for sport. So much clearer now. Perfect pairing with the Beam sound bar and super easy to setup. Very happy with it.
reviews.title: Big audio improvement - subtle design
reviews.author: Banjo

reviews.body: I have been wanting to buy this speaker for some time . Fortunately the price was reduced and I pulled the trigger. Currently I have only had it a short time and I am trying different placement in my home . The sound and bass are great . I would recommend it. I hope Sonos keeps the app working properly. I am having issues with my iTunes playing with the app which is disappointing.
reviews.title: Dynamic Bass !
reviews.author: Ron

reviews.body:
I added this to arc and noticed immediate substantial improvements for movies and video.

Obviously there is far more solidity and impact at the bottom end but it also seemed to enhance clarity in the mid band with clearer vocals and sharper edges around everything. We set it to +2 for the sub output, which seemed the sweet spot for us. Any more and it's too much.

For music it's a little more of a mixed bag, the sub-mini somehow just isn't quite quick enough to keep up and I found myself preferring it dialed back to a lower output. Don't get me wrong the setup is still fine for what it is and better with the sub than without it.

The room is a fair size perhaps 24x12 we watch tv at one end of it facing in the narrow direction.
reviews.title: Decent improvement with arcs
reviews.author: Bob

reviews.body: For the skeptic's out there, like l was. This little sub packs some great sounding bass, which took me a minute to adjust to my liking along with the satellite speakers, this system is a great sounding addition for your daily use or to use for your liking wherever you need. The sound from this system, a pair of 100's and the mini sub will blow you away.
reviews.title: Pleasant Surprise
reviews.author: Gabe

reviews.body: Seriously good bass for such a small package! It won't rattle the windows, but it will get down there! Adds so much depth and richness! I have two of these in two different systems. First one wouldn't update until I hooked it up to an Ethernet connection. After that all was good! Inconvenient but easy to do.
reviews.title: Powerful bass in a small package!
reviews.author: B Rice

reviews.body: I bought the Google Nest Hub 2 some time ago, and now the seller, who is really good, has asked if I would share my opinion on this product. My opinion is divided, because technically: sound, picture, connection, appearance etc. are good, which I cannot say about the software. The set-up is not as simple and logical as I expected it to be, to be able to use some things, there are requirements for loss of privacy that I don't think are reasonable. And then there's the fact that the device disregards your commands and decides what to do on its own. And that is unacceptable to me, for example: when I leave home and nobody is there, I have the display switched off, but when I return, the display is always on again without me wanting it to be or without me having caused it to be. I ask myself the question: what is the device doing in the background without my knowledge, without my instructions? This lack of knowledge arouses suspicion and so I have disconnected it from the power supply and am not using it at the moment. I'm thinking about what I'm going to do with it. It's a shame really, because I had a lot of plans. Yes, and I would never have thought that saying "hey Google" would make you feel stupid, as if you were saying: hey broom sweep.

I bought this Google Nest Hub because I’m a fan of the ecosystem, but it seems this one missed its morning coffee. Compared to my other Hubs, the audio isn't quite as crisp—it’s like the difference between a live concert and a concert heard through a thick velvet curtain.

Navigating the screen is also a bit of a test in patience. It moves with the quiet confidence of a snail who knows it will get there eventually, but isn’t in any particular rush.

That said, Gemini is still the MVP here. It answers my questions accurately and handles my "lights out" commands perfectly without me having to lift a finger. It’s great for a secondary spot where you don't need top-tier sound, but if you’re looking for "fast and loud," this one is more "slow and steady." 4 stars for being a reliable, if slightly sluggish, assistant!
reviews.title: The Helpful Snail on My Nightstand
reviews.author: Tim

reviews.body: The Google Nest Hub 2nd Gen is a compact and stylish smart display that works seamlessly with Google Assistant. It's great for controlling smart home devices, checking the weather, playing YouTube videos, or following recipes hands-free in the kitchen. The screen is bright and responsive, and the sleep tracking feature adds extra value for bedroom use. However, it doesn't come with a built-in camera for video calls, which may be a drawback for some users. Overall, it's a practical and affordable smart display for everyday use.
reviews.title: Smart and Handy Display, But No Camera
reviews.author: anonymous

reviews.body: I have owned 2 hubs for a couple of years and they are both consistently unreliable (since day 1). We use them to stream the nest doorbell cam. When they work, it's great. The clarity is fine. What is annoying is that it kicks off the front door and returns to the clock or the photo gallery. I have to say, "hey google, show me the front door at least 8 times/day." Why can't it just stay there? Sometimes it will state there is no connection (one of these hubs sits on the same next as the modem/router, so I know that isn't the problem). It is easily remedied by unplugging and plugging it back in (we only have to do this 1-2 times/month). I have called cs several times, hoping to get one that will find a permanent fix, but no luck. This could be such a great hub if it would just reliably stay on the front door. Seems like there could be a software fix for this. They both work this way, so I know it isn't a defective, more of a design flaw.
reviews.title: Works well when it works
reviews.author: j s

reviews.body:
This item was used or a display of some kind, in a completely different Asian language and alphabet/letter system. We plugged it in and it was already coded to another language (not English) so it took wayyyy longer for set up, because I had to find multiple YouTube videos of someone setting it up in English and just copy where the went blindly to try and change the language settings. Thankfully YouTube figured it out. Even a hard reset of the device wouldn’t take it back to English.

It ultimately works as advertised, but was just tricky to set up.
reviews.title: I was sent a used, but working - device. :(
reviews.author: Jasmin

reviews.body:
If you want a digital picture frame with weather, this device is for you.

Otherwise, there is literally nothing you can do with this device that you can't do (and do much better) with any generic Android phone or tablet . It has next to zero apps available for it. I was going to keep it just to watch Sling Tv, but, IF you can get it to launch, there's no program guide or way to change channe without voice commands. You can cast to it but you're back to using two devices. You'd be Way better off with a Fire or ONN tablet. The clock faces are weird with limited selections. Dashboard is not really cusomizable it's based on Google's suggestions. This device seems to have no reason at all to exist.
reviews.title: A Digital Picture Frame for 2025.
reviews.author: anonymous

reviews.body: There is literally nothing you can do with this device that you cant do (and do much better) with any generic Android phone / tablet and a charging dock. This device is extremely laggy, difficult to setup, comes with practically zero nstructions whatsoever, has next to zero apps available for it (and no easy way to install them - you basically have to turn over your web / app history to Google, then it will 'suggest' apps based on what it 'thinks' you want). The clock faces are weird with extremely limited selections, and no way to add more. It has no nightlight feature (despite having a wake up light), extremely limited customization options, and in general is a pretty useless device. Am generally a fan of google home devices but this particular device seems to have no reason at all to exist.
reviews.title: Truthfully, a useless device.
reviews.author: smiley1

reviews.body: Nest hub is able to view my Wyze cameras, play youtube videos, listen to Spotify, and control my Nest thermostat and smart plugs. However, the processor and RAM are not sufficient to run the apps properly and I have had to restart the Hub numerous times as it will get "stuck" when transitioning from the clock screen to opening the apps menu. Openinging my camera views on my Wyze camera takes a long time. Also, why does google have to make their AC plug so big? It covers up another socket. I like the features of the hub and as a clock and music player it works well as the sound quality has enough mids and bass for adequate sound quality but lacks hardware support to function smoothly. Soes not support Amazon music as a native app but it has Spotify, strange. I also wish when I get notifications on my phone for my front door camera it would also show up on the Nest Hub. Unless the software supports the lack luster hardware better I do not recommend this product.
reviews.title: Slow

reviews.body: Just got the Nest Hub 2nd gen as a gift.I replaced the Nest Mini 2nd gen I had in the living room with it and placed the Mini in my bedroom. I resisted getting it for the longest time due to privacy concerns and have just been using my iPhone for the home automation; same goes for the mini. Most lights, TV’s and electronics in my house are “smart” and I predominantly use Google Home/Assistant for most tasks, oppose to Amazon. I find Google to be more superior because of the cell phone and Google services integration. It’s an absolute high quality product and works great. When it’s idling it displays pics from my library I have selected, sound quality is good, not amazing. The reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is: I wish it would have video call integration, YouTube and a smoother interface. Feels a bit slow sometimes. Now, if it was detachable and use it like a tablet, making the speaker a dock, it would be perfect. Overall I feel like it’s the most bang for your buck. Thank you
reviews.title: Google Nest Hub 2. Almost there…
reviews.author: Olivian

reviews.body: Work great with our smart home lights, thermostat, cameras, etc. I was excited to get the next generation hub for the upgraded speaker sound. Sleep monitoring hasn’t been helpful; maybe I turned off notifications somewhere but have forgotten about it. I’ve used the hand gestures to pause music and other controls though while doing laundry got false responses. I love when someone rings the doorbell I can hear who it is (if their face was previously saved) and get an instant view of our Nest doorbell. We have several nest security cameras around the house and wish for a tile view with multiple cameras on the display at once. Most of my extended family has seen or experienced the smart home in action and have started to get their own devices. We’ve bought the hub and hub max for our parents which is great for sharing pics of kids seamlessly with google photos. Photo frame is primary reason I purchased the first generation following the Hub Max upon release. I'm happy with updated version.
reviews.title: Sound and Sensor Upgrades - Same great hub

reviews.body: This is marketed as a sleep monitor/sensor to help improve your sleep.It fails spectacularly at that.It succeeds amazingly in one thing: Making you sleep worse.It has a sunrise alarm (theoretically) that is supposed to be able to wake you with just light. Everyone else that does this understands that it should start out with minimal brightness and very red and slowly transition to brighter and bluer. This starts out at maximum brightness immediately. Furthermore you CANNOT turn off the noise alarm (or delay the noise alarm) so that you are actually woken up by the light. This makes the sunrise alarm worse than useless.The display will randomly make noises or turn the screen on for a second or two during the night. So it WILL wake you up with light.. even if you didn't set an alarm... but not at the correct time.The settings for this are distributed among at least 5 different apps it's nearly impossible to configure. It can't self-configure.The output "suggestions" are garbage
reviews.title: Randomly Wakes Me Up In the Middle of the Night
reviews.author: Yoni

reviews.body: Why did I expect anything else? It'll be that way until they suddenly kill off the feature some day. That's just how they work.I already had a Nest Hub (1st gen), so I didn't need this one. But it has this fancy new sleep tracking feature, and I have severe sleep issues. When they put it on sale, I could no longer resistSetup was easy. A bit too easy, I suspected. I was right. A few seconds of lying in your bed motionless is not enough to calibrate a the software to recognize when you're sleeping vs when you're not. Despite multiple calibrations, it still gets it wrong.Any time I am within it's view, it thinks I'm in bed. Sitting up on the side of the bed, standing beside the bed, walking back and forth on the other side of the room, all = in bed. Even when I really am in bed, it gets my awake/asleep times wrong. These mistakes happen consistently. It is of no use for sleep tracking.Plus, if you have sleep tracking turned on, you can forget ever using it like normal Nest Hub.
reviews.title: Confusing, Inaccurate, and Poorly Integrated

reviews.body: I've had this Nest Hub 2nd Gen for a month now, but I have been using a Nest Hub Max for about a yearUnlike my experience with my Nest Hub Max, which was surprisingly slow at the first few months till it magically got better, my Nest Hub was quick and snappy right out of the box. Adding it to my Google Home app was a breeze. It took just a few seconds and everything that I can see on my Nest Home Max automatically showed up on my Nest HubDisplay quality is great, although a little too small if you leave it in a corner of the room. Unlike Nest Hub Max, you have to get close to this one if you're watching news or a YouTube video. Sound quality is decent. You can hear it clearly if you're in the other room tooMy 2 biggest disappointments are:1. Lack of camera. Other products in this range have a monitoring camera that can be used as security camera2. The biggest issue is lack of apps or functionality. It cannot function as an Android tablet. Touch control of its apps are limited
reviews.title: Great Google Voice Assistant with Display
reviews.author: Shahab

reviews.body: I purchased a Nest Hub to use up a $10 discount (for purchasing our Nest Thermostat earlier this year). The original intent was to allow family members to view each-others' calendars on a shared screen device, to aid in scheduling doctors appointments, meetings, etc. Sadly, this isn't something the Nest Hub is able to do, which was a disappointing discovery. For what it does, however, it does very well. It's ambient screen brightness adjustment works well in the bedroom as an alarm clock, and an easy way to check on our smart lights and thermostat without the voice commands (helpful when our partner is still sleeping). The audio quality is also much better than the Google Minis that we've been using previously, so listening to music is more enjoyable on this device. We'll keep it in our smart-device ecosystem, but wish it had some more calendar features for a houeshold.
reviews.title: Good, but missing an assumed calendar feature...
reviews.author: Rorowe

reviews.body:
Good Points: Screen looks nice. Voice control works with smart lights.

Improvement Points: Touch screen is terribly unresponsive by today's standards. Very unintuitive to set up properly so I gave up.

As an example of its logic, at one point it only lets you get to a setting by using voice control but then only lets you choose the following option using touch control. As it's also sluggish in operation you can easily hit the wrong touch button and then there's no option to go back. So you have to start again with a completely illogical sequence.

Hence the following examples of things I don't like, may be due to not having been set up properly.

Anyway, it only reads my main Google calendar not my sub or associated calenders, which makes it useless to check my agenda.

I can't set up the screen to show exactly what I want e.g. agenda on one half, notifications on the other.

I can't show photos from my local server only those that are stored on Google Photos. I can only show a single Google Photo album album as a screen saver not all my Google photos.

The voice commands are not intuitive so you'll have to memorize any you want to use. In other words it will only be useful if you intend to use the voice commands frequently enough to remember them.

The automated routines (morning, evening, etc) are another example of big tech companies thinking they know what we want to do better than we know.

Mine nearly went into the bin after several hours of trying to get it to do anything useful. I've kept it but only ever use it to turn my smart lights on and off.
reviews.title: Review of GOOGLE Nest Hub (2nd Gen) Smart Display with Google Assistant - Chalk
reviews.author: Reviewed by Currys customer

reviews.body:
The Google Nest Home Max is by far the most worthless home efficiency tool you can buy. It does have the ability to make video and audio calls, but then so does your phone. It also has the ability to help answer questions you may have: “Hey Google, how many cups in a quart?” but then so does a Google Home Mini that you can buy for $40($20 from most Facebook marketplace sales).

What it does not have is any functionality that you would want in a standing hub system. It has no way of showing a monthly family calendar so you can see what’s going on or plan-ahead. It has no way of creating a user-friendly chore or task-list so you can be more efficient with your day. It also doesn’t work on new network router systems, so you have to be a little network savvy and ensure you disable IPv6 in multiple settings of your router in order for it to actually work in the first place.

Finally, while you’re trying to troubleshoot and fix all the issues with your Google Nest Hub Max system your short return window is slowly dwindling down, and working with their customer support is similar to working with a movie stereotyped version of the Department of Motor Vehicles (no offense DMV, you’ve been good to me). Once you get sent back and forth between two different departments under the guise of trying to help you, you’ll eventually give up. You will be the new proud owner of the worlds bulkiest, non-wireless, least versatile tablet in the world.

Run away, don’t buy this product, good luck.
reviews.title: Do not buy this.
reviews.author: Christopher Luther

reviews.body: This is my first experience with a "smart speaker" type thing. I'm mostly using it as a photo frame and occasional music player. The sound quality is on par with a decent small Bluetooth speaker. You sort of have to learn what commands are understood, and which ones produce the smart speaker equivalent of crickets ("something went wrong..."). And the reaction time can be deadly slow. Because this thing relies completely on verbal commands, it's a little frustrating, but usually I get what I want. The other verbal features ("is it going to snow?"; "What's in a gimlet?") are spookily accurate. But I'm glad I can turn the mic off with a switch.It took a while to figure out how to get my photos on my iPhone into the Google photos app and make an album that would display on the device. I'm pretty happy with it now, but I can’t say it was easy to learn. The image quality is good and the various display settings are great. I wish the resolution was a little better.
reviews.title: Pretty cool although sometimes a little sleepy
reviews.author: Tom in NC

reviews.body:
Bought this while on sale for Father's Day at $70. Always wanted to have a Google Home Hub so it was worth the deal. I always thought the Google Home Hub was more advanced but it is lacking in some areas. Don't expect it to be a tablet. It does provide very basic use around the house if you have a smart house but don't expect it to be the best in video quality and responsiveness. Overall, I'm happy with it as a bundle for $70. If anything, I can use the Google Home Hub as a Smart Picture Frame.

I've been using Wyze Camv3 for almost a year now and I can say I'm quite satisfy with it. It's simple to set up and use. I like that it can have local storage so if you didn't want to subscribe to the service, it'll still record all encounters onto the local storage. I found that this is all I really need since I don't mind back tracking to find a clip. As of now, I am subscribed to the service because I like that I can watch the videos at x1, x2, and x4 the video speed and I have a new puppy. I have encounter issues where the cameras lagged or didn't load but a simple restart of the app fixes this. I also found restarting the cameras every few days helps with lag and loading. One down side for sure is that if Wyze Server goes down, you won't be able to load your cameras on the app at all. I had this happen once to me. Local recording, however, does continue to record even if the Wyze Server is down.

Overall, satisfy with the cameras for being budget friendly, user friendly, and being what I need in terms of minimal surveillance. Satisfy with the Google Home Hub for the price I got it at since it's very basic and works best as a smart picture frame, music hub, and as an addition to a smart home.
reviews.title: Great Bundle if on Sell
reviews.author: X. Xiong

reviews.body:
Responsiveness:The touch screen response is fast.
Voice Control:Voice control work perfectly and the setup real easy.

I think this is original unit old new stock from Japan year made 2022. Original language is Japan but once connect to your Google account automatically change to English. Setup real easy and quick. Real bargain for the price I paid. Thanks seller.
reviews.author: kaihnsn

reviews.body: I listen to music on my Google Mini. I bought this as a cosmetic replacement. It looks nice, displays photos, time and temperature. It has all the same Google Assistant features as the Mini. If music isn't your primary need or if you're not that demanding with sound, you might like this. Not that the Mini has awesome sound, but this is even less quality, and that's after adjusting the equalizer.
reviews.title: Nice to look at, terrible audio
reviews.author: JoeB

reviews.body: Obviously not tested before they sent it. Had green screen when set up, hard to set up for elderly parents who live interstate and CEX had no care as to how they were going to have a new one set up for them as I planned to be down when they received it. Would have been professional to test before they cause so much hassle sending a faulty product out. Offered refund which didn’t help parents get a new one and have it set up. There is no way possible this could have been tested before going out. Another blatant lie from un untrustworthy company. So clearly a gamble if you purchase.
reviews.title: Green screen not tested before they go Out. Gamble
reviews.author: Jayde163

reviews.body:
This is my 6th Google Home for my house. It's really great. It makes life easier to control lights, TV, aircond, fans, playing music and watching YouTube or even Netflix. Highly recommended.
Product from the Seller is in English. Comes with China plug pin but Seller gave me a free adaptor. I could setup immediately. Fast shipment and delivery. Seller is recommended and their price is the best! Thank you Seller.

The only blunder is the Courier. They didn't handle my package with care. Box was torn and dented. Perhaps Seller can place a fragile sticker on the package to ensure Courier handle it with care.

This hub was a little disappointing because it does not automatically bring up live feeds where motion/people are detected. To see the cameras, you have to manually go to each. Also, it’s not easy to switch between them with a swipe, you have to navigate the menu anew to see them. It’s a bit annoying. Other than that, it works fairly well. Adequate screen brightness and sound. Compatible with google nest devices.
reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.author: Grudgen

reviews.body: I got one of these for free from the Google One 2TB deal and decided to get another. If I'd known functionality would be relatively crippled compared to Alexa I may have been less inclined: there is no motion sensing support or other such triggers which really give your house that space-age feeling. Besides that, on rare occasions devices will disconnect randomly despite getting a strong 5g signal from a nearby repeater, and the voice interpretation is sometimes completely wrong even after weeks of training itself with my voice samples. Once I was speaking directly into my kitchen hub and my workspace hub 50 feet away responded.All of these are software issues and I feel the hardware is a good deal for the price, so the question is how much do you trust Google to follow through with updates? If you're embedded into the Google ecosystem as I am you probably don't have a lot of choice, but know that Google's Smart Home system still seems to be in "early-adopter" phase.
reviews.title: Hit and miss
reviews.author: Jelly

reviews.body:
I have been using a Google Mini to run several smart plugs, smart LED lights on my balcony and two different Bluetooth speakers. Using Home, KASA and SmartLife to set up and run these items was a little challenging. Everything worked but not smoothly. I bought the Hub expecting to have to delete, reinstall and set up all the plugs, lights and speakers again to get everything set up and responding to my liking. That was not the case. I plugged in the hub logged into my network and opened Home. Everything was there. Previously I could not get the assistant to respond to my voice command for balcony lights or a fan in my living room. The first command was for the fan and it worked as did the command for the balcony lights. What I thought would be a frustrating reinstall of several items became a one step fix for everything. All plugs respond individually or in a sequence, balcony lights respond to on or off or change of colours and the fan actually responds to it designated name which it did not do with the older mini. The hub is in my living area where I can see photos, weather, ask questions in the a.m. use the timer etc. I prefer to use my Nose speakers for music so I have not actually tested the speakers in the Hub. But I simply ask for my stations, Sirius XM or speakers. Simply better with little to no additional resetting/reinstalling from me.
This was a good buy for me at a sale price.
reviews.title: Google Nest Hub 2nd Gen
reviews.author: Chuck

reviews.body: This is definitely the most basic smart home touchscreen I can imagine a company like Google selling. It gets by, but barely. Its best trait is an easy setup through the Home app. Casting media is also very straightforward, as expected. Video quality is acceptable, though it would be moreso as a secondary viewer (perhaps in a foyer niche or other restrictively small area). Touch controls aren't zippy, but faster than downright sluggish. Everything is slightly below middle ground compared to their more premium Hub Max. If you're looking for good quality YouTube videos and sound for the kitchen or an eye-catching display, this isn't the one. For a basic, no frills utilitarian purpose, I would recommend buying it on sale.
reviews.title: Basic media hub gets the job done.

reviews.author: Annie

reviews.body: Admittedly, I'm still in the "getting to know all about you" phase of using Nest Hub. I finally reached the point where I had enough smart home devices, the latest being the Nest thermostat, that I needed to consolidate them so I could use voice command. Honestly I struggled between Nest and Alexa but in the end Nest won because of the massive amount of information Google has access to, plus a great black Friday deal sealed it. Like I said before, I'm still learning all there is to know but I can tell you set up of the device was easy for any reasonably tech savvy person. I integrated my Hue hub, Samsung Smarthings robot vacuum, Nest thermostat and a few Zigbee smart plugs with only a little head scratching. I'm still refining the seamless operation of everything including streaming radio and ROKU TV. There are a few things that I need to figure out to get all of the information I want "on demand" but the product is a good one. Now if only it had a real "human" name.
reviews.title: What it does it does well!
reviews.author: Doug K

reviews.body: For what you get for the money, this is a great value. The Good: As a picture frame alone, I like the product scrolling my favorite photos. I also use it to control wifi lights via gui as my wife uses this feature. It is also a very Simple to play Spotify playlists on a speaker group throughout out house and skip through songs. I have use the google TV feature to play cartoons for my grandkids as well. There are many more good features like recipes, wellness, playing ocean sounds. Needs improvement: Google home side. That software needs work, so why this isn't specific to this device, if you are deciding between Alexa and Google home it is important. I use Heos on my stereo, so I created a routine to start a playlist on Spotify, set the playlist to random, then start playing that playlist on the stereo. After many attempts, I finally got this to work, but after a week, it started failing. ( Alexa works) Google Home needs better documentation and be less buggy.

reviews.body: This hub is best described as being a google/nest mini speaker with a display. The speaker has good sound considering how small it is and its price. The display can be used as a touchscreen or by voice and has a sharp picture. The screen can display either google generated photos or any number of google photo albums of your own creation, with the time and temperature in the lower corner. You can also simply display a digital clock (it switches to this mode in low light, a bonus if you are using it as a bedside clock). There are also other functions that the display can be used for such as playing YouTube, YouTube Music or Netflix videos, casting from your phone, alarms, timers, controlling your smart home, adding to your shopping list, displaying your calendar, etc. In other words, all of the Google smart home features plus other useful features.I liked it enough in my kitchen that I bought a second for my home and two as Christmas gifts. I'd highly recommend for any smart home.

name: Echo (4th Gen) Smart Speaker
bestFor: Built-in Zigbee smart home hub with premium Dolby stereo sound
description: Talk about well-rounded. Echo combines premium sound, a built-in Zigbee smart home hub, and a temperature sensor. Powerful speakers deliver clear highs, dynamic mids, and deep bass for rich, detailed sound that adapts to any room. Just ask Alexa to play music, answer questions, make calls, and tell you the news, sports scores, weather, and more. Use your voice to play a song, artist, or genre through your favourite streaming service. And with multi-room music, you can fill your whole home with music, radio stations, podcasts, and Audible using compatible Echo devices in different rooms. The built-in smart home hub lets you easily set up and manage smart devices that use Zigbee. Just say, Alexa, discover my devices and Echo will discover and set up your compatible devices. Make your life easier at home. Set timers, ask questions, add items to lists, and create calendar events and reminders. With access to thousands of Alexa skills, you can check the traffic and weather, or play the news. With Announcements, you can contact other compatible Echo devices to let everyone know dinners ready or remind the kids that its bedtime. Plus, hands-free calling helps you stay in touch with friends and family who have a compatible Echo device or the Alexa app. Alexa and Echo devices are built with multiple layers of privacy protection. Echo smart speakers have a microphone off button that electronically disconnects the microphones. You also have control over your voice recordings and can view, hear, or delete them at any time.

reviews.body: I have had the Bose smart soundbar for about a week and a half. The initial set up was a little fiddly and the app seemed to be 'stuck' performing an update. I eventually unplugged the unit, waited 30 seconds and switched on again and everything fell into place. It is certainly a big improvement on my TV's speakers. It has great sound and I find the bass more than adequate. Music streaming is easy and the sound is also very good. However, I have yet to get any sense of height from the upfiring speakers, including from programmes with Dolby Atmos sound. Maybe I just haven't watched the right programmes/ films yet and I am still playing around with the settings. Time will tell. I'm sorry to say the app is poor. It is slow, frequently crashes and at one point was repeatedly requesting feedback. It seemed to be stuck in a loop and I had to uninstall and reinstall to stop it happening. In fact, my phone sent a push notification that the Bose app was crashing frequently and I should put it in a deep sleep! App aside, quite pleased with the soundbar so far.

reviews.author: Laura S

reviews.body:
The Smart Soundbar is a new mid-range product from Bose. The overall profile of the soundbar is low and sleek, allowing a user to place the soundbar right in front of their TV without the worry of it blocking any sensors affecting the TV remote control. On the top of the soundbar the power and mute buttons are flush with the system. With the size of the soundbar and the sound quality, I feel it is best suited for TV’s 50” and below. Mine is set up on a Sony 65” X90J and at times the sound seems to be somewhat underwhelming.

The soundbar is a simple plug and play. I didn’t have to reprogram any remotes or have my Sony TV search for the soundbar. Once the Bose app found the soundbar on my Wi-Fi, I was up and running.

Streaming music with either Bluetooth or Airplay was a bit of a challenge as there is no equalizer on the Bose app to open up the soundbar. Selecting the AI dialogue mode does help with the clarity and adjusting the bass, treble.

Watching live TV or streaming gives a clean, crisp overall sound. This is where the AI dialogue shines, but again, you will have to adjust the bass and treble to your preferred settings. There are no presets via the app. You can make modifications using the remote control or the Bose app.

Overall, the soundbar is a nice entry to mid-level soundbar for a smaller TV. I think it would work well in a small bedroom or even on a desk if one didn’t want to use PC speakers.

Pros – Small, sleek, mid-range soundbar
For smaller areas
Easy set up
Works with all remotes

Cons – Lacking bass
reviews.title: Nice Soundbar With A Few Exceptions
reviews.author: RavenKat

reviews.body:
The Bose Smart Soundbar is just a hair shy of being amazing. It is packed FULL of features from Alexa and Google Assistant support to built in support for all of the top music apps like Spotify, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, Tidal, and more! It looks amazing with it's elegant sleek design and it's incredibly easy to setup.

The Soundbar works with the existing Bose app and has full features to adjust your audio preferences, play music, and enable features. It includes AI Dialogue detection, which levels the volume when people are speaking. It does a really great job at this and really improves the experience.

My favorite feature is that you can pair them with the Bose Ultra Open Earbuds for personal surround sound. This works really well for rooms that don't or can't have additional satellite speakers. By pairing the earbuds and enabling Personal Surround sound it creates a fully immersive audio experience that's comfortable for long periods of time. It's truly an unreal experience.

However, there is one thing the soundbar is lacking: Bass. The audio quality from the soundbar for normal TV watching falls a little flat. It is an upgrade to having no soundbar at all, but it sounds a little "tinny" even after adjusting the audio settings. The audio quality did improve when watching a show on AppleTV+ with Dolby Atmos support and with certain 4k movies. Music from Spotify, YouTube Music, and Tidal all sound really great as well!

The fix for everyday TV watching is to either use the Ultra Open Earbuds constantly or invest in the Bose subwoofer and additional speakers.

reviews.body:
My normal device before this was a Sonos Ray. I was satisfied with the Sonos, but it's only output is Optical with no ability for HDMI hookups.
I've used and owned many other soundbars and spent some time with the Bose Smart Ultra Soundbar. The Ultra still fetches a price of around eight or nine hundred dollars and offers Bose's AdaptIQ (which I thought seemed a bit gimmicky before becoming a believer).This soundbar does not have this ability but does offer a few "extras" other devices may not. It seems to be a nice middle-of-the-road unit.
There is room to expand the system with satellites and a sub, but it's not 100% necessary.
I've been using mine in my bedroom and it works great for this purpose.
I have it wall mounted and connected to my TV through eArc which gives me the benefit of having the soundbar turn on and off with my TV. I was able to easily pair my existing remote with it (using a Roku Ultra box/remote), which was very easy and intuitive with Bose's "Roku-Ready" capabilities.
Pairing with the Bose app upon initial installation was quick and easy, and I have not experienced any connection issues or hiccups. There are also an optical input/standard Bose bass module output, and a port to plug in an IR blaster in case it's mounted behind the TV or in a cabinet, etc.
I've had no issues with IR with the soundbar mounted above my TV and out of the way.
You can also add a wireless Bose amp or wireless Bose speakers as well.

This device can work as a standalone Alexa voice assistant, or can be easily integrated with Alexa and Google Home.
The ability to cast from my android devices (AirPlay works for iPhones) and Bluetooth capabilities offer everything I'd ask for from a Soundbar.
Ability to add "Groups" of Bose speakers from within the app is a nice plus (I have the soundbar "grouped" with my existing Bose Amp which pushes a couple Seinnheiser bookshelf speakers for when I want to listen to music a little louder.
Unfortunately I'm unable to group this way from any HDMI output coming from the television.
The volume can go fairly loud without too much distortion, although I have noticed it can become a little muddled. Using Bose AI dialogue mode really helps to keep any spoken word more pronounced and at the forefront of other noise or music when streaming video.
This is very similar in size and style to the Bose Smart Soundbar 600 but has some extras such as the AI dialogue mode. The ability to set up "personal surround sound" using the still fairly new Bose Ultra Open Earbuds is a great feature- but currently these are the only earbuds that will work to achieve this because of their open design and Bose branding.
You'll have to decide where to spend that money if you wish to update/upgrade your system from here.
The Bose Smart Soundbar retails for $500 with another $300 price tag for the Ultra Open buds. In my opinion these earbuds are worth that price, but this review is for the 2024 Smart Soundbar. It's worth noting that these two can be bought as a bundle, but you'd only save a couple bucks this way. It'd be nice if they knocked like $50 off for the bundle.
The Bose 600 Soundbar goes for about $450 brand new as of this writing, and I feel like the extra money is worth it when you account for these newer features only offered on this sound bar currently.

reviews.body:
The Ecobee is a high-quality piece of hardware with professional-grade customization. However, the user experience is a total maze of "smart" logic that constantly contradicts itself.

​The Good: Granular Control
​If you know your HVAC system, this unit is solid. I love that I can set a 0.5°F temperature differential to keep my house steady—most thermostats force a full 1°F swing which lets humidity get out of control. The ability to set a minimum fan runtime per hour is a lifesaver for preventing water buildup in the drain pan and keeping the air from getting stagnant. These "pro" settings are exactly why I bought it.

​The Bad: A Software "Cluster"
​The interface is a nightmare of hidden, overlapping features. You can disable one "Smart" setting, thinking you finally have control, only to wake up the next morning to a house that's 75% humidity because another "Smart" feature you didn't even know existed (like Smart Recovery or Follow Me) decided to override your manual hold.

​It feels like the software is constantly fighting you:
​You have to hunt through three different menus just to make it act like a "dumb" thermostat. Some settings are only on the wall unit, while others are in the app.

​The "Smart" logic is so aggressive that it will "mute" sensors in occupied rooms just because it didn't see enough motion, leaving you (and in my case, my pet bird) in a hot, humid room while the thermostat thinks everything is fine.

​The Verdict
​It’s a powerful tool, but Ecobee has made it incredibly un-user-friendly. They’ve layered so many "eco" and "intelligent" features on top of each other that they all end up tripping over one another. If you have the patience to spend days "locking it down" and killing all the smart logic, it’s a 5-star machine. But out of the box? It’s a frustrating experience that requires way too much babysitting.

5 STARS Only if ------ A fix/update to the UI to decrease confusion and stop letting the "smart" features contradict the manual settings.
reviews.title: Great Hardware, Sabotaged by Contradictory Software
reviews.author: Ecobee Review

reviews.body: We switched to the Ecobee thermostat when Nest discontinued support for their first and second generation thermostats. The Ecobee hardware is good quality. However the functionality of the control app generationally inferior to the Nest app. Our major requirement is to have remote access and control during long periods away from home. While this is possible with the Eccobee product, it requires multiple steps for each of our five thermostats. In our case what I could do from the Nest Home Screen with one step, now requires three steps for each unit .... fifteen steps through multiple screens to basically set and hold an away temperature, the same to reverse and set a home temp. There are automation functions but they really are designed for a home that is occupied full time. The home/away/sleep functions never seem to really learn that the house isn't occupied and therefore always wants to turn the heat on at some point during the day. Even those you may also be upset with google for pulling the rug out from the first gen themostat products, if I had it to do over I'd go with the new Nest units because of the superior remote control available in their app.
reviews.title: Good hardware, terrible app!
reviews.author: Richard

reviews.body:
Ecobee is easy to setup. If you are unsure what you are doing, they have an app that walks you through everything. Still if you are unsure the customer service is top notch and will get you through the setup process with ease. They will walk you through the setup start to finish, then test the system to ensure all functions of your thermostat are working, help you setup a schedule (even explain the schedule to you).

Once you get through the setup and start playing with the system yourself you will fall in love with it. Connecting to Apple HomeKit, Alexa, or Google makes life easy. Ecobee works with other products too such as Yale locks.

I have had this thermostat for over a month and my energy has lowered. My house stays at a comfortable temp in each room (if you keep the doors shut and the sensors in all rooms with the exception of the bathrooms).

The price is a little high but the quality and features that went into this thermostat is worth it. I highly recommend this thermostat to all. Plus you may get a rebate (which they do the leg work to see if you qualify for).

Don't think about it BUY THIS THERMOSTAT!!! You won't regret it.

If you have a browser that protects against cookies ( DuckDuckGo. Firefox, etc.) you will have to switch back to google/chrome, bing/edge, etc. Otherwise, the app will not let you sign in. AFTER it's all installed, you can go back, but may(?) have to make exceptions since this tracks weather & works with your energy provider. The actual setup of the thermostat was a no-brainer. Very simple. I spent a little while getting familiar with "comfort zones". Once I did, programming the thermostat was a breeze. I really like the reports that the iPhone app produces. And I really like the "follow me" setting for some serious savings in when my A/C is running. I am using the app to control two separate thermostats; my home and also my Church. Switching between the two is easy as well. I have only thought up one thing I would like to see Ecobee do in the future: An alert for when the thermostat is manually changed and thereby over riding the schedule. I'd like to know when it was put into manual mode.

Our ecobee was installed seven months ago with our new Carrier HVAC and it has performed admirably. We installed remote sensors in all for bedrooms, the basement room, and two mid-level rooms. I’m fascinated watching the app, because it shows when the room is actually occupied and subsequently shows the HVAC system’s response to that new occupancy. It lags slightly, waiting to see if the detection was just someone popping in and popping back out, but after a couple minutes the system responds to a true occupancy. We have a wide variation between the basement and the rest of the living space, but overall the ecobee provides a reasonable balance throughout. No system is perfect so I give four stars for the commendable response it provides to our three living levels and highly recommend the ecobee.
